findings.claim: The CLI prints nothing at all. Usage, the unknown-transform error, 'no files matched', the changed-file list, the dry-run report and errors are all silent: printUsage runs an empty forEach, L186-195 are empty bodies and L198 swallows the error.
findings.fix: Restore stdout/stderr output, add a biome override turning noConsole off for src/codemod/**, print the changed/unchanged/error summary with paths and the dry-run list, and exit 2 with usage when args are missing.
findings.groupTitle: Codemod CLI prints nothing (empty printUsage, empty report bodies, swallowed error)

findings.claim: --concurrency=0 hangs forever: chunked() never advances i. --concurrency=abc (NaN) processes zero files silently.
findings.fix: Validate Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 1, otherwise error and exit 2.
findings.groupTitle: --concurrency=0 hangs and NaN processes zero files

findings.claim: .js/.mjs/.cjs files are parsed with the 'ts' parser, which rejects JSX. A .js file containing JSX throws, is counted as an error and is skipped silently.
findings.fix: Use ts for .ts/.mts/.cts, tsx for .tsx, and babel (or tsx) for .js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs.
findings.groupTitle: .js/.mjs/.cjs parsed with the ts parser, so JSX in .js fails

findings.claim: cmdk-root is mapped to 'data-command', but modern-cmdk emits data-command-root and its CSS and README target [data-command-root]. Migrated selectors and JSX therefore point at an attribute nothing renders.
findings.fix: Map cmdk-root to data-command-root and fix the tests.
findings.groupTitle: cmdk-to-modern attribute map is wrong (cmdk-root to data-command) and missing five equivalents

findings.claim: The attribute map omits cmdk-dialog, cmdk-overlay, cmdk-group-heading, cmdk-group-items and cmdk-list-sizer, all of which have data-command-* equivalents. [cmdk-group-heading] (ubiquitous in shadcn/ui) survives migration untouched.
findings.fix: Add the 5 mappings and report cmdk-label and cmdk-item-select, which have no equivalent.
findings.groupTitle: cmdk-to-modern attribute map is wrong (cmdk-root to data-command) and missing five equivalents

findings.claim: cmdk's state attributes data-selected="true" and data-disabled="true" are not migrated to modern-cmdk's data-active="" and data-disabled="", so the common [cmdk-item][data-selected="true"] and Tailwind data-[selected=true]: styling silently stops matching.
findings.fix: Inside rewritten selectors, rewrite [data-selected="true"] to [data-active] and [data-disabled="true"] to [data-disabled], plus the Tailwind variants.
findings.groupTitle: data-selected/data-disabled state values and Tailwind variants are not migrated

findings.claim: Only JS/TS ASTs are processed, so stylesheets (.css/.scss), the main home of [cmdk-*] selectors, are never migrated. The CLI feeds them to a JS parser, which throws, and the error is hidden.
findings.fix: Route style files through replaceInString as raw text (or a PostCSS selector pass) in the CLI.
findings.groupTitle: Non-JS files (CSS, JSON, MD) are globbed and fed to the JS parser; stylesheets never migrated

findings.claim: A ref parameter not named 'ref' becomes a shorthand destructure of a nonexistent prop ({ forwardedRef, ...props }), so the ref is always undefined in React 19.
findings.fix: j.objectProperty(j.identifier('ref'), j.identifier(refName)) with shorthand only when refName === 'ref'.
findings.groupTitle: A ref param not named 'ref' becomes a shorthand destructure of a nonexistent prop

findings.claim: forwardRef<T, Props> type arguments and the ref annotation are dropped, so untyped params become implicit any. The header's promised output 'Props & { ref?: React.Ref<HTMLDivElement> }' is never produced.
findings.fix: Read path.node.typeArguments/typeParameters and annotate the ObjectPattern with Props & { ref?: React.Ref<T> }.
findings.groupTitle: forwardRef<T, Props> type arguments and the ref annotation are dropped

findings.claim: Specifiers are rewritten blindly. cmdk's CommandRoot and defaultFilter do not exist in modern-cmdk/react, so rewritten imports break, and useCommandState's state shape differs.
findings.fix: Map CommandRoot to Command, report defaultFilter and useCommandState selector usage, and error on unknown specifiers.
findings.groupTitle: Import specifiers rewritten blindly (CommandRoot, defaultFilter, useCommandState, default import)

findings.claim: shouldFilter={expr} becomes filter={expr}, but modern-cmdk's filter accepts only a function, false or undefined, so a boolean that can be true fails type-checking.
findings.fix: Emit filter={expr ? undefined : false}, or report the site for manual migration.
findings.groupTitle: shouldFilter={expr} becomes filter={expr}, a type error when expr can be true

findings.claim: cmdk's filter prop signature (value, search, keywords) => number differs from modern-cmdk's (item, query) => number|false. An element carrying both shouldFilter={false} and filter={fn} ends up with duplicate filter attributes, and custom filters are not adapted.
findings.fix: Detect an existing filter attribute, warn, and adapt or flag the custom filter.
findings.groupTitle: Duplicate filter attributes, and cmdk custom filter signatures are not adapted

findings.claim: There are no tests for the CLI. The transform tests (tests/unit/codemod-*.test.ts, 365 lines) call the transforms directly, so the silent output, the concurrency hang and the .js parser failure went unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add integration tests that spawn dist/codemod/cli.mjs on a temp fixture dir and assert exit codes, stdout and rewritten files.
findings.groupTitle: No CLI integration tests (spawn the built cli on fixture dirs)

findings.claim: The forward-ref tests use toContain('ref'), which passes on the broken { forwardedRef } output. Renamed refs, type args, aliases and memo(forwardRef()) are untested.
findings.fix: Use exact input/output fixtures.
findings.groupTitle: Transform tests use toContain substrings and lack exact input/output fixtures

findings.claim: The codemod ships inside the runtime library: a 2.46 MB cli.mjs with jscodeshift, babel, recast and globby bundled in, which every consumer of a 6.3 kB core downloads.
findings.fix: Split into its own package (e.g. modern-cmdk-codemod) with jscodeshift and globby as real dependencies.
findings.groupTitle: 2.46 MB codemod bundle ships inside the runtime library

findings.claim: The documented directory form './src' relies on globby's expandDirectories default (true), which globs every file type (CSS, JSON, MD, images). Each one is parsed as JS, throws, and is silently counted as an error.

findings.claim: Promise.allSettled batching only overlaps I/O. jscodeshift parse/print is synchronous and CPU-bound, so the work runs on one core, and each batch waits on its slowest file.

findings.claim: The resolveDone/done promise is resolved synchronously and then awaited, a no-op indirection.

findings.claim: FrecencyEngine sync dispose disposes storage synchronously before its microtask-deferred save, so IdbFrecencyStorage drops the write and MemoryFrecencyStorage is cleared then repopulated; #dirty never reset.
findings.fix: Dispose storage only after save resolves (.finally), and give CommandMachine an [Symbol.asyncDispose] that awaits frecencyEngine[Symbol.asyncDispose]().
findings.groupTitle: Sync dispose drops the deferred save and the machine never flushes frecency
findings.note: Landed as e8c042e (1.6/frecency 6c8ba72): recordSelection schedules one trailing save after FLUSH_DELAY_MS (1000 ms); pagehide and visibilitychange-to-hidden save and cancel the timer; flush() clears the timer and the dirty flag before the save; load() merges stored records into the engine's own map (frequencies add, lastUsed takes the later); the sync dispose starts the quiet save and disposes the storage only once every save settled. Titles: 'CE-01: sync dispose disposes the storage only after the save settled'; 'CE-15: selections recorded before an async load resolves are merged, not dropped' (DG-62's guide claim is now true of the code); 'SEC-02: three selections at 0/400/800 ms give one save at 1800 ms with all three counted'; 'SEC-02: pagehide saves and cancels the pending timer'; DG-08's round trip is 'DG-63: a machine saves its selections to IndexedDB and a second machine ranks by them (TUB-24, CE-31, SEC-02, DG-08)' (c76f788). Verified Chromium only; the real-browser order of pagehide vs visibilitychange is unverified. The guide pages (:35, :41) are re-read by DOCS.

findings.claim: The machine never calls frecencyEngine.flush() and only sync-disposes it, so IdbFrecencyStorage-backed frecency never persists across sessions through the machine or React layer.
findings.fix: Debounced/idle flush after ITEM_SELECT plus async dispose that awaits the flush; add an integration test with fake-indexeddb.
findings.groupTitle: Sync dispose drops the deferred save and the machine never flushes frecency
findings.note: Landed as 640f4ce (af1ac92, re-adapted to the batching block of c339027 after the rebase): the machine handles its frecency load (a rejection is reported once through console.warn('[modern-cmdk] frecency load failed:', error), the row CE-60 format, because the machine has no error path: ruling), marks its results dirty once the engine merged the stored records and commits unless a batch is pending (whose own commit picks up dirty), skips the refilter when already disposed, and gains [Symbol.asyncDispose] (awaits the engine's flush, then the sync dispose) on the factory's return type CommandMachine & AsyncDisposable while the exported interface stays unchanged (LD-05, ruling). Titles: 'CE-14: hydration re-ranks the current results without another event'; 'CE-14: a load that settles after dispose does not search or emit' (red without the guard: search called twice); 'SEC-27: a rejecting load is reported once and the machine keeps working'; 'CE-02: await using flushes the pending save before the block ends'; 'CE-02: a synchronous dispose of a dirty machine still persists the selection'. Hostile verifier on the adapted commit: CONFIRMED (hydration with and without a pending batch, the microtask path, the guard, StrictMode does not bring CE-78 back, dispose order, LD-05 types). Follow-ups filed: CE-109 (redundant emit at an empty query), CE-110 (error channel).

findings.claim: Public API docs say scoreItemAsync yields via scheduler.yield() and batchScoreItems(query, items, batchSize?) yields between batches; code never yields and has no batchSize parameter.

findings.claim: load() replaces #data wholesale, dropping selections recorded before the async load resolves.
findings.fix: Merge loaded records with in-memory ones (sum frequency, max lastUsed).
findings.groupTitle: Frecency load is unguarded, unvalidated, overwrites in-memory records and never refilters
findings.note: Landed as e8c042e (1.6/frecency 6c8ba72): recordSelection schedules one trailing save after FLUSH_DELAY_MS (1000 ms); pagehide and visibilitychange-to-hidden save and cancel the timer; flush() clears the timer and the dirty flag before the save; load() merges stored records into the engine's own map (frequencies add, lastUsed takes the later); the sync dispose starts the quiet save and disposes the storage only once every save settled. Titles: 'CE-01: sync dispose disposes the storage only after the save settled'; 'CE-15: selections recorded before an async load resolves are merged, not dropped' (DG-62's guide claim is now true of the code); 'SEC-02: three selections at 0/400/800 ms give one save at 1800 ms with all three counted'; 'SEC-02: pagehide saves and cancels the pending timer'; DG-08's round trip is 'DG-63: a machine saves its selections to IndexedDB and a second machine ranks by them (TUB-24, CE-31, SEC-02, DG-08)' (c76f788). Verified Chromium only; the real-browser order of pagehide vs visibilitychange is unverified. The guide pages (:35, :41) are re-read by DOCS.

findings.claim: With filter={false}, every ITEMS_LOADED batch is registered and never removed, and each Command.Item adds a second copy under a useId id. Stale results from earlier queries stay counted and keyboard-reachable with no DOM, so Empty never shows.

findings.claim: The home-page feature "Sub-1ms search on 100K items with optional WASM" is false. The TS baseline at 100K is 85 ms, the 0.8 ms WASM figure dates from 0.9.0 and has not been measured since, and the WASM engine is unpublished and always falls back.

findings.claim: A module top-level `using machine = createCommandMachine(...)` disposes the machine when the module finishes evaluating. The subscriber, scheduler and keyboard listener are gone before the user types, so the example is dead after the first render.
findings.fix: Use const plus explicit machine[Symbol.dispose]() on teardown, or `using` inside a scope that lives as long as the UI.
findings.groupTitle: vanilla.md's top-level `using` disposes the machine at module end
findings.note: apps/docs/examples/vanilla.md keeps the machine in a const disposed on a non-persisted pagehide, renders options with createElement/textContent/replaceChildren and combobox/listbox/aria-activedescendant wiring like the React adapter (react/input.tsx:69-75, react/list.tsx:159, core/registry.ts getItem), and its Svelte $effect returns unsubscribe plus dispose; fix round a13bcf2.

findings.claim: 10,000 JSX Command.Items each dispatch REGISTER_ITEM, and each one runs a full refilter over the growing registry: O(n^2) at mount (about 50M item visits). All 10K components also re-render on every state change. This contradicts "smooth 60fps with 10,000 items".
findings.fix: Recommend the `items` prop with virtual rows; refilter once per scheduler tick in the machine.
findings.groupTitle: Each REGISTER_ITEM refilters the whole registry, so mount is O(n^2)
findings.note: apps/docs/examples/virtualized.md and recipes/emoji-picker.md drop the fps claim and say every Command.Item mounts and registers while virtualization skips only off-screen DOM (react/item.tsx:72, react/list.tsx:111-136); guide/virtualization.md follows in afd13a2 and 5a4f0aa. NAR-emoji-2's code half (one refilter per batch for registry events) is c339027.

findings.claim: `await createWorkerSearchEngine()` never resolves: worker init throws before posting `ready`. Even when it works, the sync search() returns the previous searchAsync() cache, so <Command.Dialog search={engine}> shows stale results. "Sub-millisecond" is false.
findings.fix: Remove the section until the engine initialises and the machine supports async engines.

findings.claim: og:description advertises "WASM search" as a feature, but the package is private 0.9.0, unpublished, and non-functional (always falls back).

findings.claim: IndexedDB frecency persistence never writes. The engine saves only on dispose, and its dispose defers the save to a microtask after disposing the storage, so IdbFrecencyStorage.save returns early. On a page reload dispose never runs.
findings.fix: Flush (debounced) on recordSelection and on pagehide/visibilitychange, await the save before disposing the storage, and add a fake-indexeddb round-trip test.
findings.groupTitle: IndexedDB frecency saves only on dispose, after the storage is already disposed
findings.note: Landed as e8c042e (1.6/frecency 6c8ba72): recordSelection schedules one trailing save after FLUSH_DELAY_MS (1000 ms); pagehide and visibilitychange-to-hidden save and cancel the timer; flush() clears the timer and the dirty flag before the save; load() merges stored records into the engine's own map (frequencies add, lastUsed takes the later); the sync dispose starts the quiet save and disposes the storage only once every save settled. Titles: 'CE-01: sync dispose disposes the storage only after the save settled'; 'CE-15: selections recorded before an async load resolves are merged, not dropped' (DG-62's guide claim is now true of the code); 'SEC-02: three selections at 0/400/800 ms give one save at 1800 ms with all three counted'; 'SEC-02: pagehide saves and cancels the pending timer'; DG-08's round trip is 'DG-63: a machine saves its selections to IndexedDB and a second machine ranks by them (TUB-24, CE-31, SEC-02, DG-08)' (c76f788). Verified Chromium only; the real-browser order of pagehide vs visibilitychange is unverified. The guide pages (:35, :41) are re-read by DOCS.

findings.claim: The documented module-level `new IdbFrecencyStorage()` is permanently disabled by the first unmount, because the machine disposes consumer-owned storage. After a StrictMode remount, load() is empty and save() is a no-op.

findings.claim: The core example is wrong: getState() right after send() is unprocessed (events are batched), and the empty query skips frecency, so 'settings first, boosted by frecency' is only registration order.

findings.claim: Selections recorded before the async frecency load() resolves are lost, because load() replaces the data wholesale.
findings.fix: Merge the loaded records into the in-memory ones.
findings.groupTitle: Selections recorded before the async frecency load() resolves are lost
findings.note: Landed as e8c042e (1.6/frecency 6c8ba72): recordSelection schedules one trailing save after FLUSH_DELAY_MS (1000 ms); pagehide and visibilitychange-to-hidden save and cancel the timer; flush() clears the timer and the dirty flag before the save; load() merges stored records into the engine's own map (frequencies add, lastUsed takes the later); the sync dispose starts the quiet save and disposes the storage only once every save settled. Titles: 'CE-01: sync dispose disposes the storage only after the save settled'; 'CE-15: selections recorded before an async load resolves are merged, not dropped' (DG-62's guide claim is now true of the code); 'SEC-02: three selections at 0/400/800 ms give one save at 1800 ms with all three counted'; 'SEC-02: pagehide saves and cancels the pending timer'; DG-08's round trip is 'DG-63: a machine saves its selections to IndexedDB and a second machine ranks by them (TUB-24, CE-31, SEC-02, DG-08)' (c76f788). Verified Chromium only; the real-browser order of pagehide vs visibilitychange is unverified. The guide pages (:35, :41) are re-read by DOCS.

findings.note: Landed as c76f788 (81f9a39), the machine-level frecency suite tests/unit/frecency-machine.test.ts (10 tests) on fake-indexeddb. DG-63 'DG-63: a machine saves its selections to IndexedDB and a second machine ranks by them (TUB-24, CE-31, SEC-02, DG-08)'; TUB-24 storage half 'TUB-24: data saved by one instance is loaded by a new instance on the same database after dispose' (b292896) and engine half 'TUB-24: a selection left in an await using block is stored and a new IdbFrecencyStorage loads it' (e8c042e); CE-31's persistence half is the DG-63 test and its disabled-exclusion half is the D78 matrix (74ee107); TUB-07 'TUB-07: after a selection a query matching several items ranks the selected item first' replaces the vacuous assertion at machine-integration.test.ts:45. Also here: 'P07: the machine disposes the storage the caller passed in, after its last save' pins the 1.x ownership contract, and 'LD-05: CommandMachine stays implementable without Symbol.asyncDispose and the machine still has one'.
