findings.groupTitle: The async guide uses third-party react-error-boundary instead of the exported CommandErrorBoundary

findings.claim: architecture/overview.md and guide/architecture.md duplicate each other (layers, ES table, worker diagram) and contradict each other (editions, message-name case).
findings.fix: Merge into one architecture section, and keep the module table as a single internals page.
findings.groupTitle: architecture/overview.md and guide/architecture.md duplicate and contradict each other

findings.claim: 'TypeScript >= 7.0.2' as a consumer requirement is not derived from anything; the emitted .d.mts files need IteratorObject (TS 5.6+) and lib esnext.disposable.
findings.fix: State the real minimum; keep 'built with 7.0.2' as a separate fact.
findings.groupTitle: Installation page states the repo toolchain (ES2026 target, TS >= 7.0.2) as consumer requirements

findings.claim: Command.Dialog lays out at 2px wide. The dialog tokens are declared only on [data-command-root], but they are used on [data-command-dialog-content], [data-command-dialog] and [data-command-overlay], which are its ancestors or siblings. The var() is invalid there, so inline-size becomes auto, which is 0 under container-type:inline-size.
findings.fix: Declare the tokens on :where([data-command-root],[data-command-dialog],[data-command-overlay]) or :root inside a layer, give every var() a fallback, and add an e2e test that asserts a visible bounding box.
findings.groupTitle: Dialog tokens declared only on [data-command-root], so Command.Dialog lays out 2px wide

findings.claim: Focus is not returned to the opener when the dialog closes (APG Dialog, WCAG 2.4.3). There is no Dialog.Trigger, and Radix modal onCloseAutoFocus calls preventDefault and then focuses triggerRef, which is null.
findings.fix: Record document.activeElement when the dialog opens. In onCloseAutoFocus, preventDefault and restore that element; offer a returnFocus prop. Add an e2e test.
findings.groupTitle: Dialog close does not return focus to the opener

findings.claim: During a search, ArrowDown follows score order (filteredIds), but items render in JSX order. The active highlight jumps across groups, and screen-reader order does not match browse mode.
findings.fix: Render in filteredIds order (reorder the DOM per group, as cmdk does) or navigate in DOM order. Do not use CSS order. Add an e2e test that compares the two orders.
findings.groupTitle: Arrow navigation follows score order while the DOM renders in JSX order

findings.claim: Disabled options are hidden when the query is empty but appear when searching. While searching they become the initial active descendant and are reachable with the arrow keys; Enter then does nothing.
findings.fix: Always render disabled options with aria-disabled, and skip them in navigate(), in first-active selection and in ITEM_ACTIVATE.
findings.groupTitle: Disabled options appear while searching and can become the active descendant
findings.note: R2/D78 disabled contract landed as 74ee107 (52057c7: disabled items rendered with aria-disabled and data-disabled, skipped by NAVIGATE, ITEM_ACTIVATE and ITEM_SELECT, excluded from the first active item; `disabledItems: 'hide'` restores the hidden rendering) and 8ddd517 (9760e16: 'hide' also drops ids a self-indexing engine returns). Proof set: tests/unit/disabled-matrix.test.ts, the 'disabled items' describe of command.test.tsx and the D78 e2e test. Visible side effects at rest for the changeset: a group holding only disabled items shows; Command.Empty no longer appears when only disabled items exist; filteredCount, the results announcement and the virtualization threshold count disabled items.

findings.claim: There is no IME composition guard. Pressing Enter to confirm a CJK candidate runs the active command, and the arrow keys are taken from the candidate window.
findings.fix: Add `if (event.isComposing || event.keyCode === 229) return;` at the top of the handler, plus a unit test.
findings.groupTitle: No IME composition guard in the keyboard handler

findings.claim: Item shortcuts are bound on the whole document. A match calls preventDefault and stopPropagation regardless of the target element, IME state, open state or scope. A single-key shortcut would swallow typing everywhere (WCAG 2.1.4), and the React API offers no way to turn this off.
findings.fix: Add a shortcuts option ('global' | 'when-open' | false). Ignore editable targets and isComposing, drop stopPropagation, and reject single-character shortcuts unless opted in.
findings.groupTitle: Item shortcuts are bound on the whole document with no scope or opt-out

findings.claim: The axe gate is red on main, but continue-on-error on the e2e job hides it, so CI reports green.
findings.fix: Fix the contrast (A11Y-08), then remove continue-on-error so a11y failures block merges.

findings.claim: The default library CSS fades text with opacity (heading 0.6, shortcut 0.5, empty 0.6, placeholder 0.5). Combined with the theme colours this fails WCAG 1.4.3.
findings.fix: Remove opacity from text, add a --command-muted-color token whose default passes 4.5:1, and keep opacity only for disabled items.
findings.groupTitle: Default CSS fades text with opacity and fails WCAG 1.4.3

findings.claim: JSX attribute strings do not process \u escapes, so the RTL demo's label, placeholder and group headings are literal backslash-u text.
findings.fix: Use expression containers ({'...'}) or literal Arabic text, and add an e2e test that checks the accessible name under dir=rtl.
findings.groupTitle: RTL demo shows literal \u escape text in JSX attribute strings

findings.claim: Empty reads the portal ref during render, so on first render it lands inline inside role=listbox and can stay there. Loading has no portal at all. Both put role=status inside the listbox, which is invalid.
findings.fix: Have List own a persistent status region that Empty and Loading write into through context, or store the container element in state so the portal target exists on first commit.
findings.groupTitle: Status announcements are split across misplaced, noisy live regions (Empty, Loading, result count, page changes)

findings.claim: Loading combines role=status (polite) with aria-live=assertive and puts aria-busy=true on the live region itself, which suppresses announcements. It is also mounted together with its content, which screen readers announce unreliably. The AllStates loading demo never renders.
findings.fix: Use one persistent polite region whose text changes when loading starts, keep aria-busy on the listbox only, and pass loading in the demo.
findings.groupTitle: Status announcements are split across misplaced, noisy live regions (Empty, Loading, result count, page changes)

findings.claim: The result-count live region announces on every keystroke with no debounce, says '0 results available.' while loading, repeats what Empty announces, and hard-codes the English plural.
findings.fix: Debounce by about 500 ms, stay silent while loading or pending, keep a single region, and default to Intl.PluralRules.
findings.groupTitle: Status announcements are split across misplaced, noisy live regions (Empty, Loading, result count, page changes)

findings.claim: Virtualized options have no aria-setsize or aria-posinset, so screen readers report positions like '1 of 23'. After End, aria-activedescendant points to an id that is not rendered yet.
findings.fix: Set aria-setsize to filteredCount and aria-posinset to index + 1, and always render (pin) the active item.
findings.groupTitle: Virtualized options lack aria-setsize/aria-posinset, and the active item is not pinned

findings.claim: The keyboard map departs from the APG editable combobox. Home and End are stolen from the caret, modifiers are ignored, PageUp/PageDown and Alt+Arrow are missing, and Enter and Escape call preventDefault unconditionally.
findings.fix: Let Home/End move the caret (use Ctrl+Home/End for options), add PageUp/PageDown, return early on modifiers or defaultPrevented, and only call preventDefault on Enter when an item is active.
findings.groupTitle: Keyboard map departs from the APG editable combobox (Home/End, PageUp/PageDown, modifiers, preventDefault)

findings.claim: Clicking an option in the inline palette moves focus to body. The scoped key listener then ignores keys, so the keyboard stops working.
findings.fix: Call preventDefault in onPointerDown so focus stays in the input, or refocus the input after select.
findings.groupTitle: Clicking an inline option moves focus to body and keyboard control is lost

findings.claim: The palette handles Enter, Arrow, Escape and Backspace from any descendant (root.contains), and the dialog listens on the whole document. Nested buttons and form fields lose these keys; Enter cannot activate a button inside the palette.
findings.fix: Handle keys only when the event target is the combobox input (or an element that opts in).
findings.groupTitle: Palette and dialog handle keys from any descendant or the document, ignoring defaultPrevented and nested layers

findings.claim: Escape is not layered. Radix and the document listener both send CLOSE (onOpenChange(false) fires twice), and the palette closes even when a nested layer has already handled Escape.
findings.fix: Use only Radix onEscapeKeyDown in the dialog, skip events with defaultPrevented, and have inline Escape clear the search.
findings.groupTitle: Palette and dialog handle keys from any descendant or the document, ignoring defaultPrevented and nested layers

findings.claim: aria-keyshortcuts receives raw strings such as 'Mod+N' and 'Ctrl+C', which are not valid ARIA key names. It is also set even when the shortcut is not registered (items without onSelect).
findings.fix: Emit the platform-resolved names (Control+N or Meta+N), and only when the binding is live.
findings.groupTitle: aria-keyshortcuts gets raw 'Mod+N' strings and is set when the binding is not live

findings.claim: formatShortcut labels meta as 'Ctrl' on non-Mac platforms, but the matcher requires metaKey. A 'Cmd+K' item shows Ctrl+K on Windows, yet only Win+K fires it.
findings.fix: Label an explicit meta as Win or Meta; reserve Ctrl for Mod and ctrl.
findings.groupTitle: formatShortcut labels an explicit meta as 'Ctrl' on non-Mac platforms

findings.claim: Matching uses event.key only. Option combinations on macOS, Shift+digit, and non-US layouts (the backquote in 'Mod+`') never match.
findings.fix: Fall back to event.code (KeyK, Backquote, DigitN) when event.key does not match.
findings.groupTitle: Shortcut matcher uses event.key only and misses Option, Shift+digit and non-US layouts

findings.claim: scrollIntoView passes behavior:'smooth' explicitly, which overrides the reduced-motion CSS scroll-behavior. The stylesheet header claim that all animations respect reduced motion is therefore false.
findings.fix: Omit behavior so CSS controls it, or use 'instant' when prefers-reduced-motion matches.
findings.groupTitle: scrollIntoView forces behavior:'smooth' and overrides reduced motion

findings.claim: The reduced-motion '*' override (which also forces iteration-count 1) and the global .sr-only class leak into the host application.
findings.fix: Scope the rules under [data-command-root], [data-command-dialog] and the overlay, and rename the class to [data-command-sr-only].
findings.groupTitle: Reduced-motion '*' override and global .sr-only class leak into the host app

findings.claim: The tokens are unlayered, so consumers' layered overrides cannot change them, and the command.* layers, including the a11y layer, lose to any unlayered consumer CSS. In the playground, Vite hoists the playground's @layer statement above the inlined import, so command.* outranks the playground theme.
findings.fix: Put everything, tokens included, in a single @layer modern-cmdk.*, use !important for critical forced-colors and contrast rules, and document the layer order.
findings.groupTitle: Tokens are unlayered and command.* layers lose to consumer CSS

findings.claim: The active-option indicator has 1.41:1 contrast (dark) and 1.16:1 (light), below the 3:1 non-text minimum. The library ships no default [data-active] indicator, and its item :focus-visible rules are dead because options never take focus.
findings.fix: Ship a default [data-active] outline or inline-start bar at 3:1 or better, remove the dead :focus-visible rules, and darken the playground's bg-active.
findings.groupTitle: Active-option indicator is under 3:1, no default [data-active] indicator ships, and item :focus-visible rules are dead

findings.claim: --border-focus is not overridden in the light theme, so the focus ring is 2.87:1 against bg-secondary.
findings.fix: Add a light override of about oklch(0.5 0.22 250).
findings.groupTitle: Playground light theme is missing token overrides (focus ring, badge, error text) and its color-scheme does not follow the active theme

findings.claim: In the light theme the beta badge is 1.58:1 and the error text is 2.57:1. color-scheme 'light dark' on dark tokens lets native controls follow the OS theme instead of the page.
findings.fix: Add light-theme token values, set color-scheme to match the active theme, and add prefers-color-scheme defaults.
findings.groupTitle: Playground light theme is missing token overrides (focus ring, badge, error text) and its color-scheme does not follow the active theme

findings.claim: The dialog, heading, search landmark, combobox and listbox all have the same name. The forced aria-label on the input overrides a visible label (WCAG 2.5.3).
findings.fix: Name the listbox 'Results', drop the aria-label on Dialog.Content and role=search inside the dialog, and honour aria-labelledby on the input.
findings.groupTitle: Dialog, heading, search landmark, combobox and listbox share one name, and a forced aria-label overrides the visible label

findings.claim: Pushing or popping a page (including via Backspace) swaps the content silently: no announcement and no change of name.
findings.fix: Add a label prop to Command.Page and announce the page and its result count through the status region.
findings.groupTitle: Status announcements are split across misplaced, noisy live regions (Empty, Loading, result count, page changes)

findings.claim: Several assertions can never fail: /(true|)/ regexes, toBeDefined on null, and disabled tests that run against no disabled options. Coverage is only '/' and '/dialog' in the dark theme, without the wcag22aa or best-practice tags.
findings.fix: Use exact assertions. Add tests for focus restore, IME, Home caret, navigation order, live-region timing, RTL names, light theme, setsize, and /all-states. Sweep every route in both themes.
findings.groupTitle: accessibility.spec has assertions that can never fail and covers only two routes in one theme

findings.claim: The core and React entries are built by two separate tsdown configs, and the React sources import '../core/index.js'. So dist/react inlines a second copy of the core, and its d.mts redeclares the ItemId brand. Core ItemId, CommandItem, SearchEngine and CommandMachine values are therefore not assignable to modern-cmdk/react types.
findings.fix: Import 'modern-cmdk' (self-reference, kept external) in the React sources, or use one tsdown config with both entries so the core goes into a shared chunk. Add a type test that imports from both entry points. Ship as a 1.2.x patch.
findings.groupTitle: dist/react inlines a second copy of the core, so core ItemId, CommandItem and machine types are not assignable to the react types

findings.claim: `declare const __DEV__` is never defined by the modern-cmdk build, so useCommandDevtools throws ReferenceError at runtime in every consumer app. The comment 'tree-shaken in production' is false.
findings.fix: Use an inline `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'`, or add a tsdown define with a typeof guard. Add a test that runs against dist.
findings.groupTitle: Dev-only gates read an undefined __DEV__ or globalThis.process, so devtools throw and the leak flag misfires

findings.claim: The input is controlled by state.search, but updateSearch only queues SEARCH_CHANGE to rAF. React restores the old value after the change event, and the new value lands a frame later. Expect caret jumps on mid-string edits and broken IME composition (PLAUSIBLE).
findings.fix: Apply input-driven SEARCH_CHANGE synchronously, or keep local input state and defer only the refilter. Add an e2e that types in the middle of the text.
findings.groupTitle: The controlled input updates a frame late through rAF, so mid-string edits jump the caret and IME composition breaks

findings.claim: The single `pending` slot is overwritten by each postAndWait. A fire-and-forget index() followed by searchAsync() leaves one promise unresolved forever and resolves the search with the 'indexed' reply, so the search returns [].
findings.fix: Use request ids with a Map<id, resolvers>, or serialize requests on a promise chain.
findings.groupTitle: worker-engine keeps one pending slot that each postAndWait overwrites, so index() then searchAsync() hangs one promise and returns []

findings.claim: The SearchEngine.index() contract is undefined. The default engine upserts and the machine calls index([item]) per REGISTER_ITEM, but the WASM crate replaces its whole item list. With the React adapter, a WASM engine therefore only indexes the last mounted item, so 'drop-in replacement' is false.
findings.fix: In 1.x, document index() as an upsert and make WASM append/upsert. In 2.0, split the contract into upsert/remove/rebuild.
findings.groupTitle: The SearchEngine contract leaves index() semantics undefined and has no async search, so worker-engine search() returns stale cache

findings.claim: remove() clears the entire WASM index and never re-indexes, so any unmount, StrictMode remount or page change empties search. The engine also ignores keywords and disabled.
findings.fix: Keep the items on the JS side and rebuild (as worker-engine does), or add remove_ids to the crate. Index keywords too.
findings.groupTitle: WasmSearchEngine remove() clears the whole index and never re-indexes; it also ignores keywords and disabled

findings.claim: The published `modern-cmdk` codemod bin prints nothing. Usage is an empty loop, unknown transforms, no matched files and errors exit silently, and per-file results are computed and then discarded, so --dry-run reports nothing.
findings.fix: Restore stdout/stderr output (util.styleText), use util.parseArgs, print a summary and exit non-zero on errors. Add a CLI snapshot test.
findings.groupTitle: The published modern-cmdk codemod bin prints nothing: no usage, errors or dry-run output

findings.claim: ARCHITECTURE claims RegExp.escape in the parser, Promise.withResolvers in scheduler flush, a WeakRef emitter with Iterator-Helper has/listenerCount, and objectGroupBy in the registry. None of these exist in the code.
findings.fix: Rewrite the Core Engine and Keyboard sections and the file map from the code.
findings.groupTitle: ARCHITECTURE.md describes ES features and helpers the code never uses (RegExp.escape, withResolvers, WeakRef emitter, objectGroupBy, Promise.try, sumPrecise)

findings.claim: It says the core has 'No DOM APIs ... no side effects beyond subscriber notification' and that dependencies flow strictly downward. In fact every machine attaches a document keydown listener and uses rAF and navigator, and the React entry bundles a private copy of the core.
findings.fix: Document the real boundary once lazy listeners and the shared chunk land.
findings.groupTitle: The architecture docs misstate the core boundary, the WASM parity and figures, the component table, and overview behaviours

findings.claim: cmdk-root maps to data-command, but the adapter renders data-command-root. data-selected->data-active, cmdk-group-heading, cmdk-group-items, cmdk-dialog and cmdk-overlay are missing, so migrated CSS silently stops matching. The comment 'Set.union' is false.
findings.fix: Correct and extend the map, and add per-attribute fixture tests.
findings.groupTitle: The data-attrs transform maps cmdk-root to the wrong attribute and is missing selected/group-heading/group-items/dialog/overlay

findings.claim: The migration keeps cmdk's filter(value, search, keywords) signature, but modern-cmdk calls filter(item, query), so a migrated filter throws. cmdk's onSelect(value) argument is also not provided.
findings.fix: Add a filter-signature transform (wrap as (item, q) => fn(item.value, q, item.keywords)): the should-filter transform of 6d2c54d. The onSelect(value) half shipped in e4fc79b and was reverted inside the release under LD-05 (D66, W9-08): 1.x keeps `() => void`; the value argument is ARCH-62 (2.0.0).
findings.groupTitle: The migration keeps cmdk's filter(value, search, keywords) signature, so a migrated filter throws under filter(item, query)

findings.claim: ITEMS_LOADED registers the resolved items and never unregisters them. The documented pattern then renders a Command.Item per item, which registers each again under a useId id, doubling filteredCount and creating phantom navigation targets that have no DOM.
findings.fix: Either let the rendered Items register themselves (no ITEMS_LOADED) or render the items here; add an unregister cleanup in either case.
findings.groupTitle: AsyncItems registers loaded items, which then register again as rendered Items and are never unregistered

findings.claim: Disabled items are excluded for an empty query but included for a non-empty one, so a disabled React Item is invisible until the user types. The CommandItem doc says disabled items are 'excluded from filtering'.
findings.fix: Pick one rule (cmdk parity: always list them, skip them in navigate/activate/select) and apply it in both branches.
findings.groupTitle: Disabled items are hidden for an empty query but listed for a searched one
findings.note: R2/D78 disabled contract landed as 74ee107 (52057c7: disabled items rendered with aria-disabled and data-disabled, skipped by NAVIGATE, ITEM_ACTIVATE and ITEM_SELECT, excluded from the first active item; `disabledItems: 'hide'` restores the hidden rendering) and 8ddd517 (9760e16: 'hide' also drops ids a self-indexing engine returns). Proof set: tests/unit/disabled-matrix.test.ts, the 'disabled items' describe of command.test.tsx and the D78 e2e test. Visible side effects at rest for the changeset: a group holding only disabled items shows; Command.Empty no longer appears when only disabled items exist; filteredCount, the results announcement and the virtualization threshold count disabled items.

findings.claim: A custom filter returning 0 keeps the item. Only false excludes it, although the docs say score 0 is excluded and cmdk excludes 0.
findings.fix: Use `score === false || score <= 0` and ship it as a documented 1.x bugfix.
findings.groupTitle: A custom filter returning 0 keeps the item, although the docs and cmdk exclude score 0
findings.note: Landed as 5393621 (023aee7: a custom filter score of 0 or less excludes the item, as false does; the default scorer and pluggable engines are left as returned, by ruling) and 200e6d5 (the doc comment). Changeset wording from the cluster: 'results from a pluggable search engine, including createSearchEngine({ scorer }), are used as returned'.

findings.claim: Global shortcuts call the raw item.onSelect instead of ITEM_SELECT. They fire on disabled items, record no frecency, skip options.onSelect and the select event, and stopPropagation does not stop the other document listeners.
findings.fix: Register () => send({type:'ITEM_SELECT', id}), and use stopImmediatePropagation where suppression is intended.
findings.groupTitle: Global shortcuts call raw item.onSelect: they fire on disabled items and skip frecency, options.onSelect and the select event
findings.note: Landed with 3ffbd23 and e815001 by the CE-09 tests. Not adopted by ruling: stopImmediatePropagation on a handled shortcut (no contract to restore; one line if ever wanted).

findings.claim: ITEMS_LOADED skips shortcut registration, and nothing ever sets loading:true, so CommandState.loading and the list's aria-busy are always false.
findings.fix: Add a LOADING event (additive), have AsyncItems send it, and register shortcuts in ITEMS_LOADED.
findings.groupTitle: Nothing ever sets loading:true (so aria-busy is always false), and ITEMS_LOADED skips shortcut registration
findings.remaining: ITEMS_LOADED still skips shortcut registration (packages/modern-cmdk/src/core/machine.ts:308-312); the loading half was fixed by e4fc79b (1.5.0); release stays 1.6.0 [after e297590]
findings.note: Landed as 3ffbd23 (43c9b17): the shortcut of an item delivered by ITEMS_LOADED fires its onSelect; one bind helper.

findings.claim: Machine options are read once at mount. Later changes to items, groups, filter, loop or frecency are ignored, and the onSelect, onActiveChange and onSearchChange callbacks keep their first-render closures. The props look reactive but are init-only.
findings.fix: In 1.x, add latest-ref callbacks, diff items/groups into register/unregister, and add an optional `machine` prop.
findings.groupTitle: Machine options and callbacks are read once at mount, so the props look reactive but are init-only

findings.claim: The controlled sync sends CLOSE on mount, and the machine has no same-state guard, so onOpenChange(false) fires on mount and each close is reported twice.
findings.fix: Make OPEN/CLOSE/TOGGLE no-ops when the state is unchanged, and skip the sync effect when controlledOpen === state.open.
findings.groupTitle: The controlled Dialog sends CLOSE on mount and OPEN/CLOSE are not idempotent, so onOpenChange(false) fires on mount and twice per close

findings.claim: The machine is created in render and disposed in effect cleanup. Under StrictMode or Activity the disposed machine stays in use, its global shortcut listener is removed permanently, and IDB frecency becomes a no-op (PLAUSIBLE). The comment 'Strict Mode remount creates a fresh machine' is false.
findings.fix: Create the machine in the effect or make dispose reversible (lazy listener). Add a StrictMode test.
findings.groupTitle: The machine is created in render and disposed in effect cleanup, so StrictMode and Activity keep a disposed machine

findings.claim: Changing value, disabled, shortcut or keywords triggers UNREGISTER plus REGISTER, and the registry appends re-registered ids at the end, so toggling disabled moves the item to the bottom of the list.
findings.fix: Add an UPDATE_ITEM upsert event that keeps the position, and use unregister only on unmount.
findings.groupTitle: Changing value, disabled, shortcut or keywords re-registers the item and moves it to the end of the list
findings.note: Landed as aca8737 (4b10de3: UPDATE_ITEM upserts in place; React use-register split so a prop change updates instead of re-registering) and 200e6d5 (React UPDATE_ITEM tests that can fail). The useRegisterItem docs that say an item re-registers when its props change are DOCS's.

findings.claim: The sync search() the machine calls returns the cache from the last searchAsync(), whatever query that used. The machine never calls searchAsync, and the 'async adapter' named in the comment does not exist, so plugged in, the engine returns stale or empty results.
findings.fix: Add an optional SearchEngine.searchAsync and have the machine await it with a query token for cancellation (additive in 1.x).
findings.groupTitle: The SearchEngine contract leaves index() semantics undefined and has no async search, so worker-engine search() returns stale cache

findings.claim: The Worker URL points at './worker.ts', but tsdown only builds src/index.ts, so the built package would reference a worker that is never emitted (PLAUSIBLE). The package typecheck fails without pkg/, so this layer has no green gate.
findings.fix: Add worker.ts as a tsdown entry and reference './worker.js'. Add a stub pkg .d.ts so typecheck runs without wasm-pack.
findings.groupTitle: The worker URL points at an unbuilt worker.ts, and the wasm package typecheck has no green gate without pkg/

findings.claim: The SharedArrayBuffer is sized for the constructor maxResults, but searchAsync accepts a larger limit, which yields undefined scores. The crate returns UTF-8 byte offsets, which misalign highlights for non-ASCII text, and 1-2 character queries rarely match.
findings.fix: Clamp or reallocate the buffer, emit UTF-16 offsets, and add a prefix/substring fallback for short queries.
findings.groupTitle: The worker SharedArrayBuffer is sized for the constructor maxResults, offsets are UTF-8 bytes, and 1-2 character queries rarely match

findings.claim: Each REGISTER_ITEM and UNREGISTER_ITEM runs a full refilter and emit, so mounting N Items costs O(N^2) work and N stateChange emits within one scheduler batch.
findings.fix: Mark the state dirty and refilter once per executeBatch (internal, compatible).
findings.groupTitle: Each REGISTER_ITEM and UNREGISTER_ITEM runs a full refilter and emit, so mounting N items costs O(N^2)
findings.note: Landed as c339027 (1.6/machine ccbdda4: one refilter and one emit per scheduler batch, a counter marks the batch end so the scheduler contract is kept) and a87d6d7 (884b6c0: no stale NAVIGATE/ITEM_ACTIVATE after a registry event in the same batch, a throwing filter still emits). Emit order change recorded for DOCS and the changeset: onOpenChange, onSearchChange and openChange run before the batch's single stateChange. BENCH's verifier measured a 10K mount median of 17.20 ms on the branch (6415 ms at 6171765).

findings.claim: Object.assign on the compound, module-level createContext and displayName writes, a single-file bundle and sideEffects listing dist/react/index.mjs together prevent component tree-shaking. Importing only CommandSeparator ships radix Dialog and the whole machine. The ssr.md claim 'only the components you import are included' is false.
findings.fix: tsdown unbundle, /* @__PURE__ */ annotations, sideEffects ['**/*.css'], and a react/dialog subpath (Command.Dialog deprecated in 1.x, removed in 2.0).
findings.groupTitle: sideEffects, the Object.assign compound and the single-file bundle block component tree-shaking, so importing Separator ships radix Dialog
findings.remaining: Excluded from 1.4.0 under D33 (G-27): the compound Command stays an Object.assign through 1.x, so importing only CommandSeparator from modern-cmdk/react still ships CommandDialog, CommandRoot and the radix-ui import (4767 B gzip measured by size-limit at f42e064, with sideEffects as it was and as it is now). Closes in 2.0 when the barrel drops Command.Dialog and the compound is unbundled. Its docs claim (ssr.md:57) rides DG-29 (W5-04).

findings.claim: The core is not DOM-free or tree-shakeable around the machine. Every machine builds a KeyboardShortcutRegistry, which adds a document listener, and always pulls in FrecencyEngine. ARCHITECTURE:L653 says machine-only consumers do not pay for them, which is false.
findings.fix: Attach the listener lazily, add a keyboard:false option and frecency engine injection (1.x). Make global shortcuts opt-in in 2.0.
findings.groupTitle: Every machine builds a KeyboardShortcutRegistry with a document listener and pulls in FrecencyEngine, so machine-only consumers pay for both

findings.claim: startTransition around machine.send has no effect: send defers to rAF outside the transition, and useSyncExternalStore updates are always blocking. The docs' 'keeps input responsive' claim is unfounded, and isPending is effectively always false.
findings.fix: Defer inside React (useDeferredValue over the filtered ids) or drop the claim. Revisit the useOptimistic overlay.
findings.groupTitle: startTransition around machine.send has no effect, so isPending is always false

findings.claim: The machine discards SearchResult.matches, so the exported Command.Highlight (which requires ranges) has no supported data source.
findings.fix: Add state.matches or a useItemMatches(id) hook, and expose ranges to Item children (additive in 1.x).
findings.groupTitle: The machine discards SearchResult.matches, so Command.Highlight has no supported data source

findings.claim: Options.search is the search engine while state.search is the query, the same name for two things. Command.Input cannot be controlled (value is omitted) even though ARCHITECTURE lists value as a prop, and there is no controlled activeId (cmdk parity).
findings.fix: In 1.x, add a searchEngine alias, Input value, and controlled search/activeId. In 2.0, drop the engine-meaning `search`.
findings.groupTitle: Options.search names the engine while state.search names the query; there is no controlled Input value or activeId

findings.claim: The core types use `?: T | undefined`, but every React prop and hook option uses bare `?: T`. Under exactOptionalPropertyTypes, consumers cannot forward `string | undefined` (TS2375), which is why item.tsx itself needs conditional spreads.
findings.fix: Add `| undefined` to every optional prop. This is a compatible widening for 1.x.
findings.groupTitle: React props use bare ?: T, so exactOptionalPropertyTypes consumers cannot forward string | undefined

findings.claim: virtualizeThreshold (documented 'default: 100') is never read, the List hardcodes 100 and 50, and CommandMachineOptions.label and DEFAULT_MACHINE_OPTIONS are unused by the machine.
findings.fix: Wire the threshold through the stable context (with the hysteresis at half of it) or deprecate it.
findings.groupTitle: virtualizeThreshold is never read: the List hardcodes 100/50, and label and DEFAULT_MACHINE_OPTIONS are unused

findings.claim: createTelemetryMiddleware is exported but not wired to the machine. There is no telemetry option, and callers must invoke every hook and pass startTime themselves.
findings.fix: Add telemetry?: CommandTelemetryHooks to the machine options (additive) and call it with performance.now(), or deprecate it.
findings.groupTitle: createTelemetryMiddleware is exported but never wired to the machine

findings.claim: It says WASM 'implements the same ScorerFn interface' (it implements SearchEngine, without parity) and gives 'Sub-1ms on 100K' with no benchmark. It also names a nonexistent CommandContext, an Input value prop, a Loading trigger that never fires, and no Highlight props.
findings.fix: Correct the component table and mark the WASM figures as unverified targets.
findings.groupTitle: The architecture docs misstate the core boundary, the WASM parity and figures, the component table, and overview behaviours

findings.claim: The sideEffects rationale and the ES feature list are wrong. Set methods are ES2025 and groupBy ES2024, and there are no Promise.try or sumPrecise helpers. The brand snippet is wrong. primitives.ts is called 'shared' and fuzzy-scorer an 'Async scorer'.
findings.fix: Rewrite the Design Decisions section and the file map from the code.
findings.groupTitle: ARCHITECTURE.md describes ES features and helpers the code never uses (RegExp.escape, withResolvers, WeakRef emitter, objectGroupBy, Promise.try, sumPrecise)

findings.claim: The overview says events are processed synchronously, the parser uses RegExp.escape, the core has zero DOM dependencies, score-0 items are excluded, Separator is role=separator, Empty sits inside List, scheduler flush uses withResolvers, and NoInfer is used. All are false.
findings.fix: Correct each line, and re-verify after the 1.x fixes.
findings.groupTitle: The architecture docs misstate the core boundary, the WASM parity and figures, the component table, and overview behaviours

findings.claim: Every link to https://command.crimson.dev is dead: README (~30 links), package READMEs, docs config og:url/sitemap, issue template, the repo homepage and SECURITY scope.
findings.fix: Either restore DNS and add apps/docs/public/CNAME, or repoint every link (READMEs, config.ts, ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml, gh repo homepage, SECURITY.md) to the Pages URL.
findings.groupTitle: Docs origin undecided: dead command.crimson.dev links and no VitePress base for /modern-cmdk/

findings.claim: The live docs are served from /modern-cmdk/, but the config sets no `base`, so the built HTML loads /assets/* from the domain root and the site renders without CSS or JS.
findings.fix: Add base: '/modern-cmdk/' (or a working CNAME), and align the sitemap hostname and og:url with it.
findings.groupTitle: Docs origin undecided: dead command.crimson.dev links and no VitePress base for /modern-cmdk/

findings.claim: The Quick Start (root and npm README) uses <Command.Highlight>Copy to Clipboard</Command.Highlight>. The component requires text and ranges and takes no children, so the headline sample fails tsc and throws at runtime.
findings.fix: Use plain item children, or <Command.Highlight text=... ranges=... />. Also show <Command.Shortcut shortcut="Mod+C" /> instead of children, so the platform formatting applies.
findings.groupTitle: Quick Start passes children to Command.Highlight and Command.Shortcut, which take none

findings.claim: The Quick Start renders an uncontrolled <Command.Dialog> with no trigger. Nothing in the library opens it, so the sample shows a palette that can never open. The recipes (spotlight, nested, file-picker) repeat this.
findings.fix: Show controlled open/onOpenChange plus a Mod+K listener (as api/command-react.md:L302-325 does) and import modern-cmdk/styles.css.
findings.groupTitle: Docs present an uncontrolled Command.Dialog that nothing can open

findings.claim: useCommandDevtools(), advertised in the READMEs, ships `if (!__DEV__) return;` with __DEV__ only declared and never defined. Consumers whose bundler does not define __DEV__ get a ReferenceError when the effect runs.
findings.fix: Use the globalThis.process?.env.NODE_ENV guard (or import.meta.env?.DEV) and add a unit test that renders the hook.
findings.groupTitle: useCommandDevtools references an undefined __DEV__ global

findings.at: packages/create-modern-cmdk/src/index.ts:252-312 (react-full falls to basic) and :240-249 (no styles.css import)
findings.claim: The scaffolder is broken against its README. react-dialog prints 'Press Ctrl+K to open' over a dialog with no key handler. react-full produces the same JSX as react-basic. No template imports styles.css.
findings.fix: Write real templates (hotkey, frecency, pages) or drop react-full, import the stylesheet, then republish create-modern-cmdk as a patch.
findings.groupTitle: create-modern-cmdk templates: dialog without hotkey, react-full equal to react-basic, no styles.css import

findings.claim: The scaffold generates caret ranges pinned to old majors and minors, and its README claims 'TypeScript 6 strict mode' and 'All dependencies are pinned'.
findings.fix: Generate exact pins resolved at release time and update the README text.
findings.groupTitle: Scaffold emits caret ranges on old majors; README claims TS 6 and pinned deps

findings.claim: 'RegExp.escape parsing' and 'Promise.withResolvers' are claimed for the library in about 40 places (README, ARCHITECTURE x8, CHANGELOG x5, CONTRIBUTING x4, docs). The shipped package uses neither.
findings.fix: Remove both from the feature lists and list the ES2025+ features actually used (Iterator helpers, using, toSorted).
findings.groupTitle: Phantom RegExp.escape and Promise.withResolvers claims (~40 places)

findings.claim: Says the event emitter is 'GC-safe ... using WeakRef ... automatically pruned on the next emit()'. The emitter uses strong references. The same false claim appears in api/command.md:L407, CHANGELOG.md:L119 and benchmarks.md:L93.
findings.fix: Describe the strong-ref Set with Disposable on().
findings.groupTitle: Event emitter documented as WeakRef/GC-safe; it holds strong refs

findings.claim: Says the scheduler 'Uses Promise.withResolvers for the flush() method'. flush() is synchronous void. The real features (scheduler.yield, isInputPending re-queue, error isolation) are undocumented.
findings.fix: Rewrite the Scheduler section from scheduler.ts.
findings.groupTitle: Scheduler and event batching misdocumented (sync processing, withResolvers flush, CONTRIBUTING sample fails)
findings.note: ARCHITECTURE.md's Scheduler section describes rAF/queueMicrotask batching, flush() applying the updates pending at the call, error isolation and dispose, with no Promise.withResolvers and no isInputPending gate (core/utils/scheduler.ts:1-86).

findings.claim: The sample unit test expects filteredCount 1 right after send(). send() is scheduled and '// Flush the scheduler' calls nothing, so the sample test fails.
findings.fix: Await a microtask, or add a documented flush helper, before reading state.
findings.groupTitle: Scheduler and event batching misdocumented (sync processing, withResolvers flush, CONTRIBUTING sample fails)
findings.note: CONTRIBUTING.md's sample unit test is async, asserts the initial filteredCount and then awaits vi.waitFor on the filtered count, so it fails when filtering breaks (verified by running it; vitest 5.1.0 waitFor, machine.ts send).

findings.claim: Says 'The machine processes the event synchronously'. Events are batched through rAF or a microtask, which contradicts ARCHITECTURE.md:L193-205 and CONTRIBUTING.md:L647.
findings.fix: Document the batching and how core-only users await it.
findings.groupTitle: Scheduler and event batching misdocumented (sync processing, withResolvers flush, CONTRIBUTING sample fails)
findings.note: apps/docs/architecture/overview.md describes the batch (registry events mark the results dirty, SEARCH_CHANGE refilters when it runs, NAVIGATE/ITEM_ACTIVATE refilter first, one stateChange at most) and the exclusion rule (`false`, 0 or a negative score drops the item; machine.ts:73-87, :155, :260-279); fix round 144191e.

findings.claim: `virtualizeThreshold` (default 100) is documented as configurable, and the 1.2.2 changelog 'corrected' docs to it. The option is read nowhere.
findings.fix: Honour it in list.tsx (on at threshold, off at half) in a 1.x minor, or remove it from the docs and types.
findings.groupTitle: virtualizeThreshold documented and typed but read nowhere

findings.claim: The recommended tsconfig target/lib 'ES2026' is rejected by the installed TypeScript 7.0.2. Every 'ES2026 target' phrase across the docs names a target that does not exist.
findings.fix: Recommend target ES2025 or ESNext with lib ES2025 + ESNext.Disposable + DOM, and reword to 'ES2025 + Explicit Resource Management'.

findings.claim: Says radix-ui is an optional peer needed for '<Command.Dialog> only'. The whole modern-cmdk/react entry statically imports radix-ui, so any import fails without it.
findings.fix: Document radix-ui as required for modern-cmdk/react, or split Dialog into a modern-cmdk/react/dialog subpath.
findings.groupTitle: radix-ui documented as optional for Dialog only, but the whole react entry imports it

findings.claim: 'You do not need to install Radix separately unless you use it directly' contradicts installation.md:L20-28 ('will not install them automatically ... install the ones you use'). Both misstate the truth (DT-15).
findings.fix: Make one true statement in both pages.
findings.groupTitle: radix-ui documented as optional for Dialog only, but the whole react entry imports it

findings.claim: Says 'Drop-in compatibility ... works identically for basic usage'. cmdk infers an item's value from its text; modern-cmdk requires value. Several cmdk props have no equivalent.
findings.fix: List these as breaking changes and limit 'drop-in' to code that already passes value. W9-07 (b7e151c): the 'drop-in' and 'works identically' claims are gone, breaking change 9 and the Complete API Differences table name root defaultValue, forceMount on Item and Group, Loading progress and the root's div props (tests DT-17); W9-07d (d589750): section 9 lists every cmdk 1.1.1 prop modern-cmdk lacks (also Separator alwaysRender, Loading and List label, Group value, a ReactNode Group heading, asChild on every part, Dialog defaultValue) and breaking change 10 plus a table row say Command.Item onSelect receives no argument in 1.x (cmdk passes the value; 2.0 adds it, ARCH-62), each a TS2322 fact against cmdk 1.1.1's index.d.ts and the modern-cmdk source. W11-03 (2ca6ce3): section 9 and the table also name `role` on Command.Input (CommandInputProps omits it, packages/modern-cmdk/src/react/input.tsx:14; the input renders combobox over any passed role, as cmdk did), the gap the post-fix re-review found in the 'every prop' claim; the test's needles now cover every row label, including `label` on Command.Loading and `value` on Command.Group (re-review finding 2).
findings.groupTitle: 'Drop-in compatibility' claim ignores required value and missing cmdk props

findings.claim: Says that after ITEM_SELECT, SEARCH_CHANGE '' boosts 'settings' to filteredIds[0]. Frecency never re-ranks the empty query, which is exactly the Raycast/Alfred case the page cites.
findings.fix: Apply frecency bonuses to the empty query (1.x minor), or document that frecency only re-ranks non-empty searches.
findings.groupTitle: Frecency never re-ranks the empty query, contrary to frecency.md
findings.note: apps/docs/guide/frecency.md passes one module storage to <Command> as a view with a no-op dispose (StrictMode disposes the caller's storage, react/hooks/use-command-setup.ts:52-56; probe: inline 0 records, view 1), says IdbFrecencyStorage dispose only marks itself disposed (idb-storage.ts:193-228), and reads the core sample from subscribeState with a non-empty query because frecency re-ranks only non-empty filtered queries (machine.ts:165-178); fix round 7c5cae8.

findings.claim: The CSS tokens are declared only on [data-command-root], which in dialog mode sits inside [data-command-dialog-content]; the overlay is a sibling. The dialog, overlay and content consume these vars with no fallback, so blur, radius, max-width and enter/exit transitions resolve invalid.
findings.fix: Declare the tokens on :where([data-command-root],[data-command-dialog],[data-command-overlay]) inside a layer, and document the real selector.
findings.groupTitle: CSS tokens declared only on the root (dialog and overlay miss them) and left unlayered

findings.claim: Says 'The base hue is controlled by a single CSS custom property --color-hue' and documents an OKLCH --color-* palette. The library ships no such tokens; they belong to the docs site's own VitePress theme.
findings.fix: Rewrite the guide around the real --command-* tokens and label the OKLCH palette as a copyable example theme.
findings.groupTitle: Theming guide documents the docs site's --color-hue palette instead of the library's --command-* tokens

findings.claim: 'Telemetry middleware -- pluggable hooks for palette open/close, search, selection' suggests events fire automatically. createTelemetryMiddleware returns methods that nothing calls, and there is no telemetry option on the machine or any React prop.
findings.fix: Add a telemetry machine option that invokes the middleware (1.x minor), or document manual invocation.
findings.groupTitle: Telemetry middleware advertised as hooks, but nothing calls it
findings.note: packages/modern-cmdk/README.md names no RegExp.escape, says the later shortcut binding wins with getConflicts/getBindings (core/keyboard/index.ts:21-22, :89-107), runs its core sample as const, subscribe, send and teardown, and says createTelemetryMiddleware returns hooks the caller invokes (core/telemetry.ts; no telemetry option in core/types.ts); follow-ups 6880ab2 and e1c6229, the same telemetry wording in the api page (27a9475), CONTRIBUTING (fe25b20) and ARCHITECTURE (8131bba).

findings.claim: Says the React budget '~10.2 KB' measures 'the adapter's own code'. dist/react/index.mjs inlines a full second copy of the core, so apps importing both entries ship the core twice as separate module instances.
findings.fix: Use one multi-entry tsdown build with a shared chunk (or externalise the core as modern-cmdk), then re-measure and state the real adapter-only size.
findings.groupTitle: React entry inlines a second core copy; the '~10.2 KB adapter' figure is false

findings.claim: `continue-on-error` hides a red E2E job: the axe WCAG 2.1 AA audits fail on main while the workflow, CI Summary and README badge all show green. This also falsifies the 'Full accessibility' and WCAG AA claims.
findings.fix: Fix the axe violations, remove continue-on-error, and add e2e to the summary's fail condition.

findings.claim: changesets/action@v1 with @changesets/cli 3.0.1 published 1.2.2 to npm but pushed no tags and created no GitHub releases.
findings.fix: Bump to changesets/action v2.1.2, verify that tags are pushed and releases created, then backfill modern-cmdk@1.2.2 and create-modern-cmdk@1.2.1.

findings.claim: GitHub state lags npm: the 'Latest' release is modern-cmdk@1.2.1, there are no tags or releases for 1.2.2 / create 1.2.1, and a stray v1.1.5 tag duplicates modern-cmdk@1.1.5.
findings.fix: Create the missing releases through the release flow (CLAUDE.md forbids manual tag pushes) and delete or document v1.1.5.
findings.groupTitle: GitHub releases and tags lag npm (no 1.2.2 / create 1.2.1; stray v1.1.5)

findings.claim: The root CHANGELOG has no 1.2.2 entry and none for 1.0.0-1.1.1 (tags exist), jumping from 0.10.0 to 1.1.3. It duplicates the changesets changelogs in different words.
findings.fix: Make the root CHANGELOG an index linking the per-package changesets changelogs, and backfill the gaps.
findings.groupTitle: Root CHANGELOG misses 1.2.2 and 1.0.0-1.1.1 and duplicates the changesets changelogs

findings.claim: The regression baseline dates from v0.9.0 on 2026-03-07 (node 25.8.0, ubuntu-24.04, TS 6.0.1-rc). Its bundleSize block (2.8/4.2 kB, limits 3.5/5.0) contradicts size-limit, and its $schema file does not exist.
findings.fix: Re-baseline on the CI runner image, drop or correct bundleSize, and add the schema or remove $schema.
findings.groupTitle: Bench baseline dates from v0.9.0 and CI gates only 3 of 12 entries against it

findings.claim: The comparison table says cmdk 'Search: Basic substring'. cmdk 1.1.1 ships the fuzzy command-score scorer.
findings.fix: Use 'Fuzzy (command-score), not pluggable'.
findings.groupTitle: README comparison table misstates cmdk 1.1.1 (substring search, React 18, external keyboard)

findings.claim: Claims machine options use NoInfer<T>. CONTRIBUTING lists NoInfer and const type params as patterns in use, and overview.md:L278 lists NoInfer. None exist in source.
findings.fix: Remove the claims or actually apply the patterns.
findings.groupTitle: NoInfer and const type parameters claimed but absent from source

findings.claim: The vulnerability contact security@crimson.dev is likely unreachable or goes to a third party, and GitHub private vulnerability reporting is off. The 48 h / 24 h SLAs are unenforced.
findings.fix: Enable GitHub private vulnerability reporting, point SECURITY.md at it, and verify or drop the e-mail (owner action).
findings.groupTitle: SECURITY.md contact likely unreachable; private vulnerability reporting off

findings.claim: The GitHub wiki (36 pages), linked from the README and issue template, is frozen at v1.1.0 and states TypeScript 6.0.1-rc, Node 25.8.0 and old bundle sizes: a fourth, unmaintained copy of the docs.
findings.fix: Replace the wiki with a single Home page pointing at the docs site, or disable it.
findings.groupTitle: GitHub wiki frozen at v1.1.0 (TS 6 rc, Node 25)

findings.claim: 'Uses RegExp.escape (ES2026) for safe pattern construction from user-provided strings' is false. The parser only splits on '+'. Repeated at L56, L589, L678 and guide/shortcuts.md:L122.
findings.fix: Remove the claim.
findings.groupTitle: Phantom RegExp.escape and Promise.withResolvers claims (~40 places)

findings.claim: og:image and twitter:image point at /og-image.png, but only og-image.svg exists, and on a dead host.
findings.fix: Render a 1200x630 PNG into public/ and use the live origin.
findings.groupTitle: og:image and twitter:image point at a missing og-image.png

findings.claim: 'Fuzzy match highlight' and 'Match highlighting: Yes' imply integration, but match ranges never reach React state or hooks; users must score items themselves to feed Highlight.
findings.fix: Document the manual path, or expose matches via useCommandState (1.x minor).
findings.groupTitle: 'Match highlighting' implies integration, but match ranges never reach React state

findings.claim: The cmdk column says React 18 and 'Keyboard: External'. cmdk 1.1.1 supports React 19 and ships arrow, Home/End and vim bindings.
findings.fix: Use 'React 18/19' and 'No shortcut registry'.
findings.groupTitle: README comparison table misstates cmdk 1.1.1 (substring search, React 18, external keyboard)

findings.claim: 'All library styles use @layer command' is false: the token block and @property rules are unlayered, so they outrank every layered user override.
findings.fix: Move the token block into @layer command.base, or reword.
findings.groupTitle: CSS tokens declared only on the root (dialog and overlay miss them) and left unlayered

findings.claim: The copyright holder is inconsistent. The root LICENSE says Albert Badalov (commit 057662c standardized it), while the README and the four package LICENSE files that npm ships say Crimson Dev.
findings.fix: Use one holder everywhere (owner decision).
findings.groupTitle: Copyright holder differs between the root LICENSE and the shipped package LICENSE/README

findings.claim: The repo description says 'TypeScript 6 / ES2026' and carries a typescript6 topic, while the project uses TypeScript 7.0.2.
findings.fix: gh repo edit: update the description and replace the topic with typescript7.
findings.groupTitle: Repo description and topic still say TypeScript 6 / ES2026

findings.claim: The bundlephobia badge and link for the modern-cmdk/react subpath 404, and both bundlephobia shields currently render 'rate limited'.
findings.fix: Use a static badge generated from size-limit output.
findings.groupTitle: Bundlephobia badge 404s for the react subpath and shows rate-limited

findings.claim: The 'Absolute Performance' figures contradict the only recorded source and are not reproducible. The WASM row cannot have been measured, because pkg/ is never built.
findings.fix: Generate the table from a committed bench:ci results JSON and mark WASM figures 'not measured in CI'.
findings.groupTitle: Absolute and WASM-vs-TS performance figures contradict each other and are unmeasured

findings.claim: The head-to-head table comes from a happy-dom unit test that only asserts times > 0, with no environment or date recorded. The '1.0x faster' tie is counted as a win in '14 of 15', and 'precision' is actually recall.
findings.fix: Regenerate with tinybench into a committed file with the environment recorded, and use 'recall' plus honest win counts.
findings.groupTitle: Head-to-head vs cmdk table comes from a happy-dom test; ties counted as wins; 'precision' is recall

findings.claim: 'CI enforces 5%/15% thresholds' overstates the gate: only 3 of the 12 baseline entries are compared, against the stale March baseline.
findings.fix: Name the gated benchmarks or gate all of them, and re-baseline.
findings.groupTitle: Bench baseline dates from v0.9.0 and CI gates only 3 of 12 entries against it

findings.claim: 'The WASM engine implements the same ScorerFn interface' is wrong: it implements SearchEngine and plugs in through the `search` option.
findings.fix: Use 'implements SearchEngine; pass via search:'.
findings.groupTitle: ARCHITECTURE says the WASM engine implements ScorerFn; it implements SearchEngine

findings.claim: 'Consumers who only import createCommandMachine do not pay for KeyboardShortcutRegistry or FrecencyEngine' is false.
findings.fix: Say that only unused exports (IdbFrecencyStorage, telemetry, TypedEmitter, ...) are shaken.
findings.groupTitle: False claim that createCommandMachine-only consumers skip the shortcut registry and frecency

findings.claim: The budget table lists 'Time to first render < 50 ms — Playwright performance trace' and 'Memory per 10K items < 5 MB — heap snapshot' as enforced. Neither check exists.
findings.fix: Mark these as targets, or add the specs.
findings.groupTitle: Budget table lists TTFR < 50 ms and memory < 5 MB checks that do not exist
findings.note: ARCHITECTURE.md's budget table marks time to first render and memory per 10K items as targets and lists the 10K mount as the browser-bench job's tripwire at 75 ms (D94) from the runner's first 47.80 ms median (benchmarks/browser/stats.ts MOUNT_GATE_THRESHOLD_MS on 1.6/gates 100727b); D94 wording in 3aebc5d. The code half is the browser-bench job of the BENCH landing (1.6/bench 31a3f87..d679edc) and 100727b.

findings.claim: Says Set methods, Map/Object.groupBy and Promise.try 'have not landed in browsers', so helpers are mandatory. These have been in all engines since 2024/25 and on the Node >= 26.4 runtime. L553 then says to use native .intersection().
findings.fix: State a browser floor and go native (2.0, or a minor if the floor allows), or give the true reason for keeping the helpers.
findings.groupTitle: CONTRIBUTING says Set methods, groupBy and Promise.try have not landed, so helpers are mandatory

findings.claim: benchmarks.yml duplicates the ci.yml bench job (same triggers, build, bench:ci and artifact name) but without bench:compare, yet it is described as 'Benchmark tracking' and 'a dedicated CI workflow'.
findings.fix: Delete benchmarks.yml or make it the only bench job.
findings.groupTitle: benchmarks.yml duplicates the ci.yml bench job without bench:compare

findings.claim: 'All PRs require at least one approval. The CI must pass.' Main is unprotected, and the E2E/security jobs are listed as checks but cannot fail the run.
findings.fix: Add branch protection and real gates, or reword.
findings.groupTitle: CONTRIBUTING claims required approvals and passing CI, but main is unprotected and the E2E/security jobs cannot fail

findings.claim: The changelogs credit features the code does not have: retained withResolvers and RegExp.escape, a RegExp.escape parser, WeakRef emitter, useInsertionEffect registration, and <Offscreen> Activity.
findings.fix: Add an erratum entry rather than rewriting history.
findings.groupTitle: Changelogs credit features the code lacks; needs an erratum entry

findings.claim: The npm README duplicates about 80% of the root README, so every root error ships twice, and the two copies have already diverged (badges, styles import, guide links).
findings.fix: Make the package README the canonical short page and have the root README link to it.
findings.groupTitle: npm README duplicates about 80% of the root README and has diverged

findings.claim: The docs advertise aria-keyshortcuts="Mod+C". The item passes the raw shortcut string, but 'Mod' is not a valid aria-keyshortcuts key name.
findings.fix: Emit the platform-resolved form (Control+C / Meta+C) via parseShortcut.
findings.groupTitle: aria-keyshortcuts emits the raw 'Mod+C', which is not a valid key name

findings.claim: Says shortcuts are 'active even when the command palette is closed'. Item shortcuts live on mounted Command.Items, and inside Command.Dialog the content unmounts while closed.
findings.fix: Qualify the claim to inline <Command>, or keep a registry outside the dialog content.
findings.groupTitle: Docs say item shortcuts stay active while the palette is closed, but Dialog content unmounts

findings.claim: Says uncontrolled mode 'manages its own open/close state' and can be toggled by a useEffect, but no state is exposed and nothing opens it. L32 omits the required item value. L97 says 'separate Command instances' but shows two Dialogs.
findings.fix: Document controlled mode as the working mode, or add defaultOpen/hotkey props in a 1.x minor.
findings.groupTitle: Docs present an uncontrolled Command.Dialog that nothing can open

findings.claim: The samples create a new promise every render (fetchCommands(), searchAPI(query)), the pattern ssr.md:L72 says 're-suspends forever'. They also use native Object.groupBy and a non-null assertion, and the 'debounced' sample has no debounce.
findings.fix: Cache the promises (keyed cache/useMemo), add a real debounce, and use the project's helpers.
findings.groupTitle: Async-items samples create a new promise every render, skip the debounce and use native groupBy

findings.claim: Says [data-command-list] { will-change: transform } with transform: translateY positioning and smooth scroll-to-active. The code differs on every point and also contradicts CONTRIBUTING's GPU-only and RTL rules.
findings.fix: Align the doc with the code, and flag the height transition and physical left for the CSS lens.
findings.groupTitle: Virtualization guide (will-change, translateY, smooth scroll) contradicts the code

findings.claim: The docs present <Command search={workerEngine}> as working. The worker engine's synchronous search() yields the cache from the last searchAsync(), and the machine never calls searchAsync(), so results are stale or empty.

findings.claim: React mount and unmount are O(n^2): each Command.Item sends REGISTER_ITEM, and each event re-indexes, runs a full refilter() and emits.
findings.fix: Within a scheduler batch, apply all REGISTER/UNREGISTER events to the registry and engine, then run one refilter and one emit (dirty flag). Use swap-remove or tombstones for order.
findings.groupTitle: Each REGISTER_ITEM/UNREGISTER_ITEM re-indexes and runs a full refilter and emit, so mount and unmount are O(n^2) (10K mount ~9.9 s)
findings.note: The browser gate measures it: 10K mount median 18.80 ms (min 14.70, max 26.80; Chromium 158, 7 runs after 1 warm-up) at efe658c against 6415.2 ms before the CORE landings (roadmap: about 9.9 s).

findings.claim: Incremental pruning also runs for custom scorers and options.filter, which need not be monotone. A min-length filter returns zero results permanently.

findings.groupTitle: Incremental pruning also runs for non-monotone custom scorers and options.filter, so results vanish for good
findings.note: Landed as 3a8b472 (cherry-pick of 583997a). Incremental pruning runs only with the default scorer and compares lowercased queries; a custom scorer or filter rescans every item per keystroke (restores the ARCHITECTURE.md Plug Points filter row; changeset note under LD-05). The case-folding corner it also fixes is CE-105, pending its own test.

findings.claim: IDB frecency never persists through the machine. Sync dispose queues the save, then disposes storage, so IdbFrecencyStorage.save returns early. The machine never calls flush().
findings.fix: Save on recordSelection (debounced or idle), save before disposing storage, and do not dispose a storage the caller passed in.
findings.groupTitle: Sync dispose queues the save and then disposes storage; machine never flushes, so IDB frecency is never saved
findings.note: Two of three parts landed in 1.6.0: the engine saves on recordSelection (debounced) and on pagehide, and the storage is disposed only after its last save (e8c042e, 640f4ce). The third, not disposing a storage the caller passed in, changes the ownership contract the 1.x docs state and is pinned as the 1.x behaviour by 'P07: the machine disposes the storage the caller passed in, after its last save' (c76f788); it moves to 2.0.0 with DG-09's ownership question.

findings.claim: 'Frecency with time-based exponential decay' is false (also README L39, package README, ARCHITECTURE L266, api/command.md L234, types.ts L136). The model is a 5-step function.

findings.groupTitle: 'Frecency with time-based exponential decay' is false on README, package README, ARCHITECTURE, command.md and types.ts; model is a 5-step function

findings.claim: dist/react/index.mjs inlines a full second copy of core (about 36 KB of 67 KB raw). Using both entries ships core twice, with two class identities and two module caches.

findings.claim: find_match_ranges sets start=abs_pos+1, which slices inside a multibyte char when the needle starts with one, causing a panic (wasm trap). Ranges are byte offsets into the lowercased copy, not UTF-16 offsets.
findings.fix: Use match_indices, or advance by the first char's len_utf8, and map ranges to UTF-16 offsets on the original value.
findings.groupTitle: find_match_ranges advances start by one byte, which panics inside a multibyte char; ranges are byte offsets, not UTF-16

findings.claim: Queries under 3 chars match only items whose whole value is under 3 chars. Duplicate trigrams push idx several times, so scores exceed 1.0. Keywords are never indexed.
findings.fix: Fall back to a substring scan or bigram index for short queries, dedupe trigrams per item, and index keywords.
findings.groupTitle: Queries under 3 chars match only short values, duplicate trigrams push scores past 1.0, keywords are never indexed

findings.claim: The trigram index uses SipHash HashMap<String,Vec<usize>>. Each query allocates a HashMap sized items/4, and each hit re-lowercases its value. Indexing crosses the boundary as a JSON string.
findings.fix: Use u32-packed trigram keys with FxHash or sorted postings, a reused dense Vec<u16> counter, pre-lowered values, and a typed-array transfer.
findings.groupTitle: SipHash HashMap<String,Vec<usize>>, a per-query HashMap, per-hit re-lowercasing and a JSON-string boundary

findings.claim: The whole scorer module (levenshtein_distance, max_typo_tolerance) is unused.
findings.fix: Delete it, or wire it into search with tests.
findings.groupTitle: The whole scorer.rs module (levenshtein_distance, max_typo_tolerance) is unused

findings.claim: The miss path allocates: scoreWordBoundary and scoreFuzzy each allocate a matches array before knowing whether the item matches.
findings.fix: Run a zero-allocation subsequence pre-check, and build ranges only on success (or write into a reused Int32Array).
findings.groupTitle: scoreWordBoundary and scoreFuzzy allocate match arrays before knowing whether the item matches

findings.claim: Every word-boundary match scores exactly 0.7: totalWeightedLen always equals 2*qLen on success, so the weighting is dead arithmetic.
findings.fix: Score on segment count, coverage of word starts and first-match position.
findings.groupTitle: Every word-boundary match scores exactly 0.7; the weighting is dead arithmetic
findings.note: Landed as cea3cfd (cherry-pick of 2ee5ca5). The constants differ from the row's proposal: 0.65 + 0.03*contiguity + 0.02*coverage keeps every word-boundary score in (0.65, 0.7), above the fuzzy tier, as the spec's tier order requires (the proposed 0.3 + 0.25c + 0.15r would rank 'Gas' above 'Git: Stage All Changes' for 'gs'); the cover backtracks, failed covers are cached by smallest failing start per query index, and queries over 512 characters fall to the fuzzy tier (changeset note). Brute-force cross-check of about 62M query/target pairs by the cluster's verifier: 0 mismatches.

findings.claim: Highlight ranges can mark the wrong characters. They are computed on toLowerCase output (which can change length), and keyword-match ranges index into the keyword, not item.value.
findings.fix: Use length-preserving per-unit case folding or an offset map, and add an optional field marker to SearchResult.
findings.groupTitle: Highlight ranges are computed on toLowerCase output and keyword ranges index the keyword, so wrong characters are marked
findings.note: The SearchResult.matches JSDoc in search/types.ts (8c52018) states that ranges index the original item.value and a keyword-only match reports matches: [].

findings.claim: The empty query builds a Set of all ids that is never read, because incremental requires previousQuery.length>0.
findings.fix: Replace it with previousResults.clear().
findings.groupTitle: Incremental search still walks all n items, rebuilds the Set, and builds an unread id Set on an empty query

findings.claim: The incremental path still iterates all n items with a Set probe and rebuilds the Set, so it brings no gain for broad prefixes.

findings.groupTitle: Incremental search still walks all n items, rebuilds the Set, and builds an unread id Set on an empty query

findings.claim: Each keystroke makes about 7 O(n) allocations and a second O(n log n) frecency sort.
findings.fix: Pass the bonus into engine scoring for a single sort, build the Set and index in one loop, and compute groups lazily.
findings.groupTitle: Each keystroke makes ~7 O(n) allocations and a second O(n log n) frecency sort

findings.claim: The unbounded frecency bonus (>=4 after one recent use) is added to match scores in [0,1], so any fuzzy junk match of a used item outranks an exact match. Frequency never decays and records are never pruned.
findings.fix: Bound or normalize the bonus (for example match*(1+a*tanh(f))), use continuous half-life decay with dt clamped >= 0, and cap the record count.
findings.groupTitle: An unbounded frecency bonus (>=4) is added to [0,1] match scores, so junk matches outrank exact ones; frequency never decays, records never pruned

findings.claim: Disabled items are dropped for an empty query or filter:false, but included in search results.

findings.groupTitle: Disabled items are dropped for an empty query or filter:false but included in search results
findings.note: R2/D78 disabled contract landed as 74ee107 (52057c7: disabled items rendered with aria-disabled and data-disabled, skipped by NAVIGATE, ITEM_ACTIVATE and ITEM_SELECT, excluded from the first active item; `disabledItems: 'hide'` restores the hidden rendering) and 8ddd517 (9760e16: 'hide' also drops ids a self-indexing engine returns). Proof set: tests/unit/disabled-matrix.test.ts, the 'disabled items' describe of command.test.tsx and the D78 e2e test. Visible side effects at rest for the changeset: a group holding only disabled items shows; Command.Empty no longer appears when only disabled items exist; filteredCount, the results announcement and the virtualization threshold count disabled items.

findings.claim: 'Search wrapped in transition - input stays responsive' is false: the store emit happens later, outside startTransition, and uSES updates are synchronous.

findings.groupTitle: 'Search wrapped in transition, input stays responsive' is false: the emit runs outside startTransition and uSES updates are sync

findings.claim: Measured sizes are keyed by index and never invalidated on filter changes. The built-in list never calls measureElement (no data-index), so it always uses the 44 px estimate and variable heights or headings are mispositioned.

findings.groupTitle: Sizes are keyed by index and never invalidated, measureElement is never attached, and totalSize, start index and scrollToIndex are linear scans

findings.claim: totalSize is an O(count) loop and the start index a linear scan from 0 on every scroll. scrollToIndex is O(index) and always aligns to the top.
findings.fix: Use a prefix-sum Float64Array with binary search, rAF-coalesced scroll, and 'nearest' alignment.
findings.groupTitle: Sizes are keyed by index and never invalidated, measureElement is never attached, and totalSize, start index and scrollToIndex are linear scans

findings.claim: IndexedDB frecency never persists. Nothing calls flush(). The machine's dispose is sync: it schedules save() in a microtask and then disposes storage, which sets #disposed, so IdbFrecencyStorage.save() returns early. Data is lost every session (CWE-664).
findings.fix: Flush on a debounce/idle after recordSelection and on pagehide. Save before disposing storage. Add a fake-indexeddb reload test.
findings.groupTitle: IndexedDB frecency never persists (no flush; dispose disables storage before save)
findings.note: Landed as e8c042e (1.6/frecency 6c8ba72): recordSelection schedules one trailing save after FLUSH_DELAY_MS (1000 ms); pagehide and visibilitychange-to-hidden save and cancel the timer; flush() clears the timer and the dirty flag before the save; load() merges stored records into the engine's own map (frequencies add, lastUsed takes the later); the sync dispose starts the quiet save and disposes the storage only once every save settled. Titles: 'CE-01: sync dispose disposes the storage only after the save settled'; 'CE-15: selections recorded before an async load resolves are merged, not dropped' (DG-62's guide claim is now true of the code); 'SEC-02: three selections at 0/400/800 ms give one save at 1800 ms with all three counted'; 'SEC-02: pagehide saves and cancels the pending timer'; DG-08's round trip is 'DG-63: a machine saves its selections to IndexedDB and a second machine ranks by them (TUB-24, CE-31, SEC-02, DG-08)' (c76f788). Verified Chromium only; the real-browser order of pagehide vs visibilitychange is unverified. The guide pages (:35, :41) are re-read by DOCS.

findings.claim: Persisted IndexedDB data is trusted without validation. Corrupt, foreign or stale-schema values throw in deserializeData or inject NaN or negative values into ranking (CWE-20/CWE-502).
findings.fix: Validate each record (array, string ids, finite numbers in range), drop bad ones, and add a schema version.
findings.groupTitle: Persisted IndexedDB records are trusted without validation or a schema version
findings.note: Landed as b292896 (0ff75e8): the reader treats what idb-keyval returns as untrusted (a row is kept only when its id is a string and both numbers are finite and >= 0; a version other than undefined, 1 or 2 yields empty data and one warning; nothing stored yields empty data without a warning); save still writes the v1 shape; a second storeName in an existing database upgrades the database to add its store (idb-keyval 6.3.0 creates stores only in onupgradeneeded of a new database). Titles: 'SEC-26: drops invalid rows, keeps valid ones and warns once with the dropped count'; 'CE-60: a valid v2 payload { version: 2, records } loads the same as v1'; 'SEC-35: a second storeName in an existing database saves and loads, and the first keeps its data'. CE-112 (1.7.0) records the three-store VersionError race this leaves.

findings.claim: load() is fire-and-forget from the machine, so a rejection (IDB blocked or corrupt) goes unhandled. A late load replaces #data and erases selections recorded before hydration finished (CWE-755/362).
findings.fix: Catch and fall back to memory. Merge loaded records with in-memory ones.
findings.groupTitle: Fire-and-forget load(): unhandled rejection, and a late load erases selections made first
findings.note: Landed as 640f4ce (af1ac92, re-adapted to the batching block of c339027 after the rebase): the machine handles its frecency load (a rejection is reported once through console.warn('[modern-cmdk] frecency load failed:', error), the row CE-60 format, because the machine has no error path: ruling), marks its results dirty once the engine merged the stored records and commits unless a batch is pending (whose own commit picks up dirty), skips the refilter when already disposed, and gains [Symbol.asyncDispose] (awaits the engine's flush, then the sync dispose) on the factory's return type CommandMachine & AsyncDisposable while the exported interface stays unchanged (LD-05, ruling). Titles: 'CE-14: hydration re-ranks the current results without another event'; 'CE-14: a load that settles after dispose does not search or emit' (red without the guard: search called twice); 'SEC-27: a rejecting load is reported once and the machine keeps working'; 'CE-02: await using flushes the pending save before the block ends'; 'CE-02: a synchronous dispose of a dirty machine still persists the selection'. Hostile verifier on the adapted commit: CONFIRMED (hydration with and without a pending batch, the microtask path, the guard, StrictMode does not bring CE-78 back, dispose order, LD-05 types). Follow-ups filed: CE-109 (redundant emit at an empty query), CE-110 (error channel).

findings.claim: Records grow without bound and the whole namespace is rewritten on each save. QuotaExceededError is not handled, and concurrent tabs are last-writer-wins (CWE-770).
findings.fix: Add a maxRecords cap with age pruning, catch quota errors, and use idb-keyval update() (6.3.0).
findings.groupTitle: Frecency records grow without bound, quota errors are unhandled, and concurrent tabs are last-writer-wins

findings.claim: The raw glob goes straight to globby. Backslash patterns silently match nothing on Windows, gitignore is off, and symlinks are followed by default, so writes can land outside the project (CWE-59; symlink part plausible, not reproduced).
findings.fix: Apply convertPathToPattern(), set gitignore:true and followSymbolicLinks:false, and filter by extension.
findings.groupTitle: Raw glob to globby: Windows backslashes match nothing, gitignore off, symlinks followed

findings.claim: .js files with JSX are parsed with the ts parser and fail. Directory arguments expand to every file type. CSS files are never transformed, although the migration guide (L41) promises --cmdk-* CSS variable renames.

findings.claim: In dev, the hook exposes the raw search query on a global and broadcasts it to all page scripts via a CustomEvent. The CRIMSON brand is a leftover. The docs claim the effect is tree-shaken in prod, which the published dist contradicts.

findings.remaining: modern-cmdk's dist/codemod still embeds undeclared copies of jscodeshift, recast, ast-types, @babel/parser, flow-parser, esprima, source-map, tslib and tiny-invariant (chunk-jscodeshift.mjs). findings.claim: Nine release-age exclusions are now dead standing bypasses. There is no explicit minimumReleaseAge and no trustPolicy. The lockfile carries two @types/node versions.

findings.claim: idb-keyval createStore only creates the store in onupgradeneeded on a new DB, so a second storeName in an existing dbName fails with NotFoundError.
findings.fix: Document one store per DB, or derive dbName from storeName.
findings.groupTitle: A second storeName in an existing dbName fails with NotFoundError
findings.note: Landed as b292896 (0ff75e8): the reader treats what idb-keyval returns as untrusted (a row is kept only when its id is a string and both numbers are finite and >= 0; a version other than undefined, 1 or 2 yields empty data and one warning; nothing stored yields empty data without a warning); save still writes the v1 shape; a second storeName in an existing database upgrades the database to add its store (idb-keyval 6.3.0 creates stores only in onupgradeneeded of a new database). Titles: 'SEC-26: drops invalid rows, keeps valid ones and warns once with the dropped count'; 'CE-60: a valid v2 payload { version: 2, records } loads the same as v1'; 'SEC-35: a second storeName in an existing database saves and loads, and the first keeps its data'. CE-112 (1.7.0) records the three-store VersionError race this leaves.

findings.claim: Disabled items are removed only when the query is empty or filtering is off. The search path keeps them, so they are invisible at rest but appear, and can become the active item, once the user types. The tests contradict each other, and the e2e disabled-item tests never run their bodies.
findings.fix: Render disabled items with aria-disabled in both paths and skip them in NAVIGATE and active selection. Add machine and e2e tests that run with a query.
findings.groupTitle: Disabled items reappear and become active once a query is typed
findings.note: Core half in 74ee107; e2e half in c27c040 (55f2f29: the accessibility spec's disabled-item tests run their bodies against the rendered disabled option) and 34be920 (0b2c597: keyboard.spec 'D78: should skip the rendered disabled item during keyboard navigation'); Chromium e2e 106 passed on the merged tree.
