findings.claim: Several tests read machine state synchronously after send(). send() is deferred by the scheduler, so the events have not been processed yet and the assertions check the initial state. No memory is actually measured.
findings.fix: Flush the scheduler or vi.waitFor the expected end state. Measure listener counts or use FinalizationRegistry; otherwise delete the tests.
findings.groupTitle: Machine tests assert state before the deferred scheduler runs (sync reads, vacuous waitFor negatives)
findings.note: Landed as fd88993 (4805538): the memory-leak suite processes its events and measures. Titles: 'T13, MEM-1, MEM-3: 100 lifecycles process their events, leave no machine reachable after dispose, and the final machine\'s "Item 5" query keeps item-5 and drops item-0'; 'MEM-3: 10K unsubscribed listeners are released while the machine stays alive, and never fire'; 'MEM-3: dispose releases the subscribers of a machine that is still referenced'; 'MEM-2: 5000 register/unregister pairs leave only the persistent item in the registry and the filtered ids'. Red from five machine.ts mutations (SEARCH_CHANGE without refilter, subscribe cleanup a no-op, dispose without emitter dispose, UNREGISTER a no-op, a module-level array keeping every machine), each turning the new suite red with the old file green except the first. Ruling: vitest.config.ts gives the unit project execArgv ['--expose-gc'] (Vitest 5.1.0 InlineConfig.execArgv, per project, passed to fork(); poolOptions no longer exists) because the emitter is private and WeakRef plus gc() is the only real leak measure. 4 passed, 10 of 10 runs.

findings.claim: React tests leak state updates outside act(): 534 warnings across 6 files. The render helpers await one microtask, but under happy-dom requestAnimationFrame is setImmediate, so machine updates land after act. The 'queueMicrotask scheduler' comments are wrong.
findings.fix: Use one shared render helper with vi.useFakeTimers({toFake:['requestAnimationFrame','setImmediate']}) and act(()=>vi.runAllTimersAsync()), or move to Vitest browser mode with vitest-browser-react.

findings.claim: Negative assertions inside vi.waitFor pass on the first poll, before the scheduled ITEM_SELECT has run, so they prove nothing.
findings.fix: Flush the scheduler first, then assert the negative synchronously.
findings.groupTitle: Machine tests assert state before the deferred scheduler runs (sync reads, vacuous waitFor negatives)
findings.note: machine.test.ts steps batches with fake requestAnimationFrame frames (the 50 vi.waitFor polls are gone) and the negatives run after the frame: 'T15: a disabled item is not selected: the batch that runs ITEM_SELECT leaves its onSelect uncalled' (red with the !item.disabled guard dropped: 1 of 68), 'TUB-09: with loop false NAVIGATE next stays on the last item: the batch ran and the active item did not wrap' and 'TUB-09: PAGE_POP on the root page changes nothing: the batch ran and the page stays root' (red with loop ignored or PAGE_POP on root: 1 of 68 each), 'TUB-39: the using scope disposes the machine: the registry and the keyboard registry are cleared' (red with either registry dispose deleted). Wave B of CORE/tests; verifier B1 PASS_WITH_NITS (the body's poll count corrected to 50).

findings.claim: Several tests contain zero assertions or never perform the interaction they name.

findings.claim: The comment says a handler 'may or may not be called due to WeakRef', but the emitter holds strong references. The emit after scope exit is never asserted.

findings.note: Already fixed by 03bd455 (after the ledger's e55cce7 reading): the emit after scope exit is asserted and the WeakRef comment is gone. Proof 'should auto-unsubscribe via Disposable using declaration' goes red when the returned Disposable is a no-op (CORE/tests wave A, 2026-11-08).

findings.claim: About 41 of the file's 69 tests cannot fail. 23 timing tests assert only '> 0', and 18 cmdk 'baseline' tests assert '>= 0' or 'typeof boolean'. They inflate the 416 test count and cost about 3.6 s.
findings.fix: Move timing into benchmarks/ (vitest bench or tinybench). Keep the accuracy corpus as test.for cases with real thresholds.
findings.groupTitle: Timing tests that cannot fail and an unfair cmdk head-to-head printed as winners, inside unit tests
findings.note: At 1a6c208 the file holds 75 tests, 21 of them cmdk baseline tests that cannot fail (they assert typeof topCorrect or >= 0); PERF-13 switched the record-only cmdk ranking on for three more cases by ruling, because asserting it would pin a third-party library's ranking. The redesign stays here (1.9.0) with PERF-14.

findings.claim: The head-to-head is unfair. Ours rebuilds and re-indexes the engine inside the timed loop while cmdk only filters. cmdk's React render is always measured first, cold. Results come from happy-dom (no layout) and are printed as 'WINNER x faster'.
findings.fix: Do equal work on both sides, interleave warmed tinybench tasks in a real browser, and report medians with variance. Never print winners from unit tests.
findings.groupTitle: Timing tests that cannot fail and an unfair cmdk head-to-head printed as winners, inside unit tests

findings.claim: The metric labelled 'precision' is found/expected, which is recall.

findings.claim: Comment claims are false: 'plus configurable vim bindings' (none exist); cmdk loop is 'identical, enabled by default' (cmdk's loop is opt-in); there is a 'controlled state equivalent' (there is no controlled value); a '15. forceMount' section is listed but absent; the header gives wrong package paths.

findings.claim: 17 e2e tests silently pass via conditional early returns (`if (count<2) return`, `if (hasTrigger)`, `if (count>0)`) against our own known fixture.

findings.claim: The Ctrl+K dialog tests check visibility with the non-retrying isVisible() right after the key press, so the test body is effectively always skipped. They also hard-code Control, but macOS/WebKit needs Meta.

findings.claim: Several e2e selection and page-pop tests assert no outcome. Console messages are collected and then ignored.
findings.fix: Have the playground expose the last selection and page stack (a data attribute or live region) and assert them.
findings.groupTitle: E2e selection and page-pop tests assert no outcome; console messages are ignored

findings.claim: Some reads race the UI: scrollTop and count() are read immediately after input. Many waits use expect(first()).toBeVisible(), which is already true, so they wait for nothing.
findings.fix: Use expect.poll(() => list.evaluate(e => e.scrollTop)), toHaveCount or toHaveJSProperty in place of the fake waits.
findings.groupTitle: Virtualization e2e reads race the UI, and visibility waits wait for nothing

findings.claim: Some matchers can never fail. The regex /(true|)/ matches any value. A null from getAttribute still passes toBeDefined(). The aria-busy test never triggers a loading state.

findings.groupTitle: Accessibility e2e matchers can never fail (/(true|)/, toBeDefined on null, aria-busy never triggered)

findings.claim: The failure artifact step uploads playwright-report/, but the CI reporter is 'github' only, so no HTML report is ever written and the upload is always empty.

findings.claim: All tokens are declared on [data-command-root], but in Command.Dialog the overlay is a sibling and [data-command-dialog] / [data-command-dialog-content] are ancestors of the root. The vars are undefined there: no backdrop blur, no max width or radius, and the transition durations become invalid.
findings.fix: Declare the defaults on :where(:root), or on [data-command-root], [data-command-dialog], [data-command-overlay].
findings.groupTitle: CSS tokens declared on [data-command-root] are missing in the dialog and overlay and cannot be overridden on :root

findings.claim: The data-state=closed exit transitions never play, because Radix Presence delays unmount only for CSS animations, not transitions.
findings.fix: Use @keyframes exit animations (Presence waits for animationend), or forceMount with custom presence. Drop the `overlay` allow-discrete transitions, which only apply to top-layer elements.
findings.groupTitle: data-state=closed exit transitions never play under Radix Presence

findings.claim: The reduced-motion rule targets `*, *::before, *::after`, so importing the library stylesheet changes animation and transition durations across the whole host page.
findings.fix: Scope it to [data-command-root], [data-command-root] *, [data-command-dialog] and [data-command-overlay].
findings.groupTitle: Reduced-motion rule targets *, changing the host page's animations

findings.claim: `{...props}` is spread after onClick, style, id and role. A consumer onClick replaces handleSelect (selection breaks), a consumer style drops virtual positioning, and a consumer id breaks aria-activedescendant.
findings.fix: Compose handlers (call the consumer's, then select unless defaultPrevented), merge style, and spread props before the managed attributes.
findings.groupTitle: Item {...props} spread after onClick/style/id replaces selection and positioning

findings.claim: statusContainerRef.current is read during render and is null on the first render, so an Empty shown at mount renders inside role=listbox (invalid ARIA) and only moves into the portal on a later render, which remounts it.
findings.fix: Have List keep the container element in state via a callback ref and provide the element, not a ref.
findings.groupTitle: Empty reads statusContainerRef in render, so it renders inside the listbox at mount and then remounts

findings.claim: There is no isComposing guard: the Enter that commits an IME composition also selects the active item, and arrow keys during composition move through the list.
findings.fix: Return early when `event.isComposing` is true.
findings.groupTitle: No isComposing guard: IME Enter selects and arrows navigate

findings.claim: startTransition around machine.send changes an external store, which React always renders as a blocking update. isPending is effectively always false, the claim "input stays responsive" is false, and Command.Loading's isPending path is dead.
findings.fix: Keep the query in React state and derive results with useDeferredValue, or drop the transition and the claim.
findings.groupTitle: startTransition/useOptimistic around a sync external store do nothing (isPending, setOptimisticActiveId)

findings.claim: The promise stabilization ref does nothing (it always takes the new prop), so the comment "Prevents infinite re-suspension" is false; a promise created during render re-suspends forever.
findings.fix: Remove the ref and document that callers must cache the promise (the React `use` contract), or accept a loader plus a key and cache internally.
findings.groupTitle: AsyncItems: useless promise ref and loaded items never unregistered

findings.claim: ITEMS_LOADED has no cleanup, so loaded items stay registered after unmount or after a new promise. If children(items) also renders Command.Item for the same data, each entry exists twice.
findings.fix: Unregister the loaded ids in the cleanup, and document whether children should render Command.Item.
findings.groupTitle: AsyncItems: useless promise ref and loaded items never unregistered

findings.claim: The formatted shortcut depends on isMac, which core computes from navigator at module load. The server renders "Ctrl+K" while a macOS client renders the Command glyph, so hydration mismatches.
findings.fix: Format through useSyncExternalStore with a platform-neutral server snapshot, or after mount.
findings.groupTitle: Command.Shortcut formats from module-load isMac, so hydration mismatches

findings.claim: Command.Highlight wants "match ranges from search scorer", but no adapter API exposes them, and keyword hits return ranges into the keyword string rather than the value. The component cannot be driven from the React surface.
findings.fix: Add useItemMatches(id) or machine.getMatches(id) returning ranges relative to the value.
findings.groupTitle: Command.Highlight has no adapter API for match ranges

findings.claim: Command.Dialog has the same frozen-options problem as Command: only onOpenChange is routed through a ref; onSelect, onSearchChange, filter and items stay as they were at first render.
findings.fix: Use useEffectEvent or a latest-ref for every callback, and sync items/filter.
findings.groupTitle: Command and Command.Dialog capture options and callbacks once at first render

findings.claim: The react bundle inlines the whole core instead of importing the core entry, so apps that import both modern-cmdk and modern-cmdk/react ship two cores with two module states.
findings.fix: Mark ../core/index.js external in the tsdown react entry and rewrite it to 'modern-cmdk' (or emit a shared chunk).
findings.groupTitle: React entry inlines a second copy of core

findings.claim: useOptimistic is set inside a transition with no async work, so it reverts immediately. Its only caller (item.tsx L67-68) sends ITEM_ACTIVATE synchronously right after, so the optimistic layer never shows anything and still costs a transition and an object spread.
findings.fix: Remove it at the next major (it is public in UseCommandReturn and the stable context), or use it only around an async action.
findings.groupTitle: startTransition/useOptimistic around a sync external store do nothing (isPending, setOptimisticActiveId)

findings.claim: primitives.ts is orphaned: it is excluded from tsconfig and coverage, nothing imports it, and it contains JSX in a .ts file that cannot compile.
findings.fix: Delete the file and both exclude entries.
findings.groupTitle: Orphaned primitives.ts (JSX in .ts, reads deprecated element.ref)

findings.claim: Activity has been a stable React export since 19.2. The runtime `'Activity' in React` probe, the namespace import and the cast exist only because the peer floor is react>=19.0.0.
findings.fix: Raise the react/react-dom peer floor to >=19.2.0 and `import { Activity } from 'react'`, or keep the probe and fix the comments.
findings.groupTitle: Activity probe and cast exist only because the peer floor is react>=19.0

findings.claim: The header says it wraps palette contents in Activity when the dialog closes and preserves selection without remount. Nothing wires it to the dialog, the fallback path unmounts, and hidden Activity runs effect cleanups that unregister items and dispose a contained machine.
findings.fix: Correct the prose, and make registration and disposal Activity-safe.
findings.groupTitle: activity.tsx header claims a dialog wiring and a no-remount behaviour that do not exist

findings.claim: The @example calls useCommandDevtools in the component that renders <Command>, where both contexts are null, so the hook silently does nothing.
findings.fix: Show the call inside a child component of <Command>.
findings.groupTitle: useCommandDevtools emits twice per change and its @example calls it outside <Command>

findings.claim: The prop doc says "If not provided, reads from nearest Command.Item"; the component reads no context and just renders its children.
findings.fix: Implement an item context or correct the doc.
findings.groupTitle: Shortcut prop doc claims it reads from the nearest Command.Item

findings.claim: The header claims "page stack management, View Transitions API"; the file manages no stack and uses no view transition.
findings.fix: Correct the comment, or wrap pages in a feature-detected <ViewTransition> with addTransitionType('push'|'pop').
findings.groupTitle: page.tsx header claims page-stack management and View Transitions

findings.claim: "inert on background" is false: no inert is set anywhere. Radix uses aria-hidden on siblings (hideOthers) plus a scroll lock.
findings.fix: Describe the actual mechanism, or adopt inert.
findings.groupTitle: dialog.tsx header claims 'inert on background'

findings.claim: "Override these on [data-command-root] or :root": overrides on :root have no effect inside the root, because the [data-command-root] declaration is closer.
findings.fix: Move the defaults to :where(:root) so :root overrides work.
findings.groupTitle: CSS tokens declared on [data-command-root] are missing in the dialog and overlay and cannot be overridden on :root

findings.claim: The Command root accepts only className and label (no ref, style, id, data-* or event props), unlike every other part and unlike cmdk 1.1.1's Root.
findings.fix: Extend Omit<ComponentPropsWithRef<'div'>, keyof CommandMachineOptions> and spread it onto the root div.
findings.groupTitle: Command root takes only className and label (no ref/style/id/data-*/events)

findings.claim: Nothing tests useCommandDevtools, StrictMode/Activity lifecycle, visual vs navigation order, group visibility remount, Empty on first render, IME Enter, prop changes after mount, Highlight, Shortcut SSR or ErrorBoundary.
findings.fix: Add one regression test per bug, RA-01 through RA-21.
findings.groupTitle: No tests for devtools, StrictMode/Activity, prop changes, order, Empty, IME, Highlight, Shortcut SSR, ErrorBoundary

findings.claim: changesets/action@v1 cannot parse @changesets/cli 3.x publish output, so after a successful publish it never pushes tags or creates GitHub releases. That is why tags and releases stop at modern-cmdk@1.2.1 / create-modern-cmdk@1.2.0 while npm has 1.2.2 / 1.2.1.
findings.fix: Upgrade to changesets/action v2.1.2: inputs become publish-script/version-script/commit-message/pr-title, and the GITHUB_TOKEN env is dropped. Then backfill tags and releases for modern-cmdk@1.2.2 and create-modern-cmdk@1.2.1 at 3367825 (owner decision).

findings.claim: The E2E job is continue-on-error and the summary fails only on lint/test, so the axe WCAG failures on main are reported green and the README CI badge says passing.
findings.fix: Fix the axe violations, remove continue-on-error at L61, and add e2e/size/bench to the 'Fail if critical jobs failed' condition (L177).
findings.groupTitle: CI Summary fails only on lint/test, so a red E2E still reports green

findings.claim: The deployed docs site loads without CSS/JS. Pages serves it at abcrimson.github.io/modern-cmdk/ (cname empty), but VitePress builds with base '/', so every /assets/... URL 404s. The intended custom domain command.crimson.dev is NXDOMAIN.
findings.fix: Either configure the custom domain (DNS CNAME to abcrimson.github.io plus the Pages cname setting) or set base '/modern-cmdk/' in apps/docs/.vitepress/config.ts. Owner decision on the domain.
findings.groupTitle: Deployed docs 404 their assets: VitePress base '/' under the /modern-cmdk/ Pages path

findings.claim: The only vulnerability-reporting channel, security@crimson.dev, is undeliverable, and GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting is disabled.
findings.fix: Enable PVR and make /security/advisories/new the primary channel. Keep the email only after MX records exist.
findings.groupTitle: No working vulnerability-reporting channel (dead email, PVR off)

findings.claim: The first quick-start example renders <Command.Highlight>Copy to Clipboard</Command.Highlight>. CommandHighlight requires text and ranges props and ignores children, so the example fails to type-check and throws a TypeError on ranges.length at runtime.
findings.fix: Use plain text in the item, or show <Command.Highlight text="Copy" ranges={matches} /> with a real source for the ranges.
findings.groupTitle: README quick start uses <Command.Highlight> children; it needs text and ranges, so the example fails to typecheck and throws

findings.claim: The claims 'modern-cmdk wins 14 of 15 benchmarks, up to 5.9x faster' and the table L234-250 are false today. The same claim sits in the GitHub repo description.
findings.fix: Re-measure with a proper harness (tinybench, many iterations, outside happy-dom). Publish dated figures with the environment, or remove the table and the repo-description claim.
findings.groupTitle: README benchmark wins and absolute timings are unmeasured or copied

findings.claim: The Absolute Performance figures (~8.2 ms, ~0.7 ms WASM, ~1.1 ms filter, ~2.3 ms) are copied from a March 2026 baseline and do not even match it. WASM is benchmarked by nothing.
findings.fix: Regenerate the figures from a current run with date and environment. Mark WASM unmeasured. Only the bundle rows (6.29/10.17 kB) are current.
findings.groupTitle: README benchmark wins and absolute timings are unmeasured or copied

findings.claim: Every docs link (L21-25, L327, L333-341) targets https://command.crimson.dev, which does not resolve.
findings.fix: After RDG-03 is resolved, point every link at the working host, including the repo homepage.
findings.groupTitle: README, issue templates and SECURITY scope link the NXDOMAIN command.crimson.dev

findings.claim: happy-dom 20.11.10 falls inside an open high advisory. The playground's vite 8.2.2 also has open advisories (fixed in 8.2.4).
findings.fix: Pin happy-dom 21.0.4 and vite 8.3.5, then update the pnpm-workspace.yaml minimumReleaseAgeExclude L23 entry.

findings.claim: The doc says the keyboard parser 'Uses RegExp.escape (ES2026)' (also L56, L589, L678). No source file calls RegExp.escape.
findings.fix: Delete the RegExp.escape claims and describe the real parser (split, trim, lowercase, alias map, deterministic normalized string).
findings.groupTitle: Docs credit RegExp.escape, WeakRef and scheduler withResolvers that no source uses

findings.claim: The event emitter is described as 'GC-safe ... WeakRef ... automatically pruned', with has/listenerCount on Iterator Helpers. It actually holds strong references and uses Set.size.
findings.fix: Rewrite the section: strong refs, one Set per event, snapshot-on-emit, Disposable from on().
findings.groupTitle: Docs credit RegExp.escape, WeakRef and scheduler withResolvers that no source uses

findings.claim: The WASM claims 'Sub-1ms on 100K items' (L65, L301) and '<= 50 KB minified+gzipped' are unmeasured and false.
findings.fix: State ~55 KB gzip and label the latency a target. Alternatively wire a WASM bench into the standalone harness and re-measure.
findings.groupTitle: ARCHITECTURE states unmeasured WASM 'sub-1ms on 100K' and '<= 50 KB'

findings.claim: The 'Native ES2026 (use directly)' table lists RegExp.escape (keyboard parser) and Promise.withResolvers (scheduler), and L114 says the emitter uses WeakRef. None of these hold.
findings.fix: Correct the table to what is used (Iterator Helpers, using, toSorted, the ??= lazy import), and move withResolvers to the WASM worker row.
findings.groupTitle: Docs credit RegExp.escape, WeakRef and scheduler withResolvers that no source uses

findings.claim: The root changelog's newest entry is 1.2.1. modern-cmdk 1.2.2 and create-modern-cmdk 1.2.1 were released 2026-08-27 and are missing.
findings.fix: Add the 1.2.2 entry, or turn the root file into an index linking to the changesets-generated per-package changelogs.
findings.groupTitle: Root CHANGELOG is a drifted hand-kept copy missing 1.2.2 and pre-1.1.3 history

findings.claim: The issue chooser's Documentation contact link points at the dead domain command.crimson.dev. bug_report.yml L97 links the same domain.
findings.fix: Use the working docs URL in config.yml L4 and bug_report.yml L97.
findings.groupTitle: README, issue templates and SECURITY scope link the NXDOMAIN command.crimson.dev

findings.claim: The scope lists 'Documentation site (command.crimson.dev)', a domain that does not resolve.
findings.fix: Name the live site URL.
findings.groupTitle: README, issue templates and SECURITY scope link the NXDOMAIN command.crimson.dev

findings.claim: The upload-on-failure step targets playwright-report/, but the CI reporter is 'github', so no HTML report is ever written and failure triage has no artifact.
findings.fix: Use reporter [['github'],['html',{open:'never'}]] in CI, and also upload test-results/ (retain-on-failure traces).
findings.groupTitle: Upload-on-failure targets playwright-report/, but the CI reporter writes none

findings.claim: The security audit can never fail: the job is continue-on-error and the step ends with `|| echo ::warning`, while 7 Dependabot alerts (2 high) are open.
findings.fix: Land the happy-dom/vite bumps, then remove both masks so a green result means a clean audit.

findings.claim: Both benchmark workflows upload benchmarks/results/, but ci-bench.ts writes no files, so every run warns and uploads nothing. The same applies to ci.yml L141-146.
findings.fix: Have ci-bench write JSON to benchmarks/results/ (and gitignore it), or delete the upload steps.
findings.groupTitle: Benchmark workflows upload benchmarks/results/, which ci-bench never writes

findings.claim: This whole workflow duplicates the ci.yml bench job (same triggers, install, build and bench:ci), so every push and PR benchmarks twice.
findings.fix: Delete benchmarks.yml, or keep it and drop the ci.yml bench job.
findings.groupTitle: benchmarks.yml duplicates the ci.yml bench job

findings.claim: CI typechecks only modern-cmdk. The playground, create-modern-cmdk, the WASM package and the docs app are never typechecked in CI.
findings.fix: Add typecheck steps for playground and create-modern-cmdk, plus a WASM job that runs build:wasm before typecheck.
findings.groupTitle: CI and lefthook typecheck only modern-cmdk; playground, create and WASM are never typechecked

findings.claim: NODE_VERSION 26.4.0 (also in benchmarks/docs/release.yml) disagrees with .nvmrc 26.8.1 and trails the newest (26.13.0 LTS / 27.0.0-alpha.0). The actions are behind and pinned by mutable tags.
findings.fix: Use node-version-file: .nvmrc everywhere, SHA-pin each action with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment, and land the w-ci bump branch.
findings.groupTitle: Workflows hardcode NODE_VERSION apart from .nvmrc, and actions use mutable tags

findings.claim: Docs build only on push to main. There is no PR build, so a broken VitePress build is found only after merge.
findings.fix: Add a pull_request trigger, or a build-only job running `pnpm docs:build` without the deploy steps.
findings.groupTitle: Docs build only on push to main; no PR build

findings.claim: Dependabot assigns each dependency to the first matching group. dev-dependencies (listed first) swallows typescript, biome, playwright and vitest, so those 4 groups never form.
findings.fix: Order the specific groups before dev-dependencies, or delete them.
findings.groupTitle: dev-dependencies group swallows the specific Dependabot groups

findings.claim: 9 superseded Dependabot PRs (#22-#39, March to June 2026) are still open, and no npm PR has appeared since June even though 65 of 76 pins are behind.
findings.fix: Close the stale PRs. Verify that Dependabot still parses the pnpm 12 lockfile, or reduce it to a security-only role and rely on the dep-freshness sweep.

findings.claim: One open CodeQL alert has not been addressed: js/missing-origin-check in the WASM worker message handler.
findings.fix: Validate event.source/origin in worker.ts (wasm cluster). The alert closes on the next analysis.
findings.groupTitle: Open CodeQL js/missing-origin-check alert on the WASM worker
findings.fixedBy: CodeQL alert js/missing-origin-check dismissed as a false positive 2026-11-03 (DECISIONS G-05; DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope has no foreign sender)

findings.claim: The root `typecheck` script is red on a fresh clone because it includes modern-cmdk-search-wasm, which needs wasm-pack output. CLAUDE.md L14 and the PR template present it as a gate.
findings.fix: Guard the WASM typecheck with the same existsSync check its build uses, or move it to a WASM CI job after build:wasm.
findings.groupTitle: Root typecheck is red on a fresh clone because WASM needs pkg/

findings.claim: @testing-library/react 16.3.2 and @testing-library/user-event 14.6.6 are imported by no test.
findings.fix: Remove both, or migrate the React tests to RTL. Either way, make CONTRIBUTING L471 true.
findings.groupTitle: Unused root devDependencies (@testing-library/*, @js-temporal/polyfill)

findings.claim: @js-temporal/polyfill 0.5.1 is imported nowhere; Temporal was replaced by Date.now() in 1.1.3. apps/playground/package.json also lists it.
findings.fix: Remove it from root and playground, or adopt native Temporal after a Baseline check.
findings.groupTitle: Unused root devDependencies (@testing-library/*, @js-temporal/polyfill)

findings.claim: Many devDependency pins trail the newest release on any channel.
findings.fix: Apply the orchestrator bump. Only after it lands, update every doc line that names a version (README, CONTRIBUTING, CLAUDE.md, lefthook comment, biome $schema).
findings.groupTitle: devDependency pins trail the newest release, plus the doc lines that name versions

findings.claim: size-limit has no budget for dist/react/styles.css or for the codemod bin dist/codemod/cli.mjs. The 2.46 MB codemod ships in every modern-cmdk install.
findings.fix: Add a styles.css budget, and budget or externalize the codemod (or move it to its own package; codemod cluster).
findings.groupTitle: size-limit has no budget for styles.css or the 2.46 MB codemod bin

findings.claim: 'pnpm version' is documented as updating versions from changesets, but pnpm 12's built-in `version` command shadows the root script.
findings.fix: Rename the script (e.g. version:packages) and document `pnpm run version:packages` or `pnpm changeset version`.
findings.groupTitle: CONTRIBUTING documents `pnpm version`, which pnpm 12's built-in shadows

findings.claim: `pnpm --filter modern-cmdk/react run dev` matches no workspace project; modern-cmdk/react is a subpath export, not a package.
findings.fix: Delete the line.
findings.groupTitle: CONTRIBUTING's `--filter modern-cmdk/react` matches no workspace

findings.claim: The sample unit test reads getState() synchronously after send(). send() is scheduled (rAF/microtask), the '// Flush the scheduler' line has no flush, and the example fails.
findings.fix: Make the example async: `await vi.waitFor(() => expect(machine.getState().filteredCount).toBe(1))`.
findings.groupTitle: CONTRIBUTING sample test reads getState() synchronously after a scheduled send()
findings.note: CONTRIBUTING.md's sample unit test is async, asserts the initial filteredCount and then awaits vi.waitFor on the filtered count, so it fails when filtering breaks (verified by running it; vitest 5.1.0 waitFor, machine.ts send).

findings.claim: 'All PRs require at least one approval. The CI must pass.' main has no branch protection and no rulesets.
findings.fix: Add a ruleset requiring the CI checks once the masked jobs are fixed, or reword the sentence as a convention.
findings.groupTitle: CONTRIBUTING says PRs need approval and passing CI, but main has no ruleset

findings.claim: 'Set methods over manual loops -- Use .intersection(), .difference(), .union()' (and the L593 commit example 'use Set.difference') contradict L397-399, which say to use helpers, not native methods.
findings.fix: Make it one policy after the Baseline decision on native Set methods.
findings.groupTitle: CONTRIBUTING and ARCHITECTURE contradict themselves on native Set methods and objectGroupBy versus the helpers

findings.claim: '.js extension suffix (required by verbatimModuleSyntax)' and 'Wrong -- will fail at runtime' (L751-758) are false. verbatimModuleSyntax governs type elision, and moduleResolution bundler plus tsdown bundling resolve extensionless imports.
findings.fix: Describe the .js suffix as a house convention, or adopt .ts specifiers with rewriteRelativeImportExtensions.
findings.groupTitle: CONTRIBUTING claims verbatimModuleSyntax requires the .js suffix and that omitting it fails at runtime

findings.claim: A top-level `using machine = ...` in the example module is disposed when the module finishes evaluating. The scheduled send() batch is then cleared, and the subscribe callback never fires, although the comment promises automatic cleanup.
findings.fix: Put the example in a block or async function that awaits a frame, or use const plus explicit disposal on teardown.
findings.groupTitle: README's top-level `using machine` is disposed before the scheduled batch fires
findings.note: Already true at 8c4feee: the root README.md has no core example with a top-level `using` any more; no edit. Closed FIXED at the RC gate pass of 1.6.0 (G-51): the page was already true when the DOCS cluster reached it, and the docs-content tests of 20f4403 and the doc-sample gate keep it so.

findings.claim: The comparison row says cmdk supports React 18 only. cmdk 1.1.1 supports React 18 and 19.
findings.groupTitle: README comparison misstates cmdk (React 18 only, basic substring)

findings.claim: The comparison row calls cmdk search 'Basic substring'. cmdk ships the fuzzy command-score scorer.
findings.fix: Write 'command-score fuzzy'.
findings.groupTitle: README comparison misstates cmdk (React 18 only, basic substring)

findings.claim: 'Virtual scrolling at configurable threshold' is false: the virtualizeThreshold option is read nowhere and List hardcodes 100/50.
findings.fix: Wire virtualizeThreshold into CommandList (react cluster), or drop 'configurable'. Also fix the npm README, which advertises it.
findings.groupTitle: README says virtualization threshold is configurable; virtualizeThreshold is read nowhere

findings.claim: The feature list claims 'RegExp.escape parsing' and 'ES2026 throughout -- ... Promise.withResolvers, RegExp.escape' (L68). RegExp.escape is unused, and withResolvers exists only in the unpublished WASM worker.
findings.fix: List the features actually used.
findings.groupTitle: Docs credit RegExp.escape, WeakRef and scheduler withResolvers that no source uses

findings.claim: The accessibility list advertises aria-roledescription, but no component sets it.
findings.fix: Remove the claim; a combobox does not need aria-roledescription.
findings.groupTitle: README advertises aria-roledescription, which no component sets

findings.claim: The core is described as 'No DOM'. ARCHITECTURE L79 says the same. Yet KeyboardShortcutRegistry attaches a document keydown listener, the parser reads navigator, and the scheduler uses requestAnimationFrame (all feature-detected).
findings.fix: Say 'No hard DOM dependency; DOM APIs are feature-detected and SSR-safe'.
findings.groupTitle: README and ARCHITECTURE call the core 'No DOM', but it feature-detects document, navigator and rAF

findings.claim: The README says 'Development requires Node.js >= 26.4.0', but the published packages declare engines.node >=26.4.0, so the requirement binds consumers' installs (engine-strict users on Node 24 LTS fail).
findings.fix: State the consumer requirement honestly, or relax the published engines for a browser library (owner decision).
findings.groupTitle: README frames Node >= 26.4 as a dev requirement, but published engines bind consumers

findings.claim: vscode-modern-cmdk is listed (L51 and L135) as an available VS Code extension, but it is not published anywhere.
findings.fix: Mark it '(unpublished)' as the WASM row does, or publish it.

findings.claim: The tech-stack row says 'VitePress ... Shiki twoslash', but twoslash is disabled.
findings.fix: Drop 'twoslash'; @shikijs/twoslash is then a dead devDependency (docs cluster).

findings.claim: The footer says 'Copyright (c) 2026 Crimson Dev', contradicting LICENSE L3 'Albert Badalov' (commit 057662c).
findings.fix: Write 'Albert Badalov'. Also update Cargo.toml authors and the wasm LICENSE.
findings.groupTitle: README footer copyright contradicts the LICENSE holder

findings.claim: The WASM package size is given as '<= 50 KB'; measured gzip is about 55 KB.
findings.fix: State ~55 KB gzip, or shrink the module.

findings.claim: The scheduler 'Uses Promise.withResolvers (ES2024) for the flush() method' (also L57, L588). flush() is synchronous.
findings.fix: Remove the claim, and attribute withResolvers to the WASM worker-engine.
findings.groupTitle: Docs credit RegExp.escape, WeakRef and scheduler withResolvers that no source uses

findings.claim: 'Bulk removal uses Set.difference (ES2026)' contradicts the code and this document's own L177/L591. The registry box at L55 also lists objectGroupBy, which the registry never uses.
findings.fix: Say 'uses the setDifference helper' and drop objectGroupBy from L55.
findings.groupTitle: CONTRIBUTING and ARCHITECTURE contradict themselves on native Set methods and objectGroupBy versus the helpers

findings.claim: The doc says a custom `filter` replaces the scorer and that WASM 'implements the same ScorerFn interface'. In fact filter returns number|false (no match ranges), and the drop-in replacement is the `search` option (SearchEngine).
findings.fix: Document `search: SearchEngine` as the pluggable engine and `filter` as a score override.
findings.groupTitle: ARCHITECTURE says `filter` replaces the scorer; the pluggable engine is actually `search: SearchEngine`

findings.claim: The Performance Budget 'Enforcement' column claims Vitest bench, a Playwright performance trace and a heap snapshot enforce targets. None of these checks exist.
findings.fix: Mark those rows 'target (not enforced)', or add the tests.
findings.groupTitle: ARCHITECTURE's performance budget claims enforcement by checks that do not exist

findings.note: Landed as fd88993 (4805538): the memory-leak suite processes its events and measures. Titles: 'T13, MEM-1, MEM-3: 100 lifecycles process their events, leave no machine reachable after dispose, and the final machine\'s "Item 5" query keeps item-5 and drops item-0'; 'MEM-3: 10K unsubscribed listeners are released while the machine stays alive, and never fire'; 'MEM-3: dispose releases the subscribers of a machine that is still referenced'; 'MEM-2: 5000 register/unregister pairs leave only the persistent item in the registry and the filtered ids'. Red from five machine.ts mutations (SEARCH_CHANGE without refilter, subscribe cleanup a no-op, dispose without emitter dispose, UNREGISTER a no-op, a module-level array keeping every machine), each turning the new suite red with the old file green except the first. Ruling: vitest.config.ts gives the unit project execArgv ['--expose-gc'] (Vitest 5.1.0 InlineConfig.execArgv, per project, passed to fork(); poolOptions no longer exists) because the emitter is private and WeakRef plus gc() is the only real leak measure. 4 passed, 10 of 10 runs.

findings.claim: The `--target web` wasm-bindgen glue has to have its default export (init) awaited before any class is constructed. It is never called, so `new wasm.WasmSearchEngine()` throws and the engine always falls back to the TS engine.
findings.fix: `const { default: init, WasmSearchEngine } = await import('../pkg/command_search_wasm.js'); await init({ module_or_path: new URL('../pkg/command_search_wasm_bg.wasm', import.meta.url) })`, or build with `--target bundler`.
findings.groupTitle: wasm-bindgen --target web init() is never awaited with an explicit .wasm URL (main thread and worker)
findings.note: Reproduced 2026-11-08 by the docs verifier against the built packages at 17a442a: createWasmSearchEngine() warns 'WASM search engine failed to load, falling back to TypeScript scorer: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'wasmsearchengine_new')' and returns the TypeScript fallback ({ id: 'item-1', score: 0.456, matches: [[0,4],[5,11]] } for the guide's 'applcation' sample); a hand initSync with pkg/*.wasm returns { score: 0.75, matches: [] }. guide/wasm-search.md:94 no longer quotes either set of numbers (1.6/docs-frecency d263e2c).

findings.claim: The worker also never calls init, so initWorker rejects, `void initWorker()` (L149) swallows the rejection, and 'ready' is never posted.
findings.fix: Await init with an explicit wasm URL. Wrap init in try/catch and post {type:'error'}; reject on that before ready; add AbortSignal.timeout.
findings.groupTitle: wasm-bindgen --target web init() is never awaited with an explicit .wasm URL (main thread and worker)

findings.claim: The sync search() ignores its query and yields the cache from the last searchAsync. Core only ever calls search() synchronously, so the worker engine returns stale or empty results. The 'state machine's async adapter' that L181-182 mentions does not exist.

findings.groupTitle: Worker engine's sync search() ignores the query and yields the last searchAsync cache; comment names a nonexistent async adapter

findings.claim: There is only one `pending` slot, so concurrent requests overwrite each other. index() (fire-and-forget) followed by searchAsync makes the search promise resolve with {type:'indexed'} and return [], and the real results are dropped. 'Sequential request queue' (L90) is false.
findings.fix: Tag requests with ids and keep a Map<id, resolvers>, or chain every request on one promise.
findings.groupTitle: One pending slot: concurrent worker requests overwrite each other

findings.claim: find_match_ranges advances by 1 byte, so `haystack[start..]` panics when a match starts with a multi-byte char. The wasm traps and the instance becomes unusable.
findings.fix: Use `haystack.match_indices(needle)`, or advance by needle.len(); add a multibyte test.
findings.groupTitle: find_match_ranges advances by one byte: overlapping ranges, multibyte panic, UTF-8 not UTF-16 offsets

findings.claim: A query under 3 chars becomes one 1-2 char key that only matches items whose whole value is 1-2 chars, so typing 'a' or 'ap' returns no results. An empty query yields [""], so the is_empty guard at L48 can never fire.
findings.fix: Use padded trigrams (' a', ' ap') at index and query time, or a prefix/substring scan for short queries; add tests.
findings.groupTitle: Queries under 3 chars match nothing, and the empty-query guard can never fire

findings.claim: 'Scoring uses the same multi-strategy approach as the default engine (exact > prefix > substring > fuzzy)' is false.
findings.fix: Describe trigram-overlap scoring, or implement the tiers.
findings.groupTitle: README claims exact > prefix > substring > fuzzy tiers; the engine scores by trigram overlap

findings.claim: The documentation link https://command.crimson.dev is dead.
findings.fix: Link https://abcrimson.github.io/modern-cmdk/.
findings.groupTitle: Dead documentation link to command.crimson.dev

findings.claim: The Web Worker usage example does not work (sync search is stale, W06) and is missing the createCommandMachine import.
findings.fix: Rewrite the example around searchAsync, or fix core first.
findings.groupTitle: Web Worker usage example does not work and lacks the createCommandMachine import

findings.claim: No JS tests exist for wasm-engine, worker-engine or worker. Coverage excludes the package, the wasm bench is excluded, and CI never runs wasm-pack, cargo test or clippy, so W01-W09 went undetected.
findings.fix: Add a CI job (wasm-pack build, cargo test/clippy) and vitest browser-mode tests that drive the engines through createCommandMachine.
findings.groupTitle: CI never runs wasm-pack, cargo test or clippy, and the package has no JS tests or coverage
findings.remaining: Clause (2) is open: wasm-engine.ts and worker.ts are still excluded from coverage (vitest.config.ts:42-43). Clause (3) is open: wasm-engine.ts and worker.ts still have no tests, and there are no browser-mode tests through createCommandMachine. [after 73527f0]

findings.claim: The entry lists only src/index.ts, so worker.ts is never emitted (the root cause of W03).
findings.fix: `entry: ['src/index.ts', 'src/worker.ts']`.
findings.groupTitle: worker.ts is not a tsdown entry, so dist references a missing './worker.ts'

findings.claim: Match ranges are UTF-8 byte offsets into the lowercased string, but JS expects UTF-16 indices into the original value, so highlights shift for non-ASCII text.
findings.fix: Map byte offsets to UTF-16 (`encode_utf16().count()` on the prefix) against the original value.
findings.groupTitle: find_match_ranges advances by one byte: overlapping ranges, multibyte panic, UTF-8 not UTF-16 offsets

findings.claim: Duplicate trigrams are counted more than once (item 'aaaaa' pushes its idx 3 times under 'aaa', and query trigrams are not deduped), so scores exceed 1.0 and cannot be compared with core scores or frecency bonuses.
findings.fix: Dedupe trigrams per item and per query (sort+dedup or HashSet).
findings.groupTitle: Duplicate trigrams are counted more than once, so scores exceed 1.0

findings.claim: Keywords are never indexed (only [id, value] is serialised), so items that core finds by keyword cannot be found with the WASM engine.
findings.fix: Index the value plus the keywords (e.g. a value + keywords array per item) in Rust.
findings.groupTitle: Keywords are never indexed by the WASM engine

findings.claim: `... && tsdown || echo Skipping` turns a real tsdown failure into exit 0 with a misleading 'Skipping' message, so CI build steps stay green on broken builds.
findings.fix: A node script that exits 0 only when pkg/ is missing and otherwise passes on tsdown's exit code.
findings.groupTitle: '&& tsdown || echo Skipping' masks real build failures as exit 0

findings.claim: Without pkg/, tsc --noEmit fails with TS2307, and the root `pnpm typecheck` includes this package, so it is red on any clone without a WASM build.
findings.fix: Build the WASM in CI before typecheck, or remove the package from the root typecheck filter until it is built.
findings.groupTitle: Root pnpm typecheck fails with TS2307 on a clone without pkg/

findings.claim: With platform 'browser', the library build folds the dev guard to true, so the dev-only console.warn ships unguarded and fires in consumers' production builds.
findings.fix: Use core's `globalThis.process ? ... : false` guard, or platform 'neutral'; drop the define.
findings.groupTitle: WASM dev guard folds to true under platform 'browser'; the __DEV__ define is shadowed and dead

findings.claim: `dts.isolatedDeclarations` is not an option in the installed rolldown-plugin-dts, so it is silently ignored. tsdown.config.ts is outside the tsconfig include, so the excess property is never type-checked.
findings.fix: `dts: { generator: 'oxc' }`, or `dts: true` (it auto-selects oxc when isolatedDeclarations is set, index.d.mts L20).

findings.claim: The `define: { __DEV__ }` never applies: wasm-engine.ts declares a local `const __DEV__`, which shadows the global define.
findings.fix: Drop the define and use one guard pattern shared with core.
findings.groupTitle: WASM dev guard folds to true under platform 'browser'; the __DEV__ define is shadowed and dead

findings.claim: The SAB is sized for the constructor's maxResults (default 50). searchAsync(q, 100) writes past the Float32Array end and then reads undefined scores; concurrent searches also share the one SAB.
findings.fix: Clamp limit to maxResultsLimit, or allocate per request; better still, drop the SAB path (W33).
findings.groupTitle: SharedArrayBuffer path overflows for limit > maxResults and is shared by concurrent searches, for a negligible gain

findings.claim: asyncDispose sets disposed=true before postAndWait, so postAndWait rejects at once and the dispose message is never sent. The worker never replies to dispose anyway, and pending requests are never rejected.
findings.fix: Post dispose directly, reject any pending request, then terminate().
findings.groupTitle: Worker asyncDispose never posts dispose and never rejects pending requests

findings.claim: The header says it 'Falls back to main-thread WASM when SharedArrayBuffer is unavailable', and L60 says it 'Falls back to main-thread WASM if Worker construction fails entirely'. Both are false.
findings.fix: Implement the fallback (try/catch around new Worker, delegating to createWasmSearchEngine) or delete the claims.
findings.groupTitle: worker-engine header claims fallbacks to main-thread WASM that do not exist

findings.claim: There is no double-dispose guard. Machine disposal calls searchEngine[Symbol.dispose]() and the JSDoc also recommends `await using engine`, so instance.free() runs twice. PLAUSIBLE that the second free traps on the null pointer.
findings.fix: Add a `disposed` flag guard to dispose and asyncDispose.
findings.groupTitle: Engine is disposed twice (by the machine and by the recommended 'await using'), so instance.free() runs twice

findings.claim: tsdown bundles the pkg glue into a dist chunk, so the glue's `new URL('command_search_wasm_bg.wasm', import.meta.url)` would resolve under dist/, where no .wasm is copied. PLAUSIBLE.
findings.fix: Externalise ../pkg/* (a deps.neverBundle regex) or pass init an explicit URL to ../pkg/*.wasm.
findings.groupTitle: wasm-bindgen --target web init() is never awaited with an explicit .wasm URL (main thread and worker)

findings.claim: wasm-bindgen 0.2.127 and serde_json 1.0.151 are behind the newest releases, and the requirements are caret ranges rather than exact pins.
findings.fix: `wasm-bindgen = "=0.2.130"`, `serde_json = "=1.0.154"`, = pins throughout; refresh Cargo.lock; match the wasm-bindgen CLI version.

findings.claim: The rustwasm installer script installs wasm-pack v0.13.1 from the old rustwasm org; the current release is 0.15.1 from wasm-bindgen/wasm-pack.
findings.fix: `cargo install wasm-pack --locked` (or cargo binstall wasm-pack), naming 0.15.1.
findings.groupTitle: README installs wasm-pack 0.13.1 from the old rustwasm installer

findings.claim: The peer requirement is given as 'modern-cmdk >= 1.0.2'; package.json says >=1.2.2.
findings.fix: Change it to '>= 1.2.2'.

findings.claim: The performance claims 'sub-millisecond fuzzy search on datasets of 100K+ items' and 'keeps UI at 60fps' are unverified; the WASM path has never executed.
findings.fix: Remove the figures until a real benchmark produces them.
findings.groupTitle: Unverified 'sub-millisecond on 100K+' and '60fps' WASM performance claims

findings.claim: The SharedArrayBuffer path moves only the 4-byte scores while ids and matches are still structured-cloned. The 'zero-copy' gain is negligible, and it doubles the code paths and the COOP/COEP coupling.
findings.fix: Remove the SAB path (structured clone only), or transfer one packed ArrayBuffer of all results.
findings.groupTitle: SharedArrayBuffer path overflows for limit > maxResults and is shared by concurrent searches, for a negligible gain

findings.claim: levenshtein_distance and max_typo_tolerance are never called; the module only adds dead code and dead_code warnings.
findings.fix: Delete scorer.rs, or wire typo tolerance into TrigramIndex::search.
findings.groupTitle: scorer.rs levenshtein_distance and max_typo_tolerance are never called

findings.claim: Every candidate's value is lowercased again on every search.
findings.fix: Store the lowercased value alongside the original in `items` at build time.
findings.groupTitle: Each candidate value is lowercased again on every search

findings.claim: The Rust tests do not cover multibyte match ranges (they would panic, W08), 1-2 char queries (W09), duplicate-trigram scores (W16), incremental indexing (W04) or the wasm-bindgen boundary.

findings.groupTitle: Rust tests miss multibyte ranges, short queries, duplicate trigrams, incremental indexing and the bindgen boundary

findings.claim: aria-keyshortcuts gets the raw shortcut string. "Mod", "Ctrl", "Cmd" and "Option" are not ARIA modifier names, so AT exposes an invalid shortcut. The `?? undefined` is dead code.

findings.claim: Transform failures lose their file path ('(unknown)') and are never reported. The codemod exits 0 silently even when every file fails to parse.
findings.fix: Wrap processFile's body in try/catch and return {filePath, changed:false, error}. Print changed paths (path.relative(process.cwd(), p)) to stdout and `${rel}: ${error.message}` to stderr. Set process.exitCode = 1 if errorFiles.length > 0.
findings.groupTitle: Transform failures lose their path and the process exits 0 when every file fails

findings.claim: Missing arguments print nothing (printUsage is empty) and exit 0, the same as --help.
findings.fix: Make printUsage write the usage line and the AVAILABLE_TRANSFORMS list. If argv has --help or -h, print usage to stdout and exit 0. Otherwise, when parseArgs returns null, print usage to stderr, set process.exitCode = 2 and return.
findings.groupTitle: Codemod CLI prints nothing (empty printUsage, empty report bodies, swallowed error)
findings.remaining: The default exit code for missing arguments stays 0 in 1.x (LD-05); --strict exits 2 since 1.3.0. Flipping the default is a 2.0.0 change.

findings.claim: Mounting N Command.Item components runs N full refilters and N stateChange emits (O(N^2)).

findings.groupTitle: Mounting N items runs N refilters (O(N^2) registration)
findings.note: Landed as c339027 (1.6/machine ccbdda4: one refilter and one emit per scheduler batch, a counter marks the batch end so the scheduler contract is kept) and a87d6d7 (884b6c0: no stale NAVIGATE/ITEM_ACTIVATE after a registry event in the same batch, a throwing filter still emits). Emit order change recorded for DOCS and the changeset: onOpenChange, onSearchChange and openChange run before the batch's single stateChange. BENCH's verifier measured a 10K mount median of 17.20 ms on the branch (6415 ms at 6171765).

findings.claim: Each search allocates an items/4 HashMap and builds a full SearchResult (clone, lowercase, match ranges) for every candidate, then sorts all and keeps max_results.
findings.fix: Use packed u64 trigram keys. Count into a reused Vec<u16>, which needs no new dependency. Take the top k (idx, score) pairs with select_nth_unstable_by, sort those, and build SearchResult only for the kept k.
findings.groupTitle: Search allocates a HashMap per query and builds a SearchResult for every candidate before taking the top k

findings.claim: cli.ts drops the path of failed files, has a dead promise, a strip that never matches on Windows, and gutted reporting. printUsage and the report loops are empty, so failures print nothing and the CLI exits 0.

findings.fix: Mark both snippets superseded and point to LONE_SURROGATE_RE in packages/modern-cmdk/src/core/utils/string-wellformed.ts:10, or replace them with /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/.
findings.groupTitle: Executed March plans carry no historical/status banner and still direct agents to execute superseded snippets, stacks and false API-availability rationale

findings.claim: The spec example at L1347 cannot pass: using captures [Symbol.dispose] at declaration, so the later spy override never runs. The id 'test' is not an ItemId either.
findings.fix: Spy before the declaration: create m, call vi.spyOn(m, Symbol.dispose), then write using machine = m. Or assert an observable disposal effect. Use itemId('test') for the id.
findings.groupTitle: Spec code examples cannot work: `using` on subscribe(), flat tinybench stats, dispose spy set after declaration

findings.claim: ?count=Infinity throws during render and unmounts the app, and a huge finite count hangs the tab.
findings.fix: const n = Number.parseInt(params.get('count') ?? '', 10); return Number.isSafeInteger(n) && n > 0 ? Math.min(n, 100_000) : DEFAULT_ITEM_COUNT;
findings.groupTitle: ?count=Infinity crashes the app and huge counts hang the tab

findings.fix: At L570, set grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(300px, 100%), 1fr)). Delete container-type and container-name at L572-573 and the @container states block at L589-593.
findings.groupTitle: States container query targets its own container and never matches

findings.claim: The hover glow ::after at L684-700 paints beneath the button's opaque background and border, so it never shows.
findings.fix: Add isolation: isolate to the .trigger-button rule at L684. The z-index:-1 glow then paints above the button background but below its text.
findings.groupTitle: Trigger button hover glow paints beneath its opaque background

findings.claim: formatShortcut shows multi-word named keys with broken casing (Arrowup, Pagedown) because the parsed key is lowercased and only its first letter is uppercased again.
findings.fix: Add a KEY_LABELS map in parser.ts (arrowup:'↑', arrowdown:'↓', arrowleft:'←', arrowright:'→', pageup:'PageUp', pagedown:'PageDown', escape:'Esc') and use displayKey = KEY_LABELS[key] ?? the current capitalization.
findings.groupTitle: formatShortcut labels: meta shown as Ctrl off-Mac, wrong macOS glyph order, broken multi-word key casing

findings.claim: The Disposable from KeyboardShortcutRegistry.register deletes whatever binding now sits under the normalized key, including a later registration that replaced it.
findings.fix: In register(), hold const binding = {shortcut,itemId,handler} and set it. In the disposer, delete only if this.#bindings.get(shortcut.normalized) === binding.
findings.groupTitle: Keyboard register() disposer deletes a later binding under the same key

findings.claim: OPEN and CLOSE always setState, emit openChange and call onOpenChange, even when state.open already equals the target. A controlled Command.Dialog calls onOpenChange(false) on mount.
findings.fix: In machine.ts handleEvent: case 'OPEN': if (state.open) break; then the existing body. case 'CLOSE': if (!state.open) break; then the existing body. TOGGLE stays as it is.
findings.groupTitle: OPEN/CLOSE always emit and call onOpenChange even when state is unchanged

findings.claim: Sending REGISTER_ITEM again for an existing id with a changed or removed shortcut leaves the old binding active, so the old key still fires onSelect.
findings.fix: In machine.ts case 'REGISTER_ITEM': call keyboardRegistry.unregisterByItem(event.item.id) before the conditional keyboardRegistry.register block.
findings.groupTitle: Re-registering an item leaves its old shortcut binding active
findings.note: Landed as aca8737 (4b10de3): REGISTER_ITEM again for the same id with a changed shortcut leaves no old binding.

findings.claim: The '__ungrouped' sentinel (machine.ts:156, registry.ts:148/161) is a plain GroupId string. Command.Group forceId='__ungrouped' counts as visible whenever ungrouped items match, so its heading renders over no matching children.
findings.fix: Export const UNGROUPED_GROUP_ID: GroupId = groupId('__modern-cmdk/ungrouped') from types.ts and use it in machine.ts and registry.ts. registerGroup throws a RangeError when group.id === UNGROUPED_GROUP_ID.
findings.groupTitle: '__ungrouped' sentinel is a plain GroupId a user group can collide with
findings.note: UNGROUPED_GROUP_ID is a public value export of the core entry since 3e1157a (tests/dist/exports.test.ts lists it; JSDoc: a group registered under this id shares the bucket and the bucket takes its priority; +18 B core). The constants table of apps/docs/api/command.md is DOCS's.

findings.claim: The disposers from CommandRegistry.registerItem, registerItems and registerGroup remove by id, so disposing a stale handle deletes a newer item or group registered under the same id.
findings.fix: registerItem disposer: if (this.#items.get(item.id) === item) this.unregisterItem(item.id). registerItems: unregister only ids still mapped to this batch's item. registerGroup: delete only if this.#groups.get(group.id) === group.
findings.groupTitle: Registry disposers remove by id, so a stale handle deletes a newer item or group
findings.note: Landed as 418c40b (40b2897: stale registry disposers no longer delete a newer item or group) and 200e6d5 (registerItems snapshots its array: a live array the caller mutates later changes nothing).

findings.claim: IdbFrecencyStorage.load does not validate shape (a non-array records throws, bad records give NaN lastUsed), and createCommandMachine fires load() unguarded, so failures become unhandled promise rejections.
findings.fix: deserializeData: if !Array.isArray(serialized?.records) return {records:new Map()}, and skip entries whose frequency or lastUsedMs is not Number.isFinite. machine.ts:92: frecencyEngine.load().catch((e)=>console.warn('[modern-cmdk] frecency load failed:',e)).
findings.groupTitle: Frecency load is unguarded, unvalidated, overwrites in-memory records and never refilters
findings.note: Landed as b292896 (0ff75e8): the reader treats what idb-keyval returns as untrusted (a row is kept only when its id is a string and both numbers are finite and >= 0; a version other than undefined, 1 or 2 yields empty data and one warning; nothing stored yields empty data without a warning); save still writes the v1 shape; a second storeName in an existing database upgrades the database to add its store (idb-keyval 6.3.0 creates stores only in onupgradeneeded of a new database). Titles: 'SEC-26: drops invalid rows, keeps valid ones and warns once with the dropped count'; 'CE-60: a valid v2 payload { version: 2, records } loads the same as v1'; 'SEC-35: a second storeName in an existing database saves and loads, and the first keeps its data'. CE-112 (1.7.0) records the three-store VersionError race this leaves.

findings.claim: TypedEmitter.emit has no per-listener isolation: one throwing listener skips every later listener for that event, including React's store subscription.
findings.fix: In emit: for (const fn of [...set]) { try { fn(data as never); } catch (error: unknown) { if (typeof globalThis.reportError === 'function') globalThis.reportError(error); else queueMicrotask(() => { throw error; }); } }
findings.groupTitle: One throwing listener skips every later listener in TypedEmitter.emit
findings.note: core/utils/event-emitter.ts: a throwing listener no longer skips the later listeners; its error is rethrown from a microtask (not reportError: the body states why). Test 'CE-75: a throwing listener does not skip the later listeners and its error is rethrown from a microtask' (red without the fix: 1 of 16). Public behaviour change of TypedEmitter.emit (no longer throws synchronously): the 1.6.0 changeset says so (DOCS).

findings.claim: scheduler.ts:20 reads the bare identifier navigator at module load, so the whole core entry throws ReferenceError on import in any runtime without a navigator global.
findings.fix: scheduler.ts:20: const hasInputPending: boolean = typeof globalThis.navigator?.scheduling?.isInputPending === 'function'; Line 41 is already short-circuited by hasInputPending.
findings.groupTitle: Chromium-only isInputPending gate: navigator read at load, unsliced re-queue, false header
findings.note: Same defect as CE-102, already FIXED by 3922d98 (scheduler.ts reads globalThis.navigator; test in scheduler.test.ts). The CORE/machine cluster re-found it on 2026-11-08 and changed nothing.

findings.claim: find_match_ranges advances `start = abs_pos + 1` in bytes, so ranges overlap and any matching lowered query that starts with a multi-byte char (e.g. 'écl' in 'éclair') panics. The ranges are also UTF-8 byte offsets, not UTF-16.
findings.fix: Replace the loop with `haystack.match_indices(needle).map(|(i, m)| (i, i + m.len())).collect()`. Convert the byte offsets to UTF-16 code-unit offsets before returning them, and add tests for 'aaa'/'aa' and a non-ASCII query.
findings.groupTitle: find_match_ranges advances by one byte: overlapping ranges, multibyte panic, UTF-8 not UTF-16 offsets

findings.claim: The main-thread WASM engine's index() replaces the whole index (trigram.rs:24-31), and REGISTER_ITEM indexes one item at a time, so only the last registered Command.Item can match. remove() clears the whole index, so one UNREGISTER_ITEM empties search.
findings.fix: Keep a Map<ItemId,value> in wasm-engine.ts. index() upserts into it and re-serializes the full map to index_items. remove() deletes the ids and re-indexes the remainder. Then filter search results to ids present in the passed `items`.
findings.groupTitle: index() replaces the whole index and remove() clears it instead of upserting or deleting
findings.note: FIXED at 81a0403 (1.7.0 C5): search() returns only ids among the passed items (a Set of the passed ids filters the crate's hits), as the SearchEngine contract in core/search/types.ts reads; the crate limit is the whole index size because trigram.rs truncates after sorting, so filtered-out ids cannot starve the result. Closing tests: 'W44: search() returns only ids among the passed items' (real build, on a fixture whose excluded item outscores the passed ones so the limit mutation is red) and the mocked 'W44: the result limit is not starved by the filtered-out ids'.

findings.claim: On macOS, formatShortcut emits glyphs in ⌘⌃⇧⌥ order, so 'mod+alt+k' renders ⌘⌥K. Apple's HIG requires ⌃⌥⇧⌘, which gives ⌥⌘K.
findings.fix: In parser.ts:109-112, branch on isMac. Mac order: ctrl ⌃, alt ⌥, shift ⇧, meta ⌘. Keep the current non-Mac text order, and add a unit test for 'mod+alt+shift+k' that expects ⌥⇧⌘K.
findings.groupTitle: formatShortcut labels: meta shown as Ctrl off-Mac, wrong macOS glyph order, broken multi-word key casing

findings.claim: The playground toggles change their visible label and aria-pressed together, a double-encoded state. The ErrorBoundary demo's 'Reset' sets showBroken=false, but the boundary keeps its error state, so the fallback never clears.
findings.fix: Use constant labels with aria-pressed, or drop aria-pressed and keep the action labels. Add a `resetKeys?: readonly unknown[]` prop to CommandErrorBoundary that clears the error in componentDidUpdate when it changes, and pass [showBroken].
findings.groupTitle: Playground toggles double-encode state, and the ErrorBoundary demo's Reset never clears

findings.claim: In forced-colors mode, matched characters render as LinkText plus underline and look like links. In the default theme the only cue is a ~1.1:1 background tint, so matches rely on a near-invisible colour difference.
findings.fix: In the forced-colors block, set [data-command-highlight] to `background-color: Mark; color: MarkText;` with no LinkText. In the base rule, add a non-colour cue (font-weight: 600 or an underline), or raise the tint so it reaches 3:1.
findings.groupTitle: Match highlight looks like a link in forced-colors mode and relies on a ~1.1:1 tint by default
