findings.fix: Delete the isInputPending branch (scheduler.ts:39-50), hasInputPending (:20), and src/core/es2026.d.ts (its only content). Keep executeBatch synchronous so flush() applies every update. Drop canYield if unused and fix the comment on line 3.
findings.groupTitle: Chromium-only isInputPending gate: navigator read at load, unsliced re-queue, false header
findings.note: Landed on release/1.6.0 as 05563b6 (cherry-pick of 1.6/search 2475593). The isInputPending/scheduler.yield gate and core/es2026.d.ts are deleted rather than reworded: flush() applies every pending update synchronously and in order (proved on a Chromium-shaped environment with input pending); CE-97's header line and CE-77's load-time navigator read no longer exist, so both close by deletion and the matrix cites the flush test for CE-77.

findings.claim: Every literal data-attrs rewrites is reprinted double-quoted, because recast's StringLiteral printer ignores extra.raw and defaults to double quotes. Single-quote codebases get churned lines and escaped inner quotes.
findings.fix: Detect the original quote from the first rewritten literal, q = path.node.extra?.raw?.[0], and return root.toSource({ quote: q === "'" ? 'single' : 'double' }). Do not use 'auto', which ties to double. Apply the same change in all four transforms.
findings.groupTitle: Rewritten literals and import sources are reprinted double-quoted

findings.claim: Callee detection checks only the name 'forwardRef'. Cleanup counts usages of 'forwardRef' but removes a specifier matched by imported.name, so an aliased import whose local is still called is deleted, and fr() calls are never unwrapped.
findings.fix: Collect the local names of 'react' forwardRef specifiers and treat each, plus React.forwardRef, as a callee. In cleanup, count Identifier usages of each specifier's local.name (excluding the specifier) and remove only specifiers whose local is unused.
findings.groupTitle: Aliased and namespace forwardRef imports are not detected, and cleanup deletes a used alias

findings.claim: Rewritten import, export, dynamic-import and require specifiers are reprinted with double quotes, whatever the file's quote style.
findings.fix: Read the original quote from path.node.source.extra?.raw?.[0] and return root.toSource({ quote: q === "'" ? 'single' : 'double' }). Use the same helper as data-attrs and should-filter.
findings.groupTitle: Rewritten literals and import sources are reprinted double-quoted

findings.claim: scoreWordBoundary returns exactly 0.7 for every hit, so word-boundary matches cannot be ranked against each other by quality.
findings.fix: Replace the ratio with a contiguity and coverage score that stays in [0.3, 0.7]: let c = sum(matchLen^2) / qLen^2; return 0.3 + 0.25*c + 0.15*(qLen/tLen). Delete totalWeightedLen and maxPossible.
findings.groupTitle: scoreWordBoundary gives a flat 0.7 and never backtracks
findings.note: Landed as cea3cfd (cherry-pick of 2ee5ca5). The constants differ from the row's proposal: 0.65 + 0.03*contiguity + 0.02*coverage keeps every word-boundary score in (0.65, 0.7), above the fuzzy tier, as the spec's tier order requires (the proposed 0.3 + 0.25c + 0.15r would rank 'Gas' above 'Git: Stage All Changes' for 'gs'); the cover backtracks, failed covers are cached by smallest failing start per query index, and queries over 512 characters fall to the fuzzy tier (changeset note). Brute-force cross-check of about 62M query/target pairs by the cluster's verifier: 0 mismatches.

findings.claim: The greedy contiguous consumption at each word start never backtracks, so valid word-boundary matches are missed and fall through to the lower fuzzy score.
findings.fix: Make scoreWordBoundary recursive over (queryIdx, i). At each word start whose char equals query[queryIdx], try the longest contiguous run first, then shorter runs down to 1, and return the first full cover. Memoize failures on (queryIdx, wordStart).
findings.groupTitle: scoreWordBoundary gives a flat 0.7 and never backtracks
findings.note: Landed as cea3cfd (cherry-pick of 2ee5ca5). The constants differ from the row's proposal: 0.65 + 0.03*contiguity + 0.02*coverage keeps every word-boundary score in (0.65, 0.7), above the fuzzy tier, as the spec's tier order requires (the proposed 0.3 + 0.25c + 0.15r would rank 'Gas' above 'Git: Stage All Changes' for 'gs'); the cover backtracks, failed covers are cached by smallest failing start per query index, and queries over 512 characters fall to the fuzzy tier (changeset note). Brute-force cross-check of about 62M query/target pairs by the cluster's verifier: 0 mismatches.

findings.claim: Query-append pruning also runs for custom scorers, including the options.filter adapter. Any non-monotonic scorer loses valid items once the query is extended.
findings.fix: const isIncremental = useDefaultScorer && previousQuery.length > 0 && query.startsWith(previousQuery);
findings.groupTitle: Query-append pruning runs for custom scorers and misses case-only extensions
findings.note: Landed as 3a8b472 (cherry-pick of 583997a). Incremental pruning runs only with the default scorer and compares lowercased queries; a custom scorer or filter rescans every item per keystroke (restores the ARCHITECTURE.md Plug Points filter row; changeset note under LD-05). The case-folding corner it also fixes is CE-105, pending its own test.

findings.claim: In Vite or webpack 5 browser dev, globalThis.process is undefined, so __DEV__ is always false there and the leak registry never runs. dist/core and dist/react keep the guard verbatim.
findings.fix: Use the bare idiom React uses, const __DEV__ = process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production', with a `declare const process: { env: { NODE_ENV?: string } }`. Do not use a typeof-process or globalThis.process guard.
findings.groupTitle: __DEV__ guard on globalThis.process is always false in browser dev

findings.claim: Match ranges index the lowered string. When toLowerCase changes length (U+0130), Command.Highlight marks shifted characters in the original text.
findings.fix: In index() and scoreItem, when lower.length !== value.length, map the ranges back to original offsets through a per-code-point offset table built while lowering, or return matches: [] for that item.
findings.groupTitle: Match ranges index the lowered string and shift when lowering changes length

findings.claim: No shortcut string can bind the '+' key: 'Ctrl++' parses to an empty key, and 'Plus' is not aliased to '+'.
findings.fix: Split with safeShortcut.split(/\+(?!$)/) so a trailing '+' is the key, and map the part 'plus' to '+'. Note in the docs that '+' usually needs Shift, because the matcher checks shiftKey exactly.
findings.groupTitle: No shortcut string can bind the '+' key

findings.claim: Default :root tokens are dark-only but declare color-scheme: light dark. With no data-theme set, a light-OS user gets light UA scrollbars, form controls and theme-color (#fafafa) over a dark page.
findings.fix: In :root set color-scheme: dark (the [data-theme=light] block already sets light). Make index.html meta color-scheme content="dark" and a single theme-color #0a0e1a, or move the tokens to light-dark() driven by color-scheme.
findings.groupTitle: Theme bootstrap disagrees with itself: dark-only tokens versus 'light dark' color-scheme, mismatched theme-color metas, toggle ignores OS and storage

findings.claim: ThemeToggle always starts at 'dark' because dataset.theme is never set. It ignores prefers-color-scheme and loses the choice on reload.
findings.fix: Initialise from localStorage.getItem('theme') ?? (matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)').matches ? 'light' : 'dark'). Write dataset.theme and localStorage in toggleTheme, and set data-theme before first paint, from main.tsx or an inline head script.
findings.groupTitle: Theme bootstrap disagrees with itself: dark-only tokens versus 'light dark' color-scheme, mismatched theme-color metas, toggle ignores OS and storage

findings.claim: DialogDemo's Ctrl/Cmd+K handler toggles on every auto-repeat keydown, so a held chord flickers the dialog. With Caps Lock on, e.key is 'K' and the shortcut misses.
findings.fix: if (e.key.toLowerCase() === 'k' && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && !e.shiftKey && !e.altKey && !e.repeat && !e.isComposing) { e.preventDefault(); setOpen(p => !p); }
findings.groupTitle: DialogDemo Ctrl/Cmd+K toggles on auto-repeat and misses with Caps Lock

findings.claim: navigate() pushes a duplicate history entry when the current route's tab is clicked again.
findings.fix: At the top of navigate add: if (globalThis.location.pathname === path) return; Reading location keeps the callback's empty deps; comparing with route would need [route] in deps.
findings.groupTitle: Hand-rolled pushState button router: not links, duplicate history entries, no title or focus cue on route change

findings.claim: The 'System Default' theme item has no onSelect, so selecting it has no effect.
findings.fix: Add onSelect={() => setDark(matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches)} to the value="system" item, or remove the item.
findings.groupTitle: DarkModeDemo 'System Default' item has no onSelect

findings.claim: The RTL placeholder puts the ellipsis at the logical start, so in the dir=rtl input it renders before the word (on the right) instead of trailing it.
findings.fix: placeholder="بحث…" (or '...' after the word), so the ellipsis is logically last and renders on the left in RTL.
findings.groupTitle: RTL placeholder ellipsis sits at the logical start

findings.claim: One Escape fires onOpenChange(false) at least twice: once via Radix and once via the document handler. In controlled mode a third fires, because the controlledOpen sync effect re-sends CLOSE and core CLOSE emits unconditionally.
findings.fix: In machine.ts OPEN/CLOSE (and setOpen paths), return early when state.open already equals the target. In createKeydownHandler, skip Escape if event.defaultPrevented.
findings.groupTitle: Dialog open state: duplicate onOpenChange and controlled open not honoured

findings.claim: Dialog.Root follows machine state, so a controlled parent that keeps open=true still sees the dialog close, and the two stay out of sync.
findings.fix: Use const open = controlledOpen ?? state.open for Root, data-state and the keydown effect. When controlled, handleRadixOpenChange only calls onOpenChangeRef (no send). The machine's onOpenChange forwards only when uncontrolled.
findings.groupTitle: Dialog open state: duplicate onOpenChange and controlled open not honoured

findings.claim: useCommandState(s => ({ q: s.search })) or any selector that returns a fresh object or array makes getSnapshot unstable. React warns and re-renders until it hits 'Maximum update depth exceeded'.
findings.fix: Keep refs for lastState and lastResult. In getSnapshot, s = machine.getState(); if s === lastState return lastResult; else compute next and keep lastResult when (isEqual ?? Object.is)(lastResult, next). Add an optional isEqual parameter.
findings.groupTitle: useCommandState with a fresh-object selector loops to max update depth

findings.claim: After machine dispose, schedule() still queues an rAF or microtask, so send() runs handleEvent on cleared registries. This happens in the StrictMode effect double-invoke.
findings.fix: Add `let disposed = false` to createScheduler, set it in [Symbol.dispose], and return early from schedule() and flush(). StrictMode separately needs the machine re-created after dispose.
findings.groupTitle: Scheduler keeps queuing work after machine dispose
findings.note: The dispose guard was tried in ccbdda4 and reverted in 884b6c0: under React StrictMode it emptied the palette (0 options, 33 of 45 e2e tests failed) because the machine is reused after the first dispose. Stays OPEN with RA-03 (re-create the machine after dispose); what landed is a counter reset in dispose ('events dropped by dispose do not stall the batches of a machine that is used again'). Moved to 1.7.0.

findings.claim: The cmd-action snippet never calls dispatch and never renders state, so isPending is always false and Command.Loading never shows.
findings.fix: Type the action as (_prev, query: string). On Command.Input set onValueChange={(q) => startTransition(() => dispatch(q))} (prop exists, input.tsx:14), import startTransition, and render state as Command.Items.
findings.groupTitle: React 19 action snippets are inert: cmd-action never calls dispatch, and cmd-optimistic never calls addOptimistic

findings.claim: The cmd-optimistic snippet destructures addOptimistic but never calls it, so the optimistic update path is never exercised.
findings.fix: Add a Command.Item whose onSelect runs startTransition(async () => { addOptimistic(newItem); await ${persist}(newItem); }), and import startTransition from react.
findings.groupTitle: React 19 action snippets are inert: cmd-action never calls dispatch, and cmd-optimistic never calls addOptimistic

findings.claim: find_match_ranges returns UTF-8 byte offsets of the lowercased value, so highlights drift on non-ASCII. Its 1-byte advance panics (WASM trap) on repeated multibyte matches. Typo matches get no ranges.
findings.fix: Advance start by the first matched char's len_utf8(), or use match_indices. Convert byte offsets to UTF-16 offsets of the original value (sum len_utf16 over char_indices). Add non-ASCII Rust tests.
findings.groupTitle: find_match_ranges returns byte offsets and traps on repeated multibyte matches

findings.claim: The leak flag reads globalThis.process, which bundlers do not replace. It is off in browser dev and on in dev SSR, where machines are never disposed, so it warns spuriously.
findings.fix: Use bare `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'` (React's pattern) with no typeof-process guard, which would disable it in the browser. Check dist keeps it unreplaced, and skip register() when typeof window === 'undefined'.
findings.groupTitle: Dev-only gates read an undefined __DEV__ or globalThis.process, so devtools throw and the leak flag misfires

findings.claim: transform-origin: inline-start center is invalid and dropped, so the scroll indicator grows from center. page-enter slides along physical X with no RTL flip, so the 'full RTL' header claim is overstated.
findings.fix: Use transform-origin: left center plus :dir(rtl) { transform-origin: right center }. In page-enter, multiply the translate by a --dir var (-1 under :dir(rtl)). Soften the header comment.
findings.groupTitle: Invalid transform-origin and page-enter animation with no RTL flip

findings.claim: The ResizeObserver binds once to innerRef at mount. innerRef exists only in non-virtual mode, so --command-list-height freezes after a virtualization toggle or a virtual-first mount.
findings.fix: Use a callback ref that observes the new node and returns () => observer.disconnect() (React 19 ref cleanup), or observe a wrapper that always renders.
findings.groupTitle: list.tsx ResizeObserver binds once to innerRef, so --command-list-height freezes after a virtualization toggle

findings.claim: CommandHighlight neither merges nor clamps ranges. Overlapping or nested ranges (which the WASM engine emits) duplicate text, and duplicate ranges collide on React keys.
findings.fix: After sorting, skip a range when end <= lastEnd, set start = max(start, lastEnd), clamp to [0, text.length], and set lastEnd = Math.max(lastEnd, end). Add overlap, nested, duplicate and out-of-bounds tests.
findings.groupTitle: CommandHighlight neither merges nor clamps overlapping or duplicate ranges

findings.claim: Symbol.asyncDispose never sends the dispose message, because disposed is set first and postAndWait rejects at once. The worker would not reply to it anyway.
findings.fix: Mirror the sync dispose: if (!disposed) { disposed = true; worker.postMessage({ type: 'dispose' }); worker.terminate(); }. Reject any pending request, and drop the await and the try/catch.
findings.groupTitle: Symbol.asyncDispose never sends dispose

findings.claim: The public batchScoreItems and scoreItemAsync (core/index.ts:15) have no tests, and no test pins exact multi-range fuzzy matches.
findings.fix: In search.test.ts: expect(scoreItem('aon',makeItem('Application'))?.matches).toEqual([[0,1],[9,11]]); await batchScoreItems sorted desc, nulls dropped; await scoreItemAsync equals scoreItem result.
findings.groupTitle: batchScoreItems and scoreItemAsync untested and no exact multi-range match test

Brute-force cross-check of about 62M query/target pairs by the cluster's verifier: 0 mismatches.

findings.claim: The loading:false check is vacuous because loading is never true. ITEMS_LOADED (machine.ts:305-311) skips keyboardRegistry.register, so core-only async items with shortcut+onSelect get no binding.
findings.fix: In ITEMS_LOADED, loop event.items and register shortcut+onSelect the way REGISTER_ITEM does; test getKeyboardRegistry().getBindings().size after load. Drop the loading assertion or add a loading:true transition.
findings.groupTitle: ITEMS_LOADED skips keyboardRegistry.register, so async core items get no shortcut binding

findings.claim: The shortcut test checks only bindings.size. No unit test proves the global keydown listener calls an item's onSelect.
findings.fix: After the size check: document.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown',{key:'c',ctrlKey:true,bubbles:true})); expect(handler).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); make the test sync.
findings.groupTitle: No unit test proves a keydown reaches KeyboardShortcutRegistry handlers or an item's onSelect; 'Ctrl++' parses to an empty key

findings.claim: The auto-dispose test cannot tell whether the using scope ever called dispose.
findings.fix: After the block: expect(machineRef?.getRegistry().size).toBe(0); optionally expect(machineRef?.getKeyboardRegistry().getBindings().size).toBe(0).
findings.groupTitle: Dispose tests cannot tell that dispose ran, and events sent after dispose are still processed

findings.claim: The batching test does not prove that several updates coalesce into one frame request.
findings.fix: Before scheduling, const raf=vi.spyOn(globalThis,'requestAnimationFrame'); after waitFor, expect(raf).toHaveBeenCalledOnce(); raf.mockRestore().

findings.claim: Only the snapshot gap remains. No test covers a listener that adds or removes listeners during emit.
findings.fix: Add a test: h1 disposes h2's sub and adds h3 inside emit; first emit calls h1 and h2 but not h3; second emit calls h1 and h3 but not h2.
findings.groupTitle: No test covers listeners added or removed during emit (snapshot semantics)
findings.note: Landed as 6a8cfa6 (26ae4a5). Test 'TUB-42: emit iterates a snapshot, so a listener removed or added during emit takes effect on the next emit'. Red: iterating the live set gave 1 failed of 15.

findings.claim: Nothing tests exact bucket boundaries at 1/24/168/720h, or the default weights used when a partial decay config omits a bucket.
findings.fix: it.for([[1,2],[24,1.5],[168,1],[720,0.5]]) with lastUsed=now-h*3_600_000 and expect bonus; and computeFrecencyBonus(12h record,now,{hourWeight:10}) toBe(DEFAULT_FRECENCY_DECAY.dayWeight).

findings.note: Exact recency bucket boundaries at 1/24/168/720 h ('TUB-45: at $hours h a record 1 ms younger gets $below and exactly $hours h or older gets $above', templated; red with a boundary < changed to <=: 1 of 26) and the default weights of a partial decay config ('TUB-45: a partial decay config falls back to the default weight of every bucket it omits', 'TUB-45: a config that sets only %s changes only the bucket at %d h'; red with the weekWeight default changed: 5 of 26).

findings.claim: Each file gets a new API object, and withParser (which runs enrichCore, Object.assign of every type and builder) runs twice per file, though only two parsers (ts, tsx) exist.
findings.fix: Before the batch loop, build const apis = { ts: mk('ts'), tsx: mk('tsx') } where mk creates core = jscodeshift.withParser(p) once and returns { jscodeshift: core, j: core, stats, report }. Pass (p) => apis[p] to processFile.
findings.groupTitle: Batch runner is single-core, re-creates the API per file, and carries no-op async scaffolding

findings.claim: import-rewrite fully parses every globbed file even when it never mentions 'cmdk'. The other three transforms bail early.
findings.fix: Put `if (!fileInfo.source.includes(OLD_PACKAGE)) return fileInfo.source;` first in transform(), before j(fileInfo.source).
findings.groupTitle: import-rewrite parses every file, even ones that never mention cmdk

findings.claim: Every KeyboardShortcutRegistry attaches a document keydown listener in its constructor, even with zero bindings.
findings.fix: Attach in register() when #bindings goes from 0 to 1 (if no listener yet). Detach in unregister, unregisterByItem and the per-binding dispose when #bindings.size reaches 0. Keep the detach in [Symbol.dispose].
findings.groupTitle: Every KeyboardShortcutRegistry attaches a document listener even with zero bindings

findings.claim: __DEV__ reads globalThis.process, which bundlers do not replace. It is false in browser dev, true in Node without NODE_ENV, and the leak registry code ships to production. use-devtools relies on an undefined global __DEV__.
findings.fix: In packages/modern-cmdk/tsdown.config.ts, add define: { __DEV__: 'process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"' } to the core and react entries, as command-search-wasm does. In search/index.ts, replace the const with `declare const __DEV__: boolean;`.
findings.groupTitle: __DEV__ reads globalThis.process: false in browser dev, leak registry ships to prod, free __DEV__ in dist/react

findings.claim: unregisterItem is O(n), and each UNREGISTER_ITEM also triggers a full refilter, so unmounting n items is O(n^2), mostly from refilter.
findings.fix: Do not swap-remove, because order must be kept. In use-register, coalesce unmount unregisters per microtask into one UNREGISTER_ITEMS event that calls registry.unregisterItems(set), searchEngine.remove(set), keyboard unregisters, and one refilter.
findings.groupTitle: Each REGISTER_ITEM/UNREGISTER_ITEM re-indexes and runs a full refilter and emit, so mount and unmount are O(n^2) (10K mount ~9.9 s)
findings.note: registration.bench.ts (29976c4) evidence: unregister per item grows 1.24x–1.82x (1.79x–2.13x with shortcuts) from 1K to 10K, consistent with O(1) per unregister.

findings.claim: The handler never checks shiftKey/ctrlKey/altKey/metaKey, so Shift+Home and Shift+End in Command.Input call preventDefault and NAVIGATE. The user cannot select query text to the start or end. Unmodified Home/End behaves as documented.
findings.fix: In createKeydownHandler, before the NAVIGATION_KEYS lookup, return early with no preventDefault when key is Home or End and any of event.shiftKey, ctrlKey, altKey or metaKey is set.
findings.groupTitle: Shift/Ctrl+Home/End are swallowed, blocking text selection

findings.claim: An inline Command (open defaults to false, types.ts:210) still cancels Escape. Inside a dialog opened with showModal(), or a [popover], pressing Escape in the input does not close the container, and onOpenChange(false) fires for no reason.
findings.fix: In the Escape case, break when !state.open, without preventDefault or CLOSE. Alternatively, give createKeydownHandler an option such as { handleEscape } that only CommandDialog enables.
findings.groupTitle: Inline Command cancels Escape and fires onOpenChange(false)

findings.claim: If useRegisterItem/Command.Item receives new data while value, keywords, groupId, disabled and shortcut stay the same, the machine keeps the old data. A custom filter that reads item.data then filters on stale values.
findings.fix: Build the item with a getter, `get data() { return dataRef.current; }`, in place of `data: dataRef.current`. That keeps inline objects from re-registering while filters read live data. Engines that snapshot data at index() time still need a re-index.
findings.groupTitle: useRegisterItem keeps stale item.data when only data changes

findings.claim: A consumer who uses useVirtualizer with measureElement on variable-height rows gets stale sizes after a filter: index i keeps the height of the item that used to be at i. key=index reuses the DOM node, so the stable ref callback never re-measures.
findings.fix: Add an optional getItemKey(index) option (default: the index) and key measuredSizes and VirtualItem.key by it. Also clear measuredSizes when count or getItemKey changes, and add measureVersion to the virtualItems useMemo deps.
findings.groupTitle: useVirtualizer keys measured sizes by index, so they go stale after a filter

findings.claim: When virtualization turns on, the first committed frame has virtualItems = [], so every item vanishes for one painted frame until the ResizeObserver callback sets containerHeight.
findings.fix: In use-virtualizer, seed the height in a useLayoutEffect keyed on [scrollElement, enabled]: setContainerHeight(scrollElement.clientHeight) before observer.observe(), and move the RO/scroll setup into that layout effect.
findings.groupTitle: First virtual frame paints with no items until the ResizeObserver fires

findings.claim: <Command.List id="x"> replaces the listbox id, so the input's aria-controls={stable.listId} points at nothing. A consumer role or aria-label likewise overrides the ARIA wiring; Input and Item have the same pattern.
findings.fix: In list.tsx, input.tsx and item.tsx, put {...props} before the library-owned attributes. Also Omit 'id' | 'role' from CommandListProps, plus 'id' and the aria-controls/activedescendant keys from CommandInputProps.
findings.groupTitle: Consumer id/role/aria props override List and Input ARIA wiring

findings.claim: CommandHighlight duplicates text when ranges overlap, for example WASM engine matches for a self-overlapping query. Ranges past text.length do not duplicate text.
findings.fix: After toSorted in highlight.tsx, clamp each range to [0, text.length]. Skip a range when end <= lastEnd, and render a range that starts before lastEnd from lastEnd. Separately, advance start by needle.len() in trigram.rs find_match_ranges.
findings.groupTitle: CommandHighlight duplicates text on overlapping ranges

findings.claim: Command.Separator renders while a search is active, so filtered-out groups leave stray or doubled dividers. cmdk hides separators while the search is non-empty unless alwaysRender is set.
findings.fix: Add an alwaysRender?: boolean prop. Read the search from useStateContext('Command.Separator') and return null when state.search !== '' && !alwaysRender. Document the prop in apps/docs/api/command-react.md.
findings.groupTitle: Command.Separator renders during search, leaving stray dividers

findings.claim: Once CommandErrorBoundary catches an error, it shows the fallback until the parent remounts it with a new key. A function fallback has no reset callback, so a transient failure cannot be retried from the fallback.
findings.fix: Change the fallback type to (error, reset) => ReactNode, where reset = () => this.setState(INITIAL_STATE). Accept resetKeys?: readonly unknown[] and call reset in componentDidUpdate when any key changes (Object.is). Update the docs table.
findings.groupTitle: CommandErrorBoundary cannot reset or retry

findings.claim: Scaffolded apps render the palette without the default stylesheet. Adding only the import would fail tsc (TS2882), because the generated tsconfig declares no CSS module types.
findings.fix: In mainTsx add import 'modern-cmdk/styles.css'; after the react-dom import. In the generated tsconfig compilerOptions add types: ['vite/client'].
findings.groupTitle: Scaffolded apps omit modern-cmdk/styles.css, and the generated tsconfig lacks vite/client types for the CSS import

findings.claim: create-modern-cmdk inherits lib DOM from tsconfig.base.json, so DOM globals type-check in a Node-only bin.
findings.fix: Add lib: ['ESNext'] to compilerOptions in packages/create-modern-cmdk/tsconfig.json and keep types ['node']. Leave module/moduleResolution as inherited.
findings.groupTitle: Node-only create bin inherits lib DOM from the base tsconfig

findings.claim: The framework-agnostic cmd-machine snippet is unavailable in .ts and .js files, because every snippet is contributed only to the React languages.
findings.fix: Move cmd-machine into src/snippets-core.json. Contribute that file to typescript, javascript, typescriptreact and javascriptreact, and keep the rest in snippets.json for the React languages only.
findings.groupTitle: Framework-agnostic cmd-machine snippet is contributed only to the React languages, not to .ts/.js

findings.claim: createScheduler uses scheduler.yield only behind navigator.scheduling.isInputPending. Large batches never yield where yield exists without isInputPending, and they defer wholesale while input stays pending.
findings.fix: Drop isInputPending. Run the batch in chunks of about 10 updates and await globalThis.scheduler.yield() between chunks when it exists, otherwise use setTimeout(0). Keep the rAF/microtask entry. Update api/command.md:421 and es2026.d.ts.
findings.groupTitle: Scheduler yields only behind the Chromium-only isInputPending
findings.note: Landed on release/1.6.0 as 05563b6 (cherry-pick of 1.6/search 2475593). The isInputPending/scheduler.yield gate and core/es2026.d.ts are deleted rather than reworded: flush() applies every pending update synchronously and in order (proved on a Chromium-shaped environment with input pending); CE-97's header line and CE-77's load-time navigator read no longer exist, so both close by deletion and the matrix cites the flush test for CE-77.

findings.claim: The defect is in the library, not the docs. group-by.ts keeps mapGroupBy/objectGroupBy 'for cross-browser compat' even though Map.groupBy and Object.groupBy are Baseline widely.

findings.groupTitle: A hand-written mapGroupBy helper and the docs text describing it, where native Map.groupBy exists

findings.claim: detectConflicts groups through the hand-written mapGroupBy helper instead of the Baseline-widely Map.groupBy, and the docs describe the helper.
findings.fix: In matcher.ts use Map.groupBy(shortcuts, (s) => s.normalized), drop the import, and fix the comments at L2 and L33-34. Reword shortcuts.md:8 and :92 to say native Map.groupBy.
findings.groupTitle: A hand-written mapGroupBy helper and the docs text describing it, where native Map.groupBy exists

findings.claim: Index serialisation maps readonly arrays through iterator helpers (values().map().toArray()); Array.prototype.map is about 2.4x faster here and is the direct primitive for array-to-array.

findings.groupTitle: Index serialisation and result mapping use iterator helpers where Array.prototype.map is the direct primitive

findings.claim: The audit job now fails on high advisories. But CI has no schedule, so an advisory published between pushes shows up only on the next push or PR. The summary gate also ignores security.result.
findings.fix: Add 'schedule: - cron: "0 6 * * 1"' under on: in ci.yml (or a separate audit workflow). Add needs.security.result == 'failure' to the 'Fail if critical jobs failed' condition.
findings.groupTitle: CI Summary gate ignores security.result, and the audit has no schedule, so new advisories surface only on the next push

findings.claim: Render-time ref writes break Rules of React. If a concurrent render is discarded, dialog's onOpenChangeRef and use-register's onSelectRef keep callbacks from props that never committed, and the machine calls the stale ones.
findings.fix: Assign latest-value refs in useLayoutEffect, not in render. list: replace externalRefRef with useCallback(...,[ref]) and return a React 19 ref cleanup. use-command-state: drop selectorRef, useCallback deps [machine, selector]. No useEffectEvent (peer 19.0).
findings.groupTitle: Latest-value refs written during render keep uncommitted callbacks

findings.groupTitle: .sr-only uses the deprecated clip property

findings.claim: apps/docs/examples/vanilla.md:14 labels execCommand('insertText') with no value as 'Paste'. Selecting it inserts an empty string, so it deletes the selection instead of pasting. Line 15 uses execCommand('cut'), which is deprecated.
findings.fix: vanilla.md Paste: onSelect: async () => input.setRangeText(await navigator.clipboard.readText(), input.selectionStart ?? 0, input.selectionEnd ?? 0, 'end'). Cut: navigator.clipboard.writeText(selected text), then setRangeText(''). Leave the plan.

findings.remaining: Closed by DG-102 (W7-04, 37f89c9): execCommand appears only in a comment marking it deprecated. Recorded by the final review (wf_48132ab1-176).

findings.claim: The replaceInString JSDoc says it uses Set.union in a single pass. The code runs sequential replaceAll calls over two Map iterators, and the comments mislabel iterator helpers as ES2026.

findings.groupTitle: replaceInString matches only the exact [attr] form through sequential replaceAll passes

findings.claim: Docs table describes helper code that is below the real browser floor. The same table also claims RegExp.escape in the shortcut parser and Promise.withResolvers in scheduler flush; neither exists in core src (grep).

findings.groupTitle: The overview helper table describes below-floor helpers and has phantom RegExp.escape and withResolvers rows

findings.claim: scheduler.ts gates yielding on Chromium-only navigator.scheduling.isInputPending, so scheduler.yield never runs elsewhere. Under sustained input it re-queues the whole batch, which can defer updates indefinitely.
findings.fix: Drop isInputPending. For batches over N, run updates in chunks and await scheduler.yield() between chunks (fallback: rAF or setTimeout 0), never re-queueing finished work. Then delete core/es2026.d.ts.
findings.groupTitle: The scheduler gates yielding on Chromium-only isInputPending and re-queues whole batches under sustained input
findings.note: Landed on release/1.6.0 as 05563b6 (cherry-pick of 1.6/search 2475593). The isInputPending/scheduler.yield gate and core/es2026.d.ts are deleted rather than reworded: flush() applies every pending update synchronously and in order (proved on a Chromium-shaped environment with input pending); CE-97's header line and CE-77's load-time navigator read no longer exist, so both close by deletion and the matrix cites the flush test for CE-77.

findings.claim: .sr-only hides content with the deprecated clip property.
findings.fix: Replace clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0) with clip-path: inset(50%). Keep the other declarations.
findings.groupTitle: .sr-only uses the deprecated clip property

findings.claim: Internal polyfills duplicate Map/Object.groupBy (Baseline widely), String.toWellFormed (widely) and Set methods (newly 2024-06). The shipped Iterator-helper floor (Safari 18.4) already exceeds all three. Source is 4.4 KB raw.
findings.fix: Use Map.groupBy, Object.groupBy, str.toWellFormed() and the native Set methods (registry.ts and search/index.ts). Delete the three util files and their comments. Ship as a patch or minor; document the floor in the install guide.
findings.groupTitle: Internal groupBy, toWellFormed and Set-method polyfills duplicate natives that are below the shipped Safari 18.4 floor

findings.claim: The codemod CLI has a dead deferred promise and a needless async generator, and uses the objectGroupBy polyfill in a Node-only bin. Its report loops (lines 184-193) are empty, so no results are printed.
findings.fix: Remove resolveDone/done and use allResults directly; no withResolvers is needed. Make chunked a sync generator and use for...of. Use Object.groupBy. Restore console output in the report loops.
findings.groupTitle: Codemod CLI has a dead deferred promise, a needless async generator, an objectGroupBy polyfill and empty report loops

findings.claim: CodeQL scans only JS/TS, so the workflow files go unscanned. It runs a pointless autobuild for an interpreted language and leaves a false-positive alert open.
findings.fix: Add actions to the matrix, with build-mode: none. Drop the autobuild step. Add rust only after confirming codeql-action v4.39.1 supports it. Dismiss alert #1 as a false positive (dedicated worker) with a written justification.
findings.groupTitle: CodeQL skips workflow files, runs a pointless autobuild, and leaves a false-positive alert open

findings.claim: Open/close durations use the wall clock, which goes wrong if the clock jumps. The onSearch startTime clock is undocumented. The example sends the raw query to analytics.
findings.fix: Use performance.now() for openTimestamp and close. For onSearch, document startTime as performance.now() and ship that as a minor with a changeset, or keep Date.now() there. Change the example to omit or redact the query.
findings.groupTitle: Telemetry durations use Date.now, and the example sends the raw query

findings.claim: Two codemod tests wrap their case lists in single-bucket Object.groupBy plus ?? [] for-loops. A mistyped key silently drops every case. The comments call groupBy ES2026; it is ES2024.
findings.fix: In codemod-data-attrs and codemod-import-rewrite, use it.for(cases)('renames $attr', ({attr, expected}) => ...) on plain arrays. keyboard.test may keep its categories, or use describe.for per category.
findings.groupTitle: Codemod tests wrap cases in single-bucket Object.groupBy (silent drop; mislabelled ES2026)

findings.claim: The groupBy tables are indexed by unchecked string keys, so a category typo silently drops tests. `expected` is a loose Record rather than ParsedShortcut-shaped.
findings.fix: Use one named const array per category, `satisfies readonly { shortcut: string; expected: Partial<ParsedShortcut> }[]`. Replace each for/it loop with `it.for(cases)('... "$shortcut"', ({ shortcut, expected }) => ...)`.
findings.groupTitle: Single-key Object.groupBy test tables let a category typo turn suites into zero passing tests

findings.claim: A single-category Object.groupBy plus string-key lookup adds nothing, and a typo turns the 8 rename tests into zero tests that pass.
findings.fix: Make attrRenameCases a plain array of { attr, expected }. Use `it.for(attrRenameCases)('renames $attr to $expected', ({ attr, expected }) => ...)` and drop the category field. Apply the same change in codemod-import-rewrite.test.ts.
findings.groupTitle: Single-key Object.groupBy test tables let a category typo turn suites into zero passing tests

findings.claim: The set-ops.ts and group-by.ts helpers are below the browser floor the dist already requires, so they are dead compat weight.
findings.fix: Swap setX(a,b) for native a.x(b) in registry.ts and search/index.ts. Swap mapGroupBy and objectGroupBy for Map.groupBy and Object.groupBy in registry.ts, machine.ts, keyboard/matcher.ts and codemod/cli.ts. Delete both helper files.
findings.groupTitle: set-ops.ts and group-by.ts helpers sit below the browser floor and are dead compat weight

findings.claim: Items with tied scores come out in HashMap iteration order. For example, two items that both match all query trigrams can rank in either order, which makes the ranking nondeterministic.
findings.fix: Collect `Vec<(usize, f64)>` from scores and filter score > 0.1. Sort with `sort_unstable_by(|a, b| b.1.total_cmp(&a.1).then(a.0.cmp(&b.0)))`, then truncate(max_results), and only then build SearchResult and call find_match_ranges.
findings.groupTitle: Tied scores come out in HashMap order, not registration order

findings.claim: search returns `any`, so the result shape is asserted twice by hand. A field rename on the Rust side compiles cleanly and yields undefined at runtime.
findings.fix: Declare `interface WasmSearchResult { id: string; score: number; matches: [number, number][] }` in a typescript_custom_section. Put `#[wasm_bindgen(unchecked_return_type = "WasmSearchResult[]")]` on search, rebuild pkg, and delete both casts.
findings.groupTitle: wasm-bindgen search returns any, so the result shape is cast by hand twice

findings.groupTitle: Bench scripts need tsx only because they import './setup.js'; spec mis-states the strip-types flag

findings.fix: Delete hasInputPending, the early-return block at L39-50 and the es2026.d.ts Navigator.scheduling declaration. For chunking, run fixed slices and await scheduler.yield() (rAF fallback) between them. flush() must stay synchronous.
findings.groupTitle: executeBatch re-queues on isInputPending, so flush() runs nothing and events starve during fast typing
findings.note: Landed on release/1.6.0 as 05563b6 (cherry-pick of 1.6/search 2475593). The isInputPending/scheduler.yield gate and core/es2026.d.ts are deleted rather than reworded: flush() applies every pending update synchronously and in order (proved on a Chromium-shaped environment with input pending); CE-97's header line and CE-77's load-time navigator read no longer exist, so both close by deletion and the matrix cites the flush test for CE-77.

findings.claim: The core example never logs because `using machine` disposes the machine at scope end, before the batched sends run. The order of subscribe and send does not matter.
findings.fix: Use `const machine = createCommandMachine(...)`, subscribe, then send. Note that send() is batched to the next frame/microtask, and call machine[Symbol.dispose]() on teardown. Or keep `using` in an async scope that awaits a frame before exit.
findings.groupTitle: Core example never logs because `using` disposes the machine before batched sends run
findings.note: packages/modern-cmdk/README.md names no RegExp.escape, says the later shortcut binding wins with getConflicts/getBindings (core/keyboard/index.ts:21-22, :89-107), runs its core sample as const, subscribe, send and teardown, and says createTelemetryMiddleware returns hooks the caller invokes (core/telemetry.ts; no telemetry option in core/types.ts); follow-ups 6880ab2 and e1c6229, the same telemetry wording in the api page (27a9475), CONTRIBUTING (fe25b20) and ARCHITECTURE (8131bba).

findings.claim: Docs and comments call frecency 'exponential decay', but the weights are a per-bucket step function.
findings.fix: Replace 'exponential decay' with 'bucketed recency weights (hour/day/week/month/older)' at all six sites. Reword the L46 comment to '// Step weight by recency bucket'.
findings.groupTitle: Frecency described as 'exponential decay' but is a bucketed step function

findings.claim: The scorer header says items are validated at itemId(), but only ids are. Value and keywords are scored unvalidated, and the header names a stale path.

findings.note: default-scorer.ts header: 'value/keywords scored as raw UTF-16; no isWellFormed() checks on the hot path (only ids are normalized by itemId())', the 'inline iteration' and 'zero unnecessary allocations' claims dropped; idb-storage.ts header names no idb-keyval version (openStore's JSDoc says 6.3.0, matching node_modules), states that the reader validates rows and accepts v1 and v2 payloads, names the registered-symbol shim, and names serializeData/deserializeData as the Iterator Helpers users. tests/setup.ts polyfills only Math.sumPrecise, as the scorer header says.

findings.claim: With the default scorer, typing 'ab' then 'Ab' fails query.startsWith(previousQuery) at L92, so the engine rescans all n items when it could have rescored only the previous matches. Results are correct; only work is wasted.
findings.fix: Store previousLowerQuery next to previousQuery. When useDefaultScorer is true, test lowerQuery.startsWith(previousLowerQuery); keep the raw case-sensitive test for custom scorers. Reset both wherever previousQuery is reset (L72, L78, L143).
findings.groupTitle: Query-append pruning runs for custom scorers and misses case-only extensions
findings.note: Landed as 3a8b472 (cherry-pick of 583997a). Incremental pruning runs only with the default scorer and compares lowercased queries; a custom scorer or filter rescans every item per keystroke (restores the ARCHITECTURE.md Plug Points filter row; changeset note under LD-05). The case-folding corner it also fixes is CE-105, pending its own test.

findings.claim: The header (L4, 'zero redundant allocation') and the JSDoc (L41, 'zero toLowerCase() calls during search') overstate the code: search lowers the query each call (L89) and lowers unindexed items per item (L109-110).
findings.fix: Change L4 to 'pre-cached lowercase at index time, charCode comparison'. Change L41 to 'Pre-caches lowercase at index time; indexed items are never re-lowered during search (only the query is lowered once per call).'
findings.groupTitle: False comments and headers on core frecency, scorer, search, types and emitter
findings.note: Landed as 3a8b472: the header now reads 'Performance: pre-cached lowercase at index time, charCode comparison' and the JSDoc 'Pre-caches lowercase at index time; indexed items are not re-lowered during search'; the 'zero redundant allocation' and 'zero toLowerCase() calls' phrases are gone.

findings.claim: The comment at empty.tsx:22 says Empty shows only when there is a query, but it shows whenever filteredCount is 0 and loading is false, query or not.

findings.note: The `priority` JSDoc in react/group.tsx says priority orders the `groupedIds` keys while React renders groups in JSX order (TUB-06). The docs lines (apps/docs/api/command.md:153, :162 'Sort priority (lower = higher in list)') are DOCS's.

findings.fix: Change the comment to: Both should be case-insensitive (cmdk applies a small 0.9999-per-character case-mismatch penalty, hence toBeCloseTo).

findings.groupTitle: Codemod CLI prints nothing (empty printUsage, empty report bodies, swallowed error)

findings.claim: README:26 credits SharedArrayBuffer for off-main-thread search. The Worker does that job; the optional SAB only carries the Float32 scores, and search stays off-main-thread without it.
findings.fix: Reword README:26 to: 'Off-main-thread search in a Web Worker; scores travel via SharedArrayBuffer when cross-origin isolated, otherwise via structured clone'. Fix the worker-engine.ts:3 header to match.
findings.groupTitle: README credits SharedArrayBuffer for off-main-thread search; the Worker does it, and SAB carries only scores

findings.claim: In batchScoreItems, .toArray().toSorted(cmp) copies the result array a second time. The array from toArray() is a fresh local, so sorting it in place is safe.
findings.fix: Replace .toSorted((a, b) => b.score - a.score) with .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score) on the array returned by .toArray().
findings.groupTitle: scoreItemAsync/batchScoreItems hand-roll Promise.try and copy-sort

findings.claim: The JSDoc, the docs at apps/docs/api/command.md:357 and both READMEs ('Pluggable hooks') say the hooks are 'called when the palette opens'. Nothing in the library accepts or calls the middleware, so a user who follows the docs example gets no events.
findings.fix: Add a telemetry option to createCommandMachine that calls the middleware on open, close, search and select. Or reword the header, docs and READMEs to say users call onOpen, onClose, onSearch and onSelect themselves, and drop 'zero overhead'.
findings.groupTitle: Telemetry middleware is never invoked, yet docs say hooks fire on open and measure open-to-select

findings.claim: The header line 'Uses scheduler.yield() when available for input-responsive large batches' is wrong. yield runs only on Chromium, where navigator.scheduling.isInputPending exists, and only after a batch of more than 10 updates is re-queued whole.
findings.fix: Reword L3 to: 'On Chromium, when isInputPending() reports input during a batch of more than 10 updates, re-queues the batch and resumes after scheduler.yield() (rAF fallback).' Also fix the stale path on L1 to packages/modern-cmdk/src/core/utils/scheduler.ts.
findings.groupTitle: Chromium-only isInputPending gate: navigator read at load, unsliced re-queue, false header
findings.note: Landed on release/1.6.0 as 05563b6 (cherry-pick of 1.6/search 2475593). The isInputPending/scheduler.yield gate and core/es2026.d.ts are deleted rather than reworded: flush() applies every pending update synchronously and in order (proved on a Chromium-shaped environment with input pending); CE-97's header line and CE-77's load-time navigator read no longer exist, so both close by deletion and the matrix cites the flush test for CE-77.

findings.claim: ensureWellFormed hand-rolls String.prototype.toWellFormed with a lookbehind regex. That is about 3x slower per call and duplicates a native that is Baseline widely, and the header still calls it a 'cross-browser replacement'.
findings.fix: Make the body 'return str.toWellFormed();' and delete LONE_SURROGATE_RE and REPLACEMENT_CHAR. Better still, inline str.toWellFormed() at the 4 call sites and delete string-wellformed.ts.
findings.groupTitle: Set/groupBy/wellFormed helpers duplicate Baseline natives, and comments misname them

findings.claim: The header at machine.ts:1-2 gives a nonexistent path (packages/command/src/machine.ts) and says the machine is made of 'pure functions, using for subscription cleanup'. It is a closure that mutates its own state and does not use 'using' internally.
findings.fix: Replace L1-2 with '// packages/modern-cmdk/src/core/machine.ts' and '// Core state machine: closure-held state, Disposable, useSyncExternalStore-compatible subscribe/getSnapshot', or delete both lines.
findings.groupTitle: Path headers name the nonexistent packages/command/src tree

findings.claim: primitives.ts:40 reads the deprecated element.ref, which triggers React 19's dev warning if the Slot is ever rendered. The file is orphaned: JSX in a .ts file, excluded from tsconfig and Biome, imported nowhere, and outside the tsdown entries.
findings.fix: Delete packages/modern-cmdk/src/react/primitives.ts, and remove its exclude entries from packages/modern-cmdk/tsconfig.json and biome.json:174. If a Slot is ever needed, read children.props.ref instead.
findings.groupTitle: Orphaned primitives.ts (JSX in .ts, reads deprecated element.ref)

findings.claim: In virtual mode, hovering any item calls scrollToIndex, which pins that item to the top without a visibility check, so the list jumps under the pointer; arrow keys pin to top too. The effect re-runs every render.
findings.fix: Depend on virtualizer.scrollToIndex, which is stable. Make it align to nearest: scroll only when the item is outside the viewport. Skip pointer activations via a ref that handlePointerMove sets and the effect checks and clears.
findings.groupTitle: scrollToIndex always aligns the row to the top: jumps on ArrowDown and hover, O(index) scans

findings.claim: When container is inside a shadow root, document.getElementById(inputId) returns null. preventDefault has already run, so nothing gets focus when the dialog opens.
findings.fix: e.preventDefault(); (e.currentTarget as HTMLElement | null)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[id="${CSS.escape(inputId)}"]`)?.focus();
findings.groupTitle: Dialog focuses the input by document.getElementById, which fails inside a shadow root

findings.claim: The L1 'GPU-composited animations' header is false. Height (L187), item background-color (L204) and the overlay --command-overlay-opacity (L317) transitions are layout or paint. will-change: height (L186) is useless. L335 is accurate.
findings.fix: Reword L1: dialog opacity, scale and translate are compositor-only; list height, item background and overlay tint are not. Remove will-change: height at L186. Keep L335.
findings.groupTitle: styles.css header claims all animations are GPU-composited

findings.claim: The item background-color transition uses linear(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), which is equivalent to the linear keyword.
findings.fix: styles.css:204 -> transition: background-color var(--command-duration-item) linear;
findings.groupTitle: Item transition uses linear(0,.25,.5,.75,1), the same as linear

findings.claim: On first render Command.Empty sees statusContainerRef.current as null and renders inline inside the listbox, an invalid ARIA child. It moves to the status container, remounting, only on the next state-context change.
findings.fix: list.tsx: const [statusEl, setStatusEl] = useState<HTMLDivElement | null>(null); <div ref={setStatusEl} data-command-list-status="" />; provide statusEl. Context type: HTMLDivElement | null. empty.tsx: if (el) createPortal(content, el).
findings.groupTitle: Empty reads statusContainerRef in render, so it renders inside the listbox at mount and then remounts

findings.claim: cli.ts:65 uses flags.some((f) => f === '--dry-run') where flags.includes('--dry-run') is the direct form.
findings.fix: Fold into finding 12: with node:util parseArgs, --dry-run becomes options: { 'dry-run': { type: 'boolean' } }. If finding 12 is declined, use flags.includes('--dry-run').
findings.groupTitle: Hand-rolled argv parser (no --help/--version, no unknown-flag errors, .some instead of includes)

findings.claim: Disposal ownership conflicts. The machine disposes the engine (machine.ts:380), yet the wasm-engine.ts:21 JSDoc says `await using engine`. Doing both calls instance.free() twice, and dispose throws 'null pointer passed to rust'.
findings.fix: README L49: say the machine disposes the engine passed as `search`, so do not also `using` it. Change the JSDoc at wasm-engine.ts:21 to match. Make [Symbol.dispose] and [Symbol.asyncDispose] (wasm-engine.ts:69-75) idempotent with a `freed` flag.
findings.groupTitle: Engine is disposed twice (by the machine and by the recommended 'await using'), so instance.free() runs twice

findings.claim: Nothing tests the wasm-bindgen boundary or the TS wrappers. As a result, createWasmSearchEngine (and worker.ts) never call the wasm-pack init() and always fall back to the TS engine, and no test catches it.
findings.fix: Add wasm-bindgen-test tests run by `wasm-pack test --node crate` (new/index_items/search/clear/free). Add a wrapper test that inits pkg from the wasm bytes and asserts isWasm === true. Call `await wasm.default()` in wasm-engine.ts:28 and worker.ts:45.
findings.groupTitle: No tests for the wasm-bindgen boundary or the TS wrappers

findings.claim: search() walks a HashMap<usize,f64> and then calls sort_unstable_by on score alone. Results with equal scores therefore come back in arbitrary order, not the registration order core keeps.
findings.fix: Keep idx with each candidate, e.g. collect (idx, score). Sort with `b.score.total_cmp(&a.score).then_with(|| a_idx.cmp(&b_idx))`, then truncate and build SearchResult. Add a unit test with tied scores.
findings.groupTitle: Tied scores come out in HashMap order, not registration order

findings.claim: The scaffolded package.json has no script that runs tsc. vite build only transpiles, so a scaffolded app with a type error still builds green.
findings.fix: Add "typecheck": "tsc" to the generated scripts; the generated tsconfig already sets noEmit: true. Optionally change build to 'tsc && vite build', as create-vite does.
findings.groupTitle: Scaffolded package.json has no tsc script, so type errors build green

findings.claim: The test named 'without degradation' asserts only correctness (500 entries, positive bonuses). It measures no time, so it cannot detect a performance regression.
findings.fix: Rename it to 'should handle 10K frecency selections across 500 ids'. If degradation matters, add a frecency recordSelection case to benchmarks/ rather than a wall-clock assert in a unit test.
findings.groupTitle: Stress assertions that cannot fail (length >= 0, instanceof Array, 'without degradation' with no timing)
findings.note: Landed as cd0a2f3 (f5609e4). STR-1 'machine should handle state transitions under load' (red with machine.ts searching query.slice(0, 1): 1 failed of 10 new, old 10 passed); STR-3 'should handle rapid typing simulation — 10 incremental prefix queries' (red with no results past 3 characters); STR-6 'should handle special characters in search queries' (red with the scorer accepting partial matches); U-3 renamed to 'should handle 10K frecency selections across 500 ids'. The two P05 batching tests from the machine landing are kept in the same file (12 passed, 5 runs).

findings.claim: Comments at stress.test.ts:37 and :156 call Iterator helpers ES2026, but they are ES2025 (TS lib es2025). The same mislabel recurs across tests/unit/*, create-modern-cmdk/src/index.ts and modern-cmdk/src/codemod/*.
findings.fix: Replace 'ES2026 Iterator Helper(s)' with 'ES2025 Iterator helpers' at every hit of grep -rn 'ES2026 Iterator' tests packages/*/src, not just stress.test.ts.
findings.groupTitle: Iterator helpers labelled ES2026 across tests (they are ES2025)

findings.claim: results[0]?.id passes ItemId | undefined to recordSelection(itemId: ItemId) (frecency/index.ts:87). That is TS2345 under the repo's noUncheckedIndexedAccess, unnoticed only because no tsconfig type-checks tests/.
findings.fix: Replace L120-122 with: const [top] = results; if (top) frecencyEngine.recordSelection(top.id);
findings.groupTitle: tests/ is outside every tsconfig, hiding latent errors such as TS2345 in stress.test.ts

findings.claim: Root idb-keyval (package.json:48) duplicates packages/modern-cmdk/package.json:65. Root release script (L29) builds docs+playground and publishes locally with no OIDC, while CONTRIBUTING.md:250 sells it as the publish path.
findings.fix: Drop idb-keyval from root devDependencies and re-run that test. Delete the release script and the CONTRIBUTING.md:250 row (publishing is release.yml only). Do not point release.yml at it: the publish sub-action runs changeset publish --from-pack-dir itself.

findings.claim: Every JS-vs-WASM pair in wasm-search.bench.ts (1K/10K, single and incremental) runs on items with 2 keywords. The JS engine lowercases and scores both keywords per item; the WASM engine ignores keywords. The measured WASM speedup is inflated.
findings.fix: Strip keywords from the items used in the JS-vs-WASM comparison groups (keep a separate keyword-bearing JS-only bench), or add a header comment stating that WASM indexes value only and the JS numbers include keyword scoring.
findings.groupTitle: JS-vs-WASM bench pairs are not like-for-like and silently measure the TS fallback

findings.claim: ci-bench.ts measures a subset of compare-baseline.ts on identical data and gates nothing. ci.yml's bench job runs both back to back, measuring the same work twice. Neither writes benchmarks/results/, which both workflows upload.

findings.groupTitle: ci-bench.ts exits 0 on failure, duplicates compare-baseline, and no script writes benchmarks/results/

findings.groupTitle: benchmarks/standalone/setup.ts: non-spec sumPrecise, dead RegExp.escape, unused ts-expect-error, false 'Node doesn't ship these' header

findings.claim: The default theme is dark-only, but meta color-scheme 'dark light' (index.html L6), :root color-scheme 'light dark' (styles.css L100) and the light theme-color meta (L8) let a light-preferring UA render light chrome on dark tokens.
findings.fix: Set meta color-scheme content="dark". Set :root { color-scheme: dark } at styles.css L100. Keep :root[data-theme=light] { color-scheme: light }. Replace the two media-keyed theme-color metas with a single #0a0e1a.
findings.groupTitle: Theme bootstrap disagrees with itself: dark-only tokens versus 'light dark' color-scheme, mismatched theme-color metas, toggle ignores OS and storage

findings.claim: apps/playground/tsconfig.json inherits declaration:true and isolatedDeclarations:true from tsconfig.base.json L13-14. The app never emits declarations, yet tsc --noEmit still requires explicit return types on exported components (TS9013).
findings.fix: In apps/playground/tsconfig.json compilerOptions add "declaration": false and "isolatedDeclarations": false; both are needed because isolatedDeclarations requires declaration. The React.ReactNode return annotations then become optional.
findings.groupTitle: Playground tsconfig repeats or inherits library-only options (noEmit, allowImportingTsExtensions, declaration and isolatedDeclarations)

findings.claim: The module-scope fetchResults() runs once per server process during SSR. Every request shares its result, which never refreshes, and the client fetches again on hydration. Example: user 1's results get served to every later user.
findings.fix: Add an SSR variant: an async Server Component calls fetchResults() without awaiting it and passes the promise as a prop to a 'use client' palette, which passes it to Command.AsyncItems items. This gives one fetch per request.
findings.groupTitle: The SSR sample's module-scope fetch shares one result across all requests

findings.claim: @shikijs/twoslash is an unused devDependency of apps/docs. It installs twoslash 0.3.9 with an unmet TypeScript peer and is never imported.
findings.fix: Remove @shikijs/twoslash from apps/docs/package.json and update the lockfile. Keep the commented import and the markdown block (or move them to a docs/plans note) so they record when to re-add it.
findings.groupTitle: Unused apps/docs devDependencies @shikijs/twoslash and svgo

findings.claim: The docs site has no favicon link and no favicon file (public/ holds only og-image.svg), so browsers 404 on /favicon.ico. Aside: og:image and twitter:image point to og-image.png, which does not exist.

findings.claim: Each AsyncItems batch registers under the API ids and is never removed. Old results pile up in the registry and search index, and each result counts twice: as a batch item and as the rendered Command.Item.
findings.fix: Return a cleanup from AsyncItemsInner's useLayoutEffect that sends UNREGISTER_ITEM for each batch id, or add a batch-unload event. Document that each resolution replaces the previous batch.
findings.groupTitle: AsyncItems registers batches alongside the rendered Items and never unregisters them (double count, phantom ids)

findings.claim: The docs example needs items! only because Object.groupBy returns a Partial<Record>. Map.groupBy returns Map<string, T[]> and needs no assertion.
findings.fix: Replace Object.entries(Object.groupBy(results, fn)) with [...Map.groupBy(results, (r) => String(r.data?.category))], and change items!.map to items.map.

findings.claim: The example binds Mod+C. While that item is registered, every Ctrl/Cmd+C on the page, including copying text in the search input, is swallowed and runs the item's handler.

findings.claim: In controlled mode, Escape calls the consumer's onOpenChange(false) at least twice (the original CLOSE plus the prop-sync echo) and up to three times.

findings.groupTitle: Each REGISTER_ITEM refilters the whole registry, so mount is O(n^2)
findings.note: apps/docs/examples/virtualized.md and recipes/emoji-picker.md drop the fps claim and say every Command.Item mounts and registers while virtualization skips only off-screen DOM (react/item.tsx:72, react/list.tsx:111-136); guide/virtualization.md follows in afd13a2 and 5a4f0aa. NAR-emoji-2's code half (one refilter per batch for registry events) is c339027.

findings.claim: benchmarks.md:89 promises 'yields to browser when input pending', but createScheduler gates yielding on navigator.scheduling.isInputPending (Chromium-only). Firefox and Safari never yield, so a batch of more than 10 updates during typing runs in full.
findings.fix: In core/utils/scheduler.ts, drop the isInputPending gate. Run a large batch in chunks and await globalThis.scheduler.yield() between chunks when canYield, falling back to rAF. Reword benchmarks.md:89 to say it yields via scheduler.yield() where supported.
findings.groupTitle: Scheduler yields only behind the Chromium-only isInputPending
findings.note: apps/docs/benchmarks.md says a batch always runs whole with no isInputPending or scheduler.yield gate (core/utils/scheduler.ts:1-5); fix round ebb6900. The code half is 05563b6.

findings.claim: The five recipe pages have no entry point: no nav item, no hero action and no inbound link. Readers can only reach them through local search or by typing the URL.

findings.claim: The L30 comment calls Iterator.from/map/toArray 'ES2026 Iterator Helpers'. They are ES2025 (TS lib.es2025.iterator). The same mislabel recurs in the benchmarks and elsewhere.

findings.groupTitle: Iterator helpers labelled ES2026 across tests (they are ES2025)

findings.claim: The test helpers (command.test.tsx:29-62, and the same in the async, cmdk-comparison, perf-accuracy and virtualization tests) await queueMicrotask and say the scheduler is microtask-based. Under happy-dom it is rAF-based, so these waits flush nothing.
findings.fix: Add a helper: flushFrame = () => act(async () => { await new Promise<void>((r) => requestAnimationFrame(() => r())); }). Use it in place of each queueMicrotask act block, and change the comments to say rAF batching.
findings.groupTitle: React test helpers and comments assume a microtask scheduler; happy-dom flushes via rAF
findings.note: Scheduler-batch waits in the comparison and frecency React tests are one requestAnimationFrame frame, not microtask and timer sleeps ('should process SEARCH_CHANGE events independently of React', 'should support subscribe/unsubscribe pattern'; red with the frame wait made immediate: 2 of 88 and 1 of 3). U-9 is closed by 9ab0903 together with 941f612 (the React helpers).

findings.claim: Disabled handling is inconsistent. An empty query hides disabled items (machine.ts:130). A non-empty query renders disabled matches (item.tsx:92 aria-disabled), and arrow/Home/End navigation lands on them.
findings.fix: Remove the .filter at machine.ts:130 so disabled items are always kept. Make navigate() and refilter's initial activeId skip disabled registry items. Add tests for both the empty and the non-empty query.
findings.groupTitle: Disabled handling inconsistent: hidden on empty query, rendered and navigable on non-empty query
findings.note: R2/D78 disabled contract landed as 74ee107 (52057c7: disabled items rendered with aria-disabled and data-disabled, skipped by NAVIGATE, ITEM_ACTIVATE and ITEM_SELECT, excluded from the first active item; `disabledItems: 'hide'` restores the hidden rendering) and 8ddd517 (9760e16: 'hide' also drops ids a self-indexing engine returns). Proof set: tests/unit/disabled-matrix.test.ts, the 'disabled items' describe of command.test.tsx and the D78 e2e test. Visible side effects at rest for the changeset: a group holding only disabled items shows; Command.Empty no longer appears when only disabled items exist; filteredCount, the results announcement and the virtualization threshold count disabled items.

findings.claim: The comment 'Handler should not be called since ref was deleted from set' is wrong. The Set holds the listener function itself, which dispose deletes (event-emitter.ts:26).
findings.fix: Reword to '// Handler should not be called: dispose removed the listener from the set'.
findings.groupTitle: event-emitter test comments invent WeakRef/ref semantics; the emitter holds strong listener refs

findings.claim: 'should work with using declaration' never checks that leaving the block disposed the instance. It passes even if `using` does not invoke [Symbol.dispose].
findings.fix: Declare `let ref: IdbFrecencyStorage | undefined;` and set `ref = storage` inside the block. After it, add `expect((await ref!.load('dispose-test')).records.size).toBe(0);`.

findings.note: tests/unit/frecency-idb.test.ts: 'should no-op operations after dispose' (red with save or delete ignoring disposed: 1 of 25), 'should return empty data when disposed although the namespace holds a row' (a live instance saves, a disposed instance on the same database loads empty, the live one still loads the row; red with load ignoring disposed: 3 of 25), 'should work with using declaration' (TUB-72; red with dispose a no-op: 2 of 25).

findings.claim: The single-key Object.groupBy (L20-69) read via `importTestCases.rewrite ?? []` (L73) is pure indirection. A case with a misspelled type is silently never run.
findings.fix: Make the cases a plain `const rewriteCases = [...]` without the type field. Replace the loop with `it.for(rewriteCases)('rewrites $label from cmdk', (testCase) => {...})`. Remove the groupBy comment.

findings.claim: The 'search engine - incremental' bench times engine creation plus a 100K index alongside the four searches, so the incremental-search cost is not isolated.
findings.fix: Use bench(name, { beforeAll() { engine = createSearchEngine(); engine.index(items100K); }, afterAll() { engine[Symbol.dispose](); } }, () => {the 4 searches}). Keep 'full pipeline' as the index+search bench.
findings.groupTitle: Benches time engine construction, indexing and disposal along with the named operation

findings.claim: No workflow runs `vitest bench`, so benchmarks/*.bench.ts can break or stop measuring anything without CI noticing.
findings.fix: Add a step `pnpm exec vitest bench --run` to the ci.yml bench job, or delete the vitest bench files if the standalone harness is canonical.
findings.groupTitle: No workflow runs vitest bench, so benchmarks/*.bench.ts can rot unnoticed

findings.claim: 'filter 1K/10K items' (L27-39) measures construction, send-scheduling and dispose. SEARCH_CHANGE is never processed, so no filtering is measured.

findings.groupTitle: Command.Input's controlled value lags a stale transition render, and Command.Loading flashes on every keystroke

findings.groupTitle: bench:compare applies its relative thresholds to a sub-microsecond median
findings.claim: bench:compare applies the 5 % warning and 15 % failure thresholds to stateUpdate:navigate, whose baseline median is 0.00075 ms and whose run-to-run noise exceeds both (its own p99 is ten times its median): the push run 41825347128 on 2ec7389 read 0.00075 -> 0.0009 ms as +20.0 %, exited 2 and failed the required Benchmarks job, while the pull_request run on the same commit passed the same job on the same CPU model. The published contract for that benchmark is its 1 ms target, 1300 times away; the comparator has no absolute floor, so the relative rule is applied where it has no meaning. Orchestrator, 2026-11-04.
findings.fix: An absolute floor in benchmarks/baseline.json regressionThresholds (floor_ms 0.01): a median below it is reported with its delta, not compared; a median above target_ms still fails; a pure classify() in benchmarks/standalone/compare-rules.ts applies target, floor, then the relative rule, with tests first; the reason is printed and written to the results JSON; the exit-code contract is unchanged; README.md, apps/docs/benchmarks.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and the ci.yml comments state the floor (wave 8, item F-02).

findings.groupTitle: bench:compare applies its relative thresholds to a sub-microsecond median
findings.claim: A baseline median below floor_ms on an entry without target_ms is checked by nothing: rule (1) is skipped because there is no target and rule (2) always passes. Latent today (every entry in benchmarks/baseline.json carries a target_ms; navigate's is 1 ms), so a future entry added without a target would silently escape the gate. Wave-8 ledger judge (wf_96524901-ba3), 2026-11-04.
findings.fix: classify() throws for a below-floor baseline that has no target_ms (the message names the entry's median); compare-baseline.ts surfaces it as a harness error (exit 2); test (i) in tests/unit/bench-compare-rules.test.ts pins it; the header comments of both files name the rule.

findings.groupTitle: scheduler.ts throws at import on a runtime without a navigator global
findings.claim: hasInputPending is computed as typeof navigator?.scheduling?.isInputPending === 'function'. typeof guards only a bare identifier, so on a runtime where navigator is undeclared the optional chain evaluates navigator first and throws ReferenceError at module evaluation, taking the whole core entry with it (reproduced: delete globalThis.navigator in Node 28, then the expression throws 'navigator is not defined'); the line above it already reads globalThis.scheduler safely. Unreachable on the supported runtimes (Node >= 21, browsers, workers all define navigator) but it contradicts the 'DOM APIs are feature-detected' claim the READMEs and getting-started.md make. W9-03 verifier (declined to judge, outside its files), wave 9, 2026-11-04.
findings.fix: Read navigator through globalThis like the scheduler line (typeof globalThis.navigator?.scheduling?.isInputPending), with a test that deletes the navigator global, re-imports modern-cmdk and runs the scheduler.

findings.at: scripts/check-licenses.ts:143-152 (the Unknown branch of evaluate) and tests/package/license-policy.json
findings.groupTitle: check:licenses reads differently on Linux and Windows for a package whose licence file name is lowercase
findings.claim: The first real run of the Package integrity job (CI run 41914394016, ubuntu-26.04, 2026-11-04T21:16:48Z) failed `pnpm check:licenses` with 'khroma@2.1.0: unknown or missing licence' (census Unknown: 3) while the same tree on win32 lists khroma under MIT (Unknown: 2). khroma 2.1.0 (mermaid 12.3.0 -> apps/docs only) has no license field and ships a lowercase `license` file; pnpm 12.17.0's resolver (pnpm/crates/cli/src/cli_args/licenses/license_resolver.rs at v12.17.0, LICENSE_FILES lines 7-17 tried by exact name in read_first_license_file lines 86-96) opens it on NTFS and misses it on ext4. G-28's standing rule 5 ('check:licenses exits 0 on the merged wave-3 tree') was measured on Windows only. A plain Unknown exception would be stale on Windows (evaluate's stale check), so the audit needs a platform-independent resolution.
findings.fix: W4-03: a `licenseFiles` policy section with hash-pinned declarations {package, version, license, file, sha256, reason}; resolveLicenseFiles() verifies the file's sha256 through an injected reader and moves the version out of Unknown, with violations for a mismatch, a missing file, a stale declaration or a disagreeing report; the khroma entry pins sha256 66b333b0f66759a0b710459e03f7029abe17f4358114a128d2c972e642961b49.

findings.groupTitle: ARCHITECTURE.md describes dialog animations that are inert until DT-19

Wave 6 (W6-05).

findings.at: apps/docs/guide/async-items.md (Basic Usage, GranularLoading, ResilientSearch); apps/docs/examples/async-search.md (first sample)
findings.groupTitle: Async samples create the promise in render while ssr.md warns that re-suspends forever
findings.claim: async-items.md's Basic Usage, GranularLoading and ResilientSearch samples and async-search.md's first sample create the promise during render (`items={fetchCommands()}`, `searchAPI(query)`); apps/docs/guide/ssr.md:93 says 'a new promise on every render re-suspends forever'. The samples type-check (W6-07, W6-08) but contradict the warning and would loop in a browser. Reported by the W6-07 and W6-08 workers and verifiers (wf_c8b7f936-32e), 2026-11-04.
findings.fix: Create each promise where it is cached (a module-level Map keyed by the query, or useMemo on the query with a sentence why); ResilientSearch deletes the cache entry on error before the key remount; the samples and ssr.md's warning agree. W7-04.

findings.groupTitle: The 'Debounced API Search' sample has no debounce
findings.claim: async-items.md:46-48 promises a debounced search and the DebouncedSearchPalette sample (~:118) debounces nothing. Reported by the W6-07 worker (wf_c8b7f936-32e), 2026-11-04.
findings.fix: A real useDebouncedValue(value, 200) hook in the sample (useState + useEffect with setTimeout/clearTimeout; useDeferredValue is not a debounce) feeding the cached promise, or a heading that says what the sample does. W7-04.

findings.groupTitle: The Highlight sample passes an empty ranges array
findings.claim: basic-usage.md:102 passes `ranges={[/* match ranges from scorer */]}` to Command.Highlight: an empty array highlights nothing. CommandHighlightProps.ranges is ReadonlyArray<readonly [start, end]> (dist/react/index.d.mts:48-49) and the core exposes match ranges as half-open tuples (dist/core/index.d.mts:5). Reported by the W6-07 worker (wf_c8b7f936-32e), 2026-11-04.
findings.fix: Show real ranges from the search result or scorer the core exposes; if none reaches the React layer, compute them from the query in two lines and say so. W7-04.

findings.groupTitle: FrecencyOptions.enabled is a required boolean
findings.claim: FrecencyOptions declares `readonly enabled: boolean` (core/types.ts:147; dist/core/index.d.mts:175), so `new FrecencyEngine({ storage, namespace })` fails TS2741; the api/command.md sample had to add `enabled: true` (W6-06). A required boolean that is true in every documented use is API friction. Filed from the W6-06 report (wf_c8b7f936-32e), 2026-11-04.
findings.fix: Make `enabled` optional with default true (exactOptionalPropertyTypes-safe: `readonly enabled?: boolean` read as `options.enabled ?? true`); update the docs sample and the migration page; a changeset (minor). 1.5.0.

findings.groupTitle: The wasm package does not export its engine types
findings.claim: createWasmSearchEngine resolves to WasmSearchEngine | FallbackSearchEngine, neither exported from modern-cmdk-search-wasm, so a consumer who stores the engine must write `Awaited<ReturnType<typeof createWasmSearchEngine>>` (the docs now do: examples/virtualized.md, W6-08). Filed from the W6-08 report (wf_c8b7f936-32e), 2026-11-04.
findings.fix: Export the two interfaces (or one `SearchEngine` union type) from the package's public types; update the docs to the exported name; a changeset (minor) for the wasm package. 1.5.0.

findings.groupTitle: CommandErrorBoundary has no reset API
findings.claim: CommandErrorBoundary takes `fallback` (node or (error) => node) and `onError(error, info)` and exposes no reset (dist/react/index.d.mts:182-196); retry works only by changing the boundary's key, which the docs now show (async-items.md, async-search.md, W6-07/W6-08). Filed from the W6-08 report (wf_c8b7f936-32e), 2026-11-04.
findings.fix: Give the fallback render prop a `reset` callback (and/or a `resetKeys` prop) so a Retry button works without a key remount; docs updated; a changeset (minor). 1.5.0.

findings.groupTitle: The core never sets state.loading, so Command.Loading and the list's aria-busy depend on a flag nothing sets
findings.claim: state.loading is written only as false (core/machine.ts:309; core/types.ts:207 declares it); Command.Loading renders only when `loadingOverride ?? (state.loading || isPending)` is true (loading.tsx:25-27) and the list's aria-busy mirrors state.loading (list.tsx:163). Without the `loading` prop, `<Command.Loading>` never renders and aria-busy is never true, even while AsyncItems suspends. The docs were rewritten to pass `loading` (W6-07); the field remains a dead flag. Found by the W6-07 verifier (wf_c8b7f936-32e), 2026-11-04.
findings.fix: Either drive state.loading from the React layer (AsyncItems sets it while its promise is pending, via a machine event) so Command.Loading and aria-busy work without the prop, or remove the field and derive both from the pending transition; tests for both consumers; a changeset. 1.5.0.

findings.groupTitle: dist/react/styles.css is the source file, comments and all

The W7-05 header comment alone moved the gzip size from 3932 B (benchmarks/size-history/1.4.0.json at 9827e1f) to 3959 B of the 4000 B limit (size-limit 14.3.0, 2026-11-04). Observed by the W7-05 verifier and the orchestrator while closing DT-66, 2026-11-05.

Belongs with the styles.css work of 1.8.0 (DT-19), when the budget is re-baselined anyway.

findings.groupTitle: async-search.md wraps AsyncItems in Suspense boundaries that never show
