findings.groupTitle: github/codeql-action is pinned to an annotated tag object, not a commit
findings.claim: codeql.yml:36 (init), :41 (analyze) and scorecard.yml:34 (upload-sarif) pin github/codeql-action@f3bbb05694c2f74569081c28664c0866d64dec21 '# v4.39.3'. That sha is the annotated tag object of v4.39.3 (git/ref/tags/v4.39.3 -> type tag), not a commit: the commits API answers 422 for it; the tag peels to commit 33d7b85da1a04171e211befe2c739303b9a4c066 (2026-11-04T16:47:01Z). Every other action in the repository pins a release commit, and the two Analyze checks are required on main. Tools that resolve a pin as a commit (Dependabot's sha-to-tag mapping, impostor-commit audits, the freshness sweep) cannot resolve a tag object. Final review wf_48132ab1-176 (ci-and-release-plumbing), confirmed by the judge, 2026-11-05.
findings.fix: Pin 33d7b85da1a04171e211befe2c739303b9a4c066 # v4.39.3 at the three sites; verify `gh api repos/github/codeql-action/commits/33d7b85da1a04171e211befe2c739303b9a4c066 --jq .sha` and `grep -rn f3bbb05 .github` empty; validate the files with action-validator in WSL (D56). Standing rule (G-33): resolve action pins with `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<tag> --jq .sha`, which peels annotated tags, never git/ref/tags .object.sha. W8-02.

findings.at: packages/modern-cmdk/src/codemod/files.ts:198-239 (findDirtyFiles: only entries ending in '/' are prefixes) and :141-170 (git check-ignore)
findings.groupTitle: The dirty-tree refusal and discovery do not understand git submodules
findings.claim: `git status --porcelain -z` prints a modified submodule as ` M sub` with no trailing '/', so findDirtyFiles's prefix match (dirtyDirs holds only entries ending in '/') never marks a file under it dirty (the wave-1 judge's probe). Under the modern-cmdk-codemod profile discovery runs `git check-ignore` first, which exits 128 ('is in submodule') for such a path and makes the run fail with an uncaught error before any write (the W1-02b verifier's probe), so nothing is overwritten today, but the failure names no submodule and leaves no way to migrate one, and the dirty check would pass the files if discovery ever did.
findings.fix: findDirtyFiles runs status with --ignore-submodules=none and treats every entry that is a directory on disk (a gitlink, an untracked directory) as a dirty prefix; strict discovery groups matched files by the repository that owns them (gitlink roots from `git ls-files -s -z`, mode 160000) and runs check-ignore inside each, so a clean submodule's files migrate under its own .gitignore and a dirty one refuses with exit 2 through the existing path; tests first (W2-07).

findings.at: packages/modern-cmdk-codemod/src/files.ts (trustBoundary, inside, gitSearchDirs, resolveGit, isGitOutside, runGit)
findings.claim: SEC-57's resolution (cd9d415) filtered PATH against the spawn cwd, not the repository: with cwd a subdirectory, a PATH entry elsewhere in the same work tree was searched; ignoredIn passed a submodule directory as the root, so the superproject around it was searched; PATH entries and candidates were not realpath-compared, so a symlinked entry into the tree was kept, and the raw cwd (/var/folders on macOS, the runner's short TEMP path on Windows) did not match git's realpath toplevel, which made the planted copy run during ls-files on macos-26 and windows-2025 in CI run 41998415732; and a directory named git passed access, failing at spawn. The automated review of cd9d415 rated it HIGH (CWE-426); rated medium here because every path needs an absolute PATH entry inside the migrated tree or a link to it.
findings.fix: trustBoundary(cwd): the realpath of the nearest directory from realpath(cwd) upward that holds a .git entry (what rev-parse --show-toplevel reports, computed without spawning git), else realpath(cwd); the nearest rather than the outermost, so a dotfiles repository at the user's home does not exclude every PATH entry under the home (scoop shims, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Git\cmd, ~/.local/bin). discoverFiles and findDirtyFiles compute it once and pass it to every runGit of the operation (cwd is where git runs, boundary is what PATH is filtered against); inside() is the one containment test; resolveGit realpaths each kept entry and re-tests it; isGitOutside requires a regular file, X_OK and a realpath outside the boundary. SEC-58 titles: trustBoundary from a subdirectory, from a tree with no .git and through a symlink alias; a subdirectory cwd; a symlink-alias PATH entry; the CI shape (cwd the alias; a junction on Windows); a directory named git; a planted git in the superproject's bin while check-ignore runs in the submodule.

findings.claim: The pre-push size job was gated by glob packages/*/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}; lefthook's glob needs a directory between src/ and **/, so a push whose only source changes sat directly under a package's src (cli.ts, files.ts) printed 'size (skip) no matching push files' and never ran size-limit: the pushes of 2b36297 and cdc05f2 did, and CI run 41998415732's Bundle Size job caught the 93,739 B over-budget instead. Probed with lefthook run pre-push --job size --file <path>: files.ts skipped, codemod/bin.ts ran.
findings.fix: glob {packages/*/src/**,packages/*/tsdown.config.ts,package.json}: any file under a package's src, a tsdown config or the root package.json (where the budgets live) runs size-limit; a docs-only push still skips it (probed on all four shapes). The comment states the rule and the reason.

findings.claim: SEC-58's nearest-work-tree boundary (0a41f02) stopped at a submodule's .git FILE (gitdir: ../.git/modules/<name>) when cwd was inside a submodule checkout, so the superproject around it, cloned from the same untrusted source, stayed searchable: a planted git at <super>/bin on PATH ran for a dirty check from <super>/inner (red first). The automated review of 0a41f02 (CWE-426, MEDIUM) named the case; its two other suggestions were declined by ruling (G-37): validating that .git holds a HEAD (git refuses to add any path component named .git, so a clone cannot carry a decoy) and dropping every node_modules/.bin PATH entry (the boundary already covers the clone's own node_modules).
findings.fix: trustBoundary climbs from a submodule to the superproject that holds the .git/modules directory its gitdir: target lies under, and again while that superproject is itself a submodule; a .git directory (an ordinary or nested repository) and a linked worktree's .git file (.git/worktrees) stop the climb; any read, match or realpath failure stops at the submodule. SEC-59 titles in codemod-submodule.test.ts: inner and inner/deep bound to super; super > mid > leaf climbs to super; a planted git at super/bin with cwd super/inner reads clean; a worktree and a nested repository are their own boundary.

findings.at: .github/workflows/release.yml first-publish-tarball (permissions; the Smoke-test the tarball step) and first-publish-attest
findings.claim: W4-05's round-1 first-publish-tarball job held id-token: write and attestations: write while its smoke step ran scripts/codemod-tarball-smoke.ts, which npm-installs the packed codemod tarball without a lockfile (jscodeshift's transitive tree resolved at run time) and executes the installed bin: code from any transitive package ran inside a job able to mint a Sigstore certificate and write attestations, so a compromised dependency could attest arbitrary artifacts under this repository's identity. Found by the wave-4 opus-verifier of W4-05 (important) before the job ever ran; the same job's header still claimed attest and publish were the only id-token jobs, and its version-job comment contradicted the new scope gate's error text.
findings.fix: The job is split: first-publish-tarball keeps the registry-state, scope-gate, build, pack, compare, smoke, hash, source.txt and upload steps with permissions contents: read only and exposes state, tarball and sha256 as outputs; a new first-publish-attest job (needs it; state first; contents: read, id-token: write, attestations: write, artifact-metadata: write) downloads the artifact, requires exactly one tarball whose name and sha256 equal the smoke job's outputs, unpacks it for syft, attests the build provenance and the SBOM with the pinned actions and uploads the SPDX file, running no setup-node, pnpm, npm or repository script and checking out nothing. The header names attest, first-publish-attest and publish as the only id-token: write jobs and says why the smoke job holds none; the version-job comment agrees with the gate (@changesets/apply-release-plan 8.1.1 dist/index.mjs:180 skips workspace:*). Tests (D62 titles in tests/unit/release-workflow.test.ts, 9 red first): the smoke job has no id-token or attestations permission; the attest job runs no pnpm, npm, setup-node or scripts/ step and downloads first; it verifies the sha256 before attesting; the header's id-token list equals the set of jobs whose permissions hold it; the version comment no longer claims changeset version rewrites workspace specifiers. Live behaviour is proven only by the owner's release run (W8-01).

findings.at: scripts/check-package.ts bareImports (:383) and blankNonCode (:297); tests/unit/check-package.test.ts header
findings.claim: W4-02's bare-import allow-list (2ed5818) decided whether a dynamic import() or require()/__require() match sat inside a string or comment by the text before it on the same line: a call was skipped when that text held an odd count of any one quote character or any //, so a real bare import after a URL string or after an apostrophe in another quote type on the same line was never reported, and template literals and block comments were not understood at all. The test file's header also under-described what the file covers. Found by the wave-4 opus-verifier of W4-02 (two minors).
findings.fix: blankNonCode(source) (exported, pure) runs once over each chunk before any regex: string and template contents become spaces with their delimiters kept (escapes honoured, a string open at a newline ends there, ${...} substitutions reopen code through a stack of brace depths), line comments are blanked to the newline and block comments whole, newlines are never replaced so offsets and line numbers hold; the import regexes run on the blanked text with the d flag and read each specifier from the original source at the match offsets. The doc comment states the one blind spot (a regex literal is not recognised) as a possible false negative, accepted because rolldown's chunks are not expected to hold one and the pack gate runs on the real dist. SEC-33 titles, 5 red first: import() after a // string, require() after an apostrophe string, no report inside a template literal, a block comment or a line comment, code inside ${...} still scanned, blankNonCode keeps length and line count. The test header names every area the file covers.

findings.at: scripts/consumer-smoke.ts killTree (:340) and the spawn options (:378)
findings.claim: consumer-smoke.ts's step timeout killed only the direct child (child.kill('SIGKILL')) and resolved on 'close', so on POSIX a grandchild that inherited the pipes (a bundler or dev server left by a consumer app's build) held the step open until its own exit: under WSL a step with a 1.5 s timeout ran 30071 ms, until the grandchild's timer ended, and in CI such a step runs to the job's own timeout. The same flaw was fixed in template-smoke.ts by W4-04 (197919f); its worker and verifier named this file as the remaining site.
findings.fix: run() is exported with template-smoke.ts's RunResult and signature; spawn uses detached: !IS_WINDOWS so the child leads a process group; killTree on POSIX calls process.kill(-pid, 'SIGKILL') and ignores only ESRCH; Windows keeps taskkill /T /F with a 30 s timeout; the exitCode early return is gone and resolution stays on 'close', which the group kill can no longer leave open. CLI, checks, exit codes and messages unchanged. Test: 'a timeout ends the step even when a grandchild holds the pipes, and the grandchild dies' (16 green before on Windows, where taskkill /T already kills the tree; the POSIX proof is a standalone WSL Ubuntu-26.04 run of run(): 30071 ms held before, 1505 ms with the grandchild dead after). Follow-ups: template-smoke.test.ts lacks the dead-grandchild assertion; the served-app spawn near :767 is not in a process group; the WSL proof is not wired into CI.

findings.fix: The line reads what the command does: on all three packed tarballs publint (strict), no catalog:/workspace: in a packed manifest, bin shebang and execute bits and the bare-import allow-list; attw on modern-cmdk; the file lists of modern-cmdk and modern-cmdk-codemod (run pnpm build first). findings.at: scripts/consumer-smoke.ts (the `next start` spawn in main; killTree); scripts/template-smoke.ts killTree
findings.claim: Regression in a6cf620 (W4-04b, filed under DT-69): killTree switched to process.kill(-pid, 'SIGKILL') on POSIX and ignored ESRCH, but the `next start` server spawned in main was not detached, so the group kill hit ESRCH (no such process group), the error was swallowed and the server survived, keeping the port bound and the script's event loop alive after the Next scenario (WSL probe: non-detached child, kill(-pid) -> ESRCH, child alive); before a6cf620 child.kill('SIGKILL') on the direct child did stop it. template-smoke.ts's killTree had the same ESRCH-swallowing shape, latent because its only spawn is detached. Found by the wave-4 ledger judge (opus-verifier) at a6cf620, and confirmed live by CI run 42009255255 on a6cf620: Consumer app (next-webpack) and Consumer app (next-turbopack) ran from 10:17:01Z to the job's 25-minute timeout-minutes and were cancelled inside the consumer-smoke step while Consumer app (vite) passed in 66 s; run 42002360862 on adfa46e, before a6cf620, had passed all three.
findings.fix: consumer-smoke.ts: an exported spawnServer(command, args, { cwd, env }) spawns the served app with detached: !IS_WINDOWS and piped stdio, used by the `next start` call site; killTree (exported) falls back to child.kill('SIGKILL') on ESRCH when the child is alive (exitCode and signalCode null), treats ESRCH as success only when the child is gone, rethrows anything else. template-smoke.ts's killTree mirrors the fallback (W4-04d). Tests: a killTree describe in consumer-smoke.test.ts (spawnServer child killed; non-group-leader child killed through the fallback; an exited child does not throw) and the dead-grandchild assertion plus the fallback test in template-smoke.test.ts. On win32 none can go red (taskkill /T kills any tree); the proof is WSL Ubuntu-26.04 node 26.10.0: spawnServer + killTree {alive: true} before, {alive: false} after; run() grandchild {timedOut: true, elapsed: 1507, alive: false}; the fallback {nonLeaderAlive: false}.

findings.at: apps/docs/guide/wasm-search.md:113-123 (the worker-engine sample's effect) and :41-54 (the main-thread sample's effect)
findings.claim: The worker-engine sample's effect cleanup only sets disposed = true: an engine that resolves after the cleanup (React StrictMode's mount, unmount and remount; a fast route change) is never disposed and its Worker keeps running, and even an engine that resolved before the cleanup is never disposed. The samples stay type-checked by check-doc-samples (full run, pkg/ present).

findings.at: scripts/check-repo-links.ts:259-283 at f1482d7 (Checkout#resolve: `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <ref>^{commit}` and `git fetch --no-tags [--depth=1] origin <ref>` with the link's ref as the last positional argument) and #inCommit (`git cat-file` / `git ls-tree` on `<commit>:<path>`)
findings.groupTitle: The repository link check passed a Markdown link's ref and path to git and the filesystem unvalidated
findings.claim: The ref of a blob/tree/raw link is the first URL path segment written in the repository's Markdown. At f1482d7 Checkout#resolve passed it unvalidated to `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <ref>^{commit}` and, when nothing resolved, to `git fetch --no-tags [--depth=1] origin <ref>`. git parses options anywhere on its command line, so a ref such as `--upload-pack=<command>` is an option and the fetch runs that command: the W8-05e verifier ran the f1482d7 script on a scratch repository whose README linked blob/--upload-pack=touch%20pwned/README.md and GIT_TRACE showed `run_command: ... 'touch pwned ...'` with the file pwned created. ci.yml runs the Links job on pull_request to main, so a pull request's Markdown reaches the script on the runner (a pull request also controls the script itself, so the fix is defence in depth for push and local runs). Filed from the automated security review of commit f1482d7 (argument / refspec injection, MEDIUM).
findings.fix: W8-05e and W8-05f (e297590): a ref that is not main, HEAD, a hex hash of 7 to 40 characters or a name matching REF_NAME (letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'; starting with a letter, digit or '_'; no '..'; no .lock ending) is reported dead with the reason `<ref> is not a ref this check accepts (...)` before any git call (Checkout#lookup); every git call whose positional argument a link supplies carries `--end-of-options` before it (rev-parse --verify, fetch before `origin <ref>`, cat-file -t, cat-file blob, ls-tree --name-only); the fetch note names the argv run; the header and the REF_NAME comment state the rule as the regex enforces it. Tests: `SEC-61: the accepted ref names`; `SEC-61: a link's ref that is not a hash or a plain name is dead before any git call, and no option reaches git` (a scratch repository with `--upload-pack=touch%20pwned`, `a..b` and `v1@{0}` refs: exit 1, the reason on each, no `ran git` note, no pwned file, GIT_TRACE pointed at a file that must not exist afterwards); the clone test pins the note `ran git fetch --no-tags --end-of-options origin side (ok)`. The 2026-11-06 ledger judge (wf_da3f9265-1c4) listed every git argv at e297590, probed %2D%2Dupload-pack, double encoding, -x, --output= and a newline, saw no git call and no trace file, and watched the f1482d7 script fail both SEC-61 tests.

findings.groupTitle: The repository link check passed a Markdown link's ref and path to git and the filesystem unvalidated
findings.claim: A blob/main/ or tree/main/ link's path was joined onto the root with no containment check, so `..` segments left --root (or the checkout): the script stat'ed and read files outside the repository and reported their existence, line count and headings (the W8-05e verifier's probe `blob/main/../../old.ts#L1-L99999` on a scratch root printed `#L1-L99999 is outside the file's 466 lines`, the line count of a file two directories above the root). e297590 closed that for main and HEAD only: the 2026-11-06 judge (wf_da3f9265-1c4) read secret.md above a --root subdirectory through blob/<sha>/../secret.md#L99 (`#L99 is outside the file's 3 lines`; without a fragment the link passed, exit 0) and through a committed symbolic link root/link.txt -> ../secret.txt (`#L999 is outside the file's 5 lines`), while the header claimed a path that leaves the root is never read. No git option is involved (that is SEC-61); this is a read outside the root driven by repository Markdown.
findings.fix: W8-05f (e297590): Checkout#inWorkingTree computes `relative(this.#root, full)` and returns the dead Lookup `<path> leaves the repository` when the relative path is `..`, starts with `..` + sep or is absolute, before any stat or read (test `SEC-62: a path with .. segments is dead without being read`). W9-00: the lexical check moves to the top of Checkout#lookup, before the ref branch, so commit links are covered too (test `SEC-62: a commit link's path with .. segments is dead under a --root subdirectory too`, exit 0 before the fix); #inWorkingTree resolves the path with realpath and reports `<path> leaves the repository through a symbolic link` when the real path lies outside the real root, and stat, readdir and readFile use the real path (test `SEC-62: a symbolic link that resolves outside the root is dead without being read`, skipped where symlink() is EPERM); the header says the rule applies whatever the ref and names the symbolic-link case.

findings.groupTitle: The repository link check passed a Markdown link's ref and path to git and the filesystem unvalidated
findings.claim: The dead-link and unchecked-fragment lines print the decoded ref, path and fragment raw, so a link that decodes to %0A or %0D%0A splits one link across two output lines and starts a line with text the link's author chose: on a GitHub Actions runner a line starting `::warning::`, `::error::` or `::notice::` is a workflow command. The 2026-11-06 judge (wf_da3f9265-1c4) printed a stdout line `::warning::f is not covered by a rule` from blob/main/LICENSE#x%0A::warning::f and stderr lines starting `::error::` and `::notice::` from blob/main/NOPE%0A::error::p and blob/x%0D%0A::notice::r/README.md (the last through SEC-61's own reason text, which repeats the rejected ref verbatim). The header's 'one stderr line per dead link' was false for such a link.
findings.fix: W9-00: a `printable` helper escapes control, format and line/paragraph-separator characters as \u{..} in every dead-link and unchecked-fragment line, so one link stays one line and no decoded link can start a workflow command; the header's Output sentence says so. findings.groupTitle: The first-publish tarball ran freshly resolved npm code before it was hashed, recorded and attested
findings.claim: In the first-publish-tarball job the smoke step (`node scripts/codemod-tarball-smoke.ts --codemod "$TGZ"`, which runs `npm exec --package <tgz> -- modern-cmdk-codemod` over a freshly resolved dependency tree of 96 packages with no lockfile) ran BEFORE the tarball was hashed, its source recorded and the artifact uploaded. A compromised transitive dependency executing in that step could rewrite first-publish/modern-cmdk-codemod-1.0.0.tgz before the digest was taken; the .sha256 file, source.txt and both attestations (first-publish-attest verifies the download against the job's sha256 output) would then cover the rewritten bytes, and every owner check in owner-gated-1.5.0.md would pass. The comments ('smoke-tests it and uploads it'; 'so the attested bytes are the smoke-tested bytes') described the gap as a guarantee. Filed from the 1.5.0 final review (wf_0ea5231e-588, workflows lens, finding 35), 2026-11-05.
findings.fix: W9-01: the smoke step leaves first-publish-tarball, which now only packs, checks, compares, hashes, records and uploads (no freshly resolved npm code runs in it); a new job first-publish-smoke (needs first-publish-tarball, state == 'first', contents: read only, no id-token) checks out the Version PR branch, installs with --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts, downloads the uploaded artifact, verifies its sha256 against the tarball job's output and runs the smoke script, uploading nothing; first-publish-attest needs both jobs, so a failed smoke blocks the attestation, and verifies the download against the tarball job's digest; the header job graph, the D62 paragraph, the id-token paragraph and both job comments say what each job runs. Tests (tests/unit/release-workflow.test.ts, SEC-63): the tarball job contains no smoke script and no npm exec/install and hashes before it records and uploads; the smoke job downloads, verifies the digest, runs the script and holds no id-token, attestations permission or upload; the attest job needs both.

findings.groupTitle: The codemod tarball smoke installed and ran npm dependencies with no release-age gate

The header (:22-23) and the comment at :384 justified it with 'npm, unlike pnpm, applies no release-age gate', which is false for the npm that runs here: npm 12.1.0, bundled with the .nvmrc Node 28 nightly, has `min-release-age` (days), and the reviewer's probe `npm install --dry-run --min-release-age=1 typescript@7.1.0-dev.20261105.1` was refused with ETARGET while a scratch pack resolved all 96 packages under the same flag (the local tarball is never gated). findings.at: tests/unit/codemod-submodule.test.ts:58-60 (mkdtemp fixtures under os.tmpdir), :135 (scratchRepo), :152 (SEC-59 nested submodule test) at 4e5b933
findings.groupTitle: The codemod submodule tests time out at 30 s under host load and leak their scratch repositories on Windows
findings.claim: The suite builds a scratch origin, a superproject, a submodule, a nested submodule and a worktree with real git subprocesses in mkdtemp directories under os.tmpdir() for every test. On 2026-11-08, while six agent worktrees ran installs and test suites on this host, the lefthook pre-push run of the full unit suite failed on 'SEC-59: a submodule of a submodule climbs to the outermost superproject' with 'Test timed out in 30000ms' followed by 'EBUSY: resource busy or locked, rmdir C:\Users\alber\.claude-tmp\modern-cmdk-sub-onvkPu\mid' (run log push-160-matrix.log); the same run passed on retry (1641 passed, 197 s). The replay worker's full run on docs/site-2026-11-onto-main at c82bcee failed the same test the same way, and the file alone took 209 s with SEC-59 timing out again and 'SEC-55: a dirty submodule refuses under modern-cmdk-codemod' failing with 'Hook timed out in 30000ms' plus the EBUSY rmdir (replay2-gate-unit-rerun-submodule.log). 69 modern-cmdk-sub-* directories were left under C:\Users\alber\.claude-tmp at 03:50Z, so the teardown has been leaking across runs. The tests pass on CI's isolated ubuntu runner (every main CI run) and on an idle host, so the defect is the fixture design, not the codemod: wall-clock-bound git work repeated per test, a 30 s hook timeout the work can exceed, and a teardown (rm without retries) that a Windows file lock defeats and that does not run when the test body times out. Filed by the orchestrator from the two logs, 2026-11-08.
findings.fix: Plan (1.6.0, cluster CORE/tests, with H): build the git fixtures once per file in beforeAll (one origin, one superproject with its submodule and nested submodule, one worktree) and have each test read them without mutating, or reset with git checkout/clean; tear down in afterAll with fs.rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 200 }) inside try/finally so a timed-out body still removes its directories; give the file one measured timeout for the beforeAll (the git work, measured idle and under load, with the measurement in the comment) and keep the 30 s default for the tests themselves; a unit test asserts the fixture directory set is empty after the suite (no leak). No retry of a failing assertion, no raised per-test timeout to hide slowness (LD-04).
findings.note: Landed as 38a1b07 (17a2b85): the submodule suite builds its git fixtures once per file in beforeAll (60 s hook timeout, measured 5.1 to 14.9 s over 9 runs) and tears them down in afterAll; all 11 titles unchanged, SEC-56's nested-submodule tests included. Red: an afterAll that removes another path fails the file; a trustBoundary that never climbs turns the 3 SEC-59 tests red. Timing under load (vitest Duration): before 27.62, 35.33, 35.60 s; after 13.02, 13.73, 13.84 s; back to back by the verifier: old 44.4 and 28.5 s, new 5.4 and 5.7 s. Green in shuffled order with three seeds. The first run under the real pre-push load is the push of this landing.

findings.groupTitle: The default scorer loops forever on a query containing a separator when the target has a doubled separator
findings.claim: At 6171765 the word-boundary tier of scoreItem splits the query on separators and walks the target's word starts; when the query contains a separator and the target carries a doubled separator ('Settings - Profile'), the loop pushes a zero-length segment and never advances its index. scoreItem('settings profile', { value: 'Settings - Profile' }) runs out of heap (exit 134) under Node 28, so typing that query into a palette whose items use ' - ' hangs the tab. Found by the SEARCH cluster's scorer worker while rewriting the tier (CE-35, CE-36); reproduced by its opus-verifier at 6171765 in a throwaway worktree; fixed in the same commit.
findings.fix: The rewritten cover (coverQuery) advances past every separator run and backtracks instead of re-scanning; proving test tests/unit/search.test.ts 'should not hang on a query with a separator against doubled separators' (red at 6171765 by heap exhaustion, green on the branch).
findings.note: Fixed in the same commit that rewrote the tier (1.6/search 2ee5ca5, landed as cea3cfd); the hang reproduced at 6171765 by the cluster's verifier.

findings.at: packages/modern-cmdk/src/core/search/index.ts:92 at 6171765 (the raw-query startsWith test that decided incremental pruning)
findings.groupTitle: Incremental pruning compared raw queries, so a query whose lowercase form changes length or letters pruned wrongly
findings.claim: At 6171765 the incremental path decided 'the new query extends the previous one' on the raw strings while the scorer compared lowercased text, so a query whose case folding changes the string ('ΑΣ' folds to 'ας', 'ΑΣΑ' to 'ασα': final sigma) could prune items the lowercased comparison would have kept, or rescan when it need not. The SEARCH cluster's pruning commit (1.6/search 583997a, landed as 3a8b472) compares lowercased queries (`lowerQuery.startsWith(previousQuery)` with `previousQuery = lowerQuery`), which fixes the path, but no test pins the case-folding case: the CE-88 tests cover ASCII case-only changes (ab/Ab, ap/App, AP/apple) only. Reported by the SEARCH manager as a possible row, 2026-11-08.
findings.fix: CORE/tests adds the dedicated test to tests/unit/search-incremental.test.ts (a Greek query 'ΑΣ' then 'ΑΣΑ' against items 'ασα' and 'ας': the second query scores only the first query's matches and finds the right items; red by temporarily comparing raw queries); then the row is FIXED by 3a8b472 with that test in tests/bug-matrix.json.
findings.note: Landed as a6c29af (dcd94c8). Test 'CE-105: should rescan every item when only the raw queries extend each other (final sigma lowercases differently)'. Red: comparing raw queries in index.ts gave 4 failed of 17 (3 on the parent file, so this test is the new red). Correction of the row's fix sentence, which described the mechanism inverted: the fixed code compares the lowercased queries, 'ασα' does not start with 'ας', so the second query rescans every item; the raw comparison is what pruned and missed 'ασα'.

findings.at: packages/modern-cmdk/src/react/styles.css:212 and :240 at d5046eb (user-select: none on the item and the group heading)

CSS-only, after the CORE/machine landing (styles.css is that cluster's file).

findings.at: packages/modern-cmdk/src/react/styles.css:194, :404-416, :444-445 at d5046eb (scroll-timeline and the three animation-timeline uses)
findings.groupTitle: styles.css relies on two features the Safari 18.4 floor lacks: unprefixed user-select and scroll-driven animations
findings.claim: The scroll-driven animations (the list's top fade and the scroll progress bar: `scroll-timeline: --list-scroll block` at :194, `animation-timeline: --list-scroll` at :405, :415 and :445) have no `@supports` guard. web-features marks animation-timeline as Limited availability with no Safari support at the 18.4 floor, so there the `animation` shorthand runs on its time-based default and the keyframes settle in their end state: the top fade always on and the progress bar always full, instead of tracking the scroll position. Reported by the BENCH cluster from the web-features data while allow-listing scroll-timeline, animation-timeline and animation-range for useBaseline; the visual result on Safari is not yet observed in a browser.
findings.fix: Wrap the scroll-timeline and animation-timeline declarations in `@supports (animation-timeline: scroll())` so unsupporting browsers render the static list without the fade and bar; observe the before and after in Playwright's WebKit once (the e2e project is Chromium-only under D85, so a one-off `playwright test --project=webkit` or a screenshot through `pnpm exec playwright screenshot --browser webkit` is the evidence); styles.css stays inside its 4 kB size-limit row. CSS-only, after the CORE/machine landing (styles.css is that cluster's file).
findings.note: Correction to the landing note: the three useBaseline allow entries from 5c08a99 were dead on the merged tree, because RA-77's @supports guard keeps Biome from reporting the guarded properties, and were removed at 8362840 (TEB-102). The R4 test proves the remaining entries (clip, user-select) are needed.

findings.at: packages/modern-cmdk/src/react/list.tsx:94-110 at d5046eb (the switch to the virtual wrapper at 100 items)
findings.groupTitle: Crossing 100 items remounts every item: N UNREGISTER plus N REGISTER after the first all-N emit
findings.claim: When the item count crosses 100 the list switches to its virtual wrapper and React remounts every child, so each item unregisters and re-registers: after the first emit that carries all N items the machine receives N UNREGISTER and N REGISTER sends, doubling the registration work of a mount that starts above 100 items. Evidence from the 1.6.0 browser bench harness (benchmarks/browser/run.ts, 1.6/bench 816901a): `sends_after_mount` is 2N in every 1K and 10K run; the extra work lands outside the gated keystroke-to-paint window but inside the real mount cost.
findings.fix: Choose the wrapper from the registered count before the first commit of the items (the registry knows N before the list renders), or keep the same element tree across the switch so React reconciles instead of remounting; prove it with a harness run whose `sends_after_mount` equals N, and a unit test on the switch that counts REGISTER sends. Decide the 100-item threshold's documentation in the same change.
findings.note: Browser bench numbers at efe658c: sends_after_mount 2000 at N=1000 and 20000 at N=10000 in all 16 runs; the list still remounts every item when it switches to its virtual wrapper. Stays 1.7.0.

findings.groupTitle: IdbFrecencyStorage ships inside the core entry, so the core size-limit row pays for an IndexedDB adapter most consumers never import
findings.claim: The core entry re-exports IdbFrecencyStorage (index.ts:4); size-limit measures dist/core/index.mjs whole (no `import` subset in the root package.json row), so the adapter and its lazy idb-keyval loader (1755 B gzip of the 6947 B core measured on 1.6/frecency 5c08ce9 by that cluster's manager; core without it is 5460 B) count against the core budget even though a real bundler drops them for a consumer who never imports the class. The roadmap's K5 sends budget overflow to subpaths, but a `modern-cmdk/frecency` subpath can only lower the measured core if the core entry stops re-exporting the class, which removes a public export and is therefore a 2.0 change (D79: the 1.x re-export stays).
findings.fix: In 2.0.0: add the `modern-cmdk/frecency` subpath (tsdown entry, exports map, size-limit row, publint/attw/check:package file lists, docs) exporting IdbFrecencyStorage, FrecencyEngine, MemoryFrecencyStorage and computeFrecencyBonus; remove the IdbFrecencyStorage re-export from the core entry with a codemod transform that rewrites the import specifier; restore the core row's budget to the pre-1.6.0 figure. Until then the 1.6.0 decision on the core limit (D90) stands.

findings.at: tests/dist/cli-exec.test.ts, tests/unit/codemod-files.test.ts, tests/unit/codemod-submodule.test.ts, tests/unit/codemod-cli.test.ts and tests/unit/check-repo-links.test.ts at 635a76e (every fixture git spawn inherits process.env)
findings.groupTitle: The git-spawning suites inherit a hook's GIT_DIR, so a pre-push from a linked worktree commits the fixtures onto the real branch
findings.claim: git 2.56.0 exports GIT_DIR to a hook run in a linked worktree (measured 2026-11-08: a pre-push hook sees GIT_DIR=<repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>; the main checkout exports none), and the lefthook pre-push runs pnpm test. Every fixture `git init`, `add`, `commit`, `init --bare`, `submodule add` and `worktree add` of the five git-spawning suites then operates on the pushing worktree's repository instead of the fixture directory. On 2026-11-08 the first push of docs/site-2026-11-onto-main from C:/w/cmdk-docs-m failed 60 tests in those five files (the outer lefthook hooks fired inside the fixtures, then 'Unable to create index.lock' and 'cannot lock ref HEAD'), put 23 fixture commits (init, base) on the branch being pushed, left an empty `modules` directory in the worktree's git directory, and a fixture's `git init --bare` wrote core.bare=true into the shared .git/config, after which the main checkout reported itself bare. findings.fix: tests/setup.ts, which every vitest project shares through extends: true, deletes GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_PREFIX, GIT_NAMESPACE and GIT_IMPLICIT_WORK_TREE before any test runs; tests/unit/setup-git-env.test.ts pins it. Red on release/1.6.0 without the scrub: codemod-cli with GIT_DIR pointing at a scratch repository fails 7 of 66 and leaves a 'fixture' commit there; green after with the scratch repository empty. The second docs push (2ae4479) runs the whole suite under the exported GIT_DIR and is the end-to-end proof.
